title: Jets announce Qwan’tez Stiggers has been released from the hospital
summary: When Jets cornerback Qwan’tez Stiggers was taken off the practice field on a stretcher Tuesday, it was a scary moment.
full_text: ' When Jets cornerback Qwan’tez Stiggers was taken off the practice field on a stretcher Tuesday, it was a scary moment. But it appears that Stiggers is going to be fine. The Jets have announced that Stiggers was released from the hospital and is home recovering. Stiggers ended up needing to be in the hospital for only a few hours after passing out on the sideline during practice. It's unclear what led him to pass out and there's been no word on when he might be back at practice. The 24-year-old Stiggers is heading into his third season with the Jets. He's an easy player to root for given his journey to the NFL after never playing college football. Stiggers went from high school football to the Fan Controlled Football league and then signed with the Toronto Argonauts of the Canadian Football League. In 2023 Stiggers was named the CFL’s Most Outstanding Rookie, and the Jets drafted him in 2024, making him the first player in 25 years to be drafted by the NFL after playing in the CFL. Last year Stiggers played in 15 games for the Jets. He started four games on defense and was a major contributor on special teams.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Sean Payton, Dan Campbell reflect on Teddy Bridgewater's 5-0 run with the 2019 Saints
summary: When Drew Brees got hurt, Bridgwater kept the Saints' season alive.
full_text: '' After practicing briefly with the Lions in training camp, quarterback Teddy Bridgewater decided that it's time to retire. Bridgewater had an NFL career that spanned more than a decade with eight different teams, but it was one five-week stretch that two of his coaches recalled most when asked about his retirement this week. In 2019, Bridgewater was the backup quarterback with the Saints, and when Drew Brees missed five games, Bridgewater stepped in and led the Saints to a 5-0 record. At the time of Brees' injury, the Saints were 1-1 and had just been blown out by the division rival Rams, and the season could have rapidly gone downhill. But Bridgewater made sure that didn't happen. Lions head coach Dan Campbell, who was assistant head coach on that Saints team, said one of the reasons he wanted Bridgewater as his backup quarterback in Detroit was that he knew how dependable Bridgewater could be in a pinch. "I'll never forget in 2019, when Drew got injured, we had just gone out to the Rams, got beat out there, Drew hurt his thumb and was out five weeks. Teddy stepped in and we won five in a row. That was Teddy," Campbell said. Broncos head coach Sean Payton, who was the Saints' head coach at the time. reflected on how much Bridgewater meant to that Saints team. "Our experience, my experience was fantastic," Payton said. "We made a trade for him . . . He was a great asset. A really, really good teammate. He had some rare leadership skills. . . . He was important, he was on our team during a ton of wins. When Drew got hurt he went 5-0, and I think he'll find his way back into coaching or some role with football. I'm proud of him, and the type of injury he had was significant, young in his career." A devastating knee injury during a preseason practice with the Vikings in 2016 changed the trajectory of Bridgewater's career, and he never became the franchise quarterback he was expected to be in Minnesota, or anywhere else. But no one doubted his hard work, leadership and character, and he had all the traits that coaches love in a backup quarterback. Those coaches are expressing their appreciation for Bridgewater as he walks away from the NFL.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Puka Nacua reportedly dealing with only minor soreness in his groin
summary: Nacua, the star receiver heading into the final year of his rookie contract, appears to have avoided a significant injury.
full_text: ' Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left practice early on Tuesday, but his injury is not a significant concern. Nacual is just dealing with minor soreness in his groin, according to Ian Rapoport. The Rams' training staff took Nacua off the field out of an abundance of caution, but from all accounts he's going to be OK. Through three seasons, Nacua is averaging 95.3 receiving yards per game, which is the highest per-game average of any receiver in NFL history. He has decided to keep practicing even though he's heading into the final year of his rookie contract, at a time when many NFL stars entering their fourth seasons choose not to practice until their teams give them a new deal. Even a minor injury scare could be a major concern for Nacua until he has a long-term contract.
author: Michael David Smith

title: CBS continues to talk to NFL about a new broadcast deal
summary: The question of whether Tony Romo will continue to call NFL games for CBS has somewhat obscured the question of whether CBS will continue to broadcast NFL games.
full_text: The question of whether Tony Romo will continue to call NFL games for CBS has somewhat obscured the question of whether CBS will continue to broadcast NFL games. Like Fox, NBC, Prime Video, and YouTube, the CBS contract runs through 2029, once (as expected) the NFL exercises its prerogative to end the contracts four years early. Unlike the other networks, CBS has undergone a "change in control," which allows the NFL to reopen the current deal. The NFL already has embarked on active negotiations with CBS, with some reports suggesting the league may seek to bump the CBS annual fee from $2.1 billion to $3 billion — effective immediately. More recent reports have pointed to a stall in the negotiations, fueled by legal issues arising from its parent company's effort to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. At Tuesday's season-preview press event, CBS Sports president David Berson addressed the situation. "We’re in constant conversation; we have so much business with them on so many other levels,” Berson told Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing . “There’s nothing to report on this right now , but the relationship is outstanding. We’re talking to them every day. I mentioned the viewership success we’ve had, I mentioned they covet reach so much; CBS is the number one network 17 of the last 18 years . . . so they really value what we provide and we also value what they’re providing. So conversations continue, but there’s nothing at this stage to talk about.” The NFL could, in theory, pull the plug on CBS and take its games back to the market. But who would assume the CBS Sunday-afternoon slate? The other networks have their existing windows. None of them presumably would want to add half of the full Sunday afternoon slate of games. And it would be important to keep the Sunday afternoon slate on broadcast TV. A pivot of a large swath of the most traditional "free" games to streaming would create more political pushback for the NFL. Of the broadcast networks, Fox already has its Sunday afternoon games. That leaves NBC and ABC, both of which have prime-time packages. If, alternatively, CBS does a new deal at a significant bump, what happens with the other networks? CBS probably wouldn't relish the opportunity to pay significantly more while the other partners are still paying the amounts due under the existing deals. The entire situation is delicate and tricky and likely at this point to lead to no new deals before the start of the 2026 regular season. Which is what the NFL seemed to want. And so the can will apparently be kicked into 2027. Which, coincidentally, may give the Commissioner even more leverage in ongoing talks to extend his contract, which expires in March.
author: Mike Florio

title: As contract year approaches, Baker Mayfield "feels great"
summary: With no new contract coming, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield needs to be ready to get the most out of the bet he'd making on himself.
full_text: ' With no new contract coming, Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield needs to be ready to get the most out of the bet he'd making on himself. And he feels like he's ready to do that physically. “I think I’m in the best shape I’ve ever been in ,” Mayfield said on the 4th and South podcast, via JoeBucsFan.com. “It took a while to feel healthy enough to actually train and get to that point. But I feel great. You know, you find your routine in the later years of your career and you figure out what works for you schedule-wise, workout-wise, diet-wise — all things you need to adjust and adapt to as the years go on. I feel really good. Yeah, last year I was banged up but, I mean, the whole team was.” He'll need to find a way to avoid being banged up. Part of his appeal is that he'll play through anything. At some point, however, it impacts his performance. That's where it could get interesting, if he has multiple injuries through which he's playing in 2026. At some point, Mayfield at less than 100 percent may not be a better option than Jake Browning at full strength. And the coaching staff (and/or the front office) may be inclined to ask him to take a seat, if they think it's in the best interests of the team. Given the contractual posture, that becomes a potentially dicey move. Mayfield is trying to earn his next contract. He may not take kindly to any talk of being removed temporarily. It all comes down to Mayfield avoiding unnecessary hits that he has a habit of at times embracing. It's one thing to be healthy when there's no contact. Starting in Week 1, it will be open season on all NFL quarterbacks. Mayfield's short-term interests, and his long-term prospects, may hinge on staying as healthy as he can, for as long as he can.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Alleged scam artist was "desperately" seeking $75,000 loan on the day he died
summary: The case of Mohamed Coulibaly is sending shock waves throughout the NFL, as it relates to many people in the league (including coaches, executives, and players) who actually invested with him, who supposedly did (but actually didn't), and/or who had been solicited to invest.
full_text: ' The case of Mohamed Coulibaly is sending shock waves throughout the NFL, as it relates to many people in the league (including coaches, executives, and players) who actually invested with him, who supposedly did (but actually didn't), and/or who had been solicited to invest. In a Tuesday item published by the Philadelphia Inquirer , Ximena Conde reports that Coulibaly was “desperately” seeking a $75,000 loan on the day he was found dead in a swimming pool at his home. Per the report, Coulibaly sought money from a New York man to whom Coulibaly already owed $1 million. He promised a Lamborghini, two gold Rolexes, and a signed Lionel Messi cleat as collateral for a weeklong loan. He told the man that the extra money would make it possible to repay the original $1 million. Later that day, a driver arrived at the man's house with two fake watches, an unauthenticated signed cleat, and an insurance card and bill of sale for the car. The man then backed out of the loan. One of Coulibaly's alleged victims told the Inquirer that Coulibaly called on the day he died, adding that he "started to cry hysterical on the phone,” saying, "'I’ve lost it all, please help me here, please help me here.'" Coulibaly's death is being investigated by local authorities. Some in league circles who were familiar with Coulibaly's activities suspect that he may have been killed. Coulibaly's alleged scam focused on Shopify stores that apparently were fraudulent. The situation has been characterized by some as a Ponzi scheme. The situation eventually involved former Cardinals G.M. Steve Keim, who told Conde that he met Coulibaly through mutual acquaintances with the Eagles. “I introduced him to people to sell stores to and that sort of thing,” Keim told the Inquirer regarding Coulibaly. “He called me the COO but he also made promises to give me health insurance and to have some kind of bonus structure.” Keim characterized himself as one of Coulibaly's victims. “This went downhill fast,” Keim told Conde. “Not only did I get my name drug through the mud, I lost a lot of money since I was an investor.” It remains to be seen whether law enforcement determines that Coulibaly, who has been described as being 24 years old by Barron's and 23 years old by the Inquirer , died of suicide, natural causes, an accidental drowning, or foul play. Regardless, the story seems to have plenty of tentacles. And there seems to be much more of a story to tell.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyler Murray knows his running ability will make a difference when it's time to play games
summary: Murray says he has a "special" skill to move the ball with his legs.
full_text: On Tuesday, the Vikings named quarterback Kyler Murray the starting quarterback for 2026. After the decision was announced, Murray spoke to reporters. One thing that stands out may be the one thing that made a difference when making him the starter — his ability to make plays with his legs. "I think, you know, as far as my ability to move around, stuff like that, it's tough to emulate that stuff on the practice field, when bullets aren't really flying and there's no referees out here to be able to say if we were sacked or not," Murray said. "But I think when we get out there, you know, come game time, I think that stuff just happens for me. That stuff just happens, you know, trying to premeditate what I'm gonna do or anything like that. But I definitely think that's an ability of mine that, you know, is a special one." Quarterbacks coach Josh McCown previously addressed that dynamic . The Vikings have been trying to get him up to speed as to running the new offense. His instinctive and uncanny ability to run the ball will make everything in the passing game easier. Defenses will have to account for that. And it could make them hesitant in coverage, which could help receivers get open. Regardless, the Vikings have made their decision. Coach Kevin O'Connell said during the offseason that, once they name a starter, they plan to stick with him all year. In the two years the Vikings have gone to the playoffs under O'Connell, they had the same quarterback all year. In the two years they didn't, they had a revolving door. And so it's Murray moving forward. He'll be able to keep learning the offense. And he'll be in a position to pull the ball down and Road Runner away from the 11 Wile E. Coyotes who won't be able to catch him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steve Keim strongly denies DeAndre Hopkins's claim regarding positive PED test
summary: Former Cardinals receiver DeAndre Hopkins recently tweeted, then deleted, a claim that he was "set up" regarding a failed PED test.
full_text: ''' Former Cardinals receiver DeAndre Hopkins recently tweeted, then deleted, a claim that he was " set up " regarding a failed PED test. Hopkins seemed to suggest that former Cardinals G.M. Steve Keim had a role in it. On Tuesday, Keim strongly denied the accusation. "DeAndre Hopkins recently published and then deleted a statement falsely suggesting that I was responsible for contaminating or manipulating the drug test associated with his 2022 NFL suspension," Keim said in a statement provided to PFT. "That accusation is completely false. "I did not contaminate, alter, manipulate, interfere with, or cause anyone else to interfere with DeAndre's drug test or its results. I did not 'set him up' for a suspension, and I had no involvement in causing the test result that led to his suspension. "Accusing someone of deliberately interfering with an NFL drug test is an extraordinarily serious allegation. It attacks my integrity, my professional reputation, and the work I spent decades building in the National Football League. The fact that the statement was later deleted does not undo the damage caused by publishing it to a large public audience. "I have retained counsel, Raees Mohamed, Esq., to aggressively address this matter and to protect my reputation and legal rights. The relevant evidence is being reviewed and preserved, and this matter will be handled through the appropriate channels. "I have no intention of engaging in a public back-and-forth or litigating this issue on social media. But I also will not remain silent when I am falsely accused of conduct that I did not commit. "DeAndre's accusation concerning my involvement in his drug test is false. I unequivocally deny it." It appears that civil litigation is on the table regarding the claims made by Hopkins, whose allegation was made after Keim’s name surfaced in connection with Mohamed Coulibaly, an alleged scam artist who recently was found dead in the swimming pool at his home. Keim has not yet addressed the connection to Coulibaly or his company, Motion Ventures.
author: Mike Florio

title: CEO Greg Penner say Broncos have yet to consider whether new stadium will have PSLs
summary: The Denver Broncos hope to build a new stadium by 2031.
full_text: The Denver Broncos hope to build a new stadium by 2031. The project will entail many decisions. One fairly important decision, from the perspective of the folks who attend the games, has yet to be considered. PSLs. Personal Seat Licenses. The money-for-nothing charge that attaches to the ability to buy season tickets. During a Tuesday press conference with reporters, owner and CEO Greg Penner addressed the PSL issue. “Really, it’s the furthest thing from our minds right now," Penner said. "We’re so focused on — we’ve had so many steps before that. . . . [Burnam Yards is] still a preferred site but it’s not finalized that we’re going to be in that location. Obviously, that’s where we really want to be. "So really, we haven’t even gotten to PSLs yet. Our season ticket holders are vital to our organization and we’re going to keep them informed every step of the way once we get there." Plenty of teams use PSLs, which can become very expensive based on the quality of the seats. And, frankly, it's more fair to fund the construction of a new stadium through the PSL process than to impose on taxpayers generally, since most of them will never attend a game and many of them don't care about football. That may sound sacrilegious to hard-core football fans, but it's true.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay: "No new news" on Aaron Donald
summary: Everyone is waiting for Aaron Donald to decide whether he'll end a two-year retirement and return to football.
full_text: ' Everyone is waiting for Aaron Donald to decide whether he'll end a two-year retirement and return to football. Everyone, including coach Sean McVay. "He's going through his process," McVay told reporters on Tuesday. "I'm hopeful. I don't even want to put a timeline on it because what I don't want to [do is] rush this. "There are conversations we've had. Hopefully [something happens] sooner than later, but there's no new news. He is continuing to go through his process." A decision had been expected early this week. That was nudged back to the end of the week. It could still be bumped deeper into August. The Rams will need a few weeks to get Donald ready to go. They plan to utilize the same approach that was employed in 2017 and 2018, when he held out over his contract. The goal continues to be Week 1, with an expected range of 30 to 40 snaps. Before that can be activated, Donald has to make a decision as to whether he'll return.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan downplays concern over Christian McCaffrey's practice absence
summary: 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey missed practice again Tuesday.
full_text: ' 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey missed practice again Tuesday. Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak attributed McCaffrey's absence on Monday to tightness, with nothing more specific. The concern is McCaffrey had calf tightness during the 2024 training camp that carried into the season. He played only four games with what was later announced as Achilles tendinitis and a separate injury to his posterior collateral ligament. Coach Kyle Shanahan, though, said he is not concerned by McCaffrey's current setback. "No," Shanahan said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "My concern would be him toughing through tightness, like a lot of people do, and then hurting something bad, and then pulling something , which then, it could be a month. That would be our concern, so once we hear him talking a certain way, Christian's a guy who needs to get prepared for Week 1. But also, we're pretty confident in what he's done before. We're confident in what he's done these two weeks, and we just want to make sure we don't make it something to be concerned about." McCaffrey, 30, led the league with 413 touches last year. He finished the season with 311 carries for 1,202 yards with 10 touchdowns and caught 102 passes for 924 yards with seven touchdowns. He had 37 more touches in two postseason games, rushing 26 times for 83 yards, along with 11 catches for 105 yards with two scores.
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons claim OG Jaeden Roberts off waivers
summary: The Falcons claimed offensive guard Jaeden Roberts off waivers, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Falcons claimed offensive guard Jaeden Roberts off waivers, the team announced Tuesday. The Eagles waived Roberts on Monday. Roberts spent four seasons at the University of Alabama but went undrafted in the 2026 draft. He signed with the Eagles as a college free agent in May. Roberts started 37 career games in four collegiate seasons, including 2023 when current Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees was his offensive coordinator at Alabama. In the past week, the Falcons have cut inside linebacker Troy Andersen, signed defensive end Cameron Sample and running back Trey Sermon, activated right tackle Jawaan Taylor off the active/PUP list, signed tight end Nick Muse and waived wide receiver Le'Meke Brockington and linebacker Malik Verdon with injury designations.
author: Charean Williams

title: CBS is "still assessing" the "evolving" Tony Romo situation
summary: Comments from CBS Sports president David Berson hint at a full-season absence, at a minimum, for Romo.
full_text: ' All eyes and ears were on Tuesday's CBS NFL season preview press conference, given the current status of the network's top analyst, Tony Romo. At the outset of the session, CBS Sports president David Berson addressed the pink elephant in the room. “I know there’s one topic that’s been in the news a lot lately," Berson said, via Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing . "I know it’s on people’s minds here, so I’m gonna hit that right out of the gate, and that has to do with Tony Romo being on leave until further notice. I hope you can respect and appreciate that this is a personnel matter and a legal one for Tony, so I can’t speak to that aspect of things. What I can say is it’s an evolving situation, and therefore we’re still assessing . “There’s no timetable or final decision at this time. Since it continues to evolve and we’re on the eve of the season, I felt it’s very important that our team, the many, many hundreds of people who work on the NFL on CBS, have certainty and direction so we can definitively plan and focus on the production and marketing as we kick off the season. In making this decision, we had to consider the impact on our image and on our brand. That’s very important to us. Whether the games, marketing, P.R., social, the focus should be and needs to be on our presentation and this great product and not on any other factors. “Fortunately, we have a very deep bench, and I’m really proud of the way everyone’s stepping up and responding. As you know, J.J. [Watt] will join Jim [Nantz] and Tracy [Wolfson] as our lead team in Tony’s absence. They’re already knee-deep in planning, and I have every confidence they’ll be great." The full context of Berson's comments hints that it will be a full-season assignment for Watt. Which, if so, means it will be a full-season absence for Romo. Indeed, nothing Berson said changes the perception that Romo's days at CBS are numbered, and that he possibly if not probably if not likely won't be back on the air with his current employer.
author: Mike Florio

title: Free agent CB Terrion Arnold to visit Giants next
summary: Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold has made the rounds since the Lions cut him on June 29.
full_text: ' Free agent cornerback Terrion Arnold has made the rounds since the Lions cut him on June 29. The Giants are the latest team to conduct due diligence, welcoming Arnold to their team facility on Wednesday, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. Arnold was in Seattle on Sunday and New Orleans on Tuesday after previously visiting the Texans. The Colts and Jets also have shown interest. Arnold is scheduled for his arraignment hearing later this week. The third-year player faces four felony counts each of armed robbery and kidnapping after his June 24 arrest in Florida. A conviction could bring a life sentence. The Lions drafted Arnold in the first round in 2024, and he played 24 games with 22 starts in two seasons. He has totaled 91 tackles, an interception and 18 pass breakups.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Dobbs on leaving New England: “That was very frustrating, the way they handled that"
summary: New Lions backup quarterback Joshua Dobbs says he's happy to be in Detroit — but not happy with his former team, the Patriots.
full_text: New Lions backup quarterback Joshua Dobbs says he's happy to be in Detroit — but not happy with his former team, the Patriots. The Patriots were ready to move on from Dobbs this offseason, but they were holding out hope that they could get something for him in a trade. When they didn't, they cut him — two weeks after the start of free agency, when some of the teams that might have been interested in signing him had already signed other backup quarterbacks. Asked today in Detroit what the offseason has been like for him, Dobbs said it was different than other offseasons because the Patriots didn't give him the opportunity to be with another team from Day One. "It was a weird offseason because it was my first time not having OTAs and everything, and that was just by the nature of my situation in New England, with the timing. That was very frustrating, the way they handled that," Dobbs said. Dobbs emphasized that he's been working all offseason to be ready when he finally found the right team. The well-traveled Dobbs is experienced at joining new teams: He started his career with the Steelers and then went to the Jaguars, then the Steelers again, then the Browns, then the Lions, then the Titans, then the Browns again, then the Cardinals, then the Vikings, then the 49ers and then the Patriots. He knows what it is to get cut, but he doesn't like how the Patriots did it.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Browns claim TE Dae'Quan Wright off waivers, put DB Damarri Mathis on IR
summary: The Browns made a pair of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
full_text: ' The Browns made a pair of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that they claimed tight end Dae'Quan Wright off of waivers from the Eagles. They put defensive back Damarri Mathis on injured reserve in a corresponding move. Wright signed with the Eagles after going undrafted out of Ole Miss. He had 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns during his final college season. Mathis was carted off with an injury at Browns practice on Tuesday. He tore his ACL at a Panthers practice ahead of last season, so it may be back-to-back lost years for Mathis.
author: Josh Alper

title: Matthew Stafford doesn't think Puka Nacua's injury was "anything too major"
summary: Matthew Stafford is neither a trainer nor a doctor.
full_text: ' Matthew Stafford is neither a trainer nor a doctor. But as a quarterback entering his 18th pro season, he has an idea of what a serious injury looks like. Head coach Sean McVay did not have a real update on why Puka Nacua left Tuesday’s joint practice with the Cowboys, and Stafford didn't know much about it either. But he also did not get any indication that Nacua's injury was significant. "I did not [see what happened]," Stafford said, via Lindsey Thiry of ESPN. "I'm not really sure what the issue was, but nobody ran up to me in a panic, so I don’t think it was anything too major ." That's not confirmation that nothing serious happened to Nacua. But it is a positive signal when there isn't any other concrete information. Nacua caught 129 passes for 1,7115 yards with 10 touchdowns last season. The Rams’ first preseason game is set for Saturday afternoon against the Chiefs. Given McVay’s history, starters are highly unlikely to play for Los Angeles.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jets CB Qwan'tez Stiggers transported to the hospital after passing out at practice
summary: Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was transported in an ambulance to a local hospital after losing consciousness during a joint practice with the Buccaneers.
full_text: ' Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was transported in an ambulance to a local hospital after losing consciousness during a joint practice with the Buccaneers. Jets coach Aaron Glenn said after practice that Stiggers was conscious and talking on the field. Stiggers also received an IV before being taken by stretcher to the waiting ambulance. The Jets have not updated Stiggers' condition. Glenn said Stiggers "came to the sideline, and he just passed out." "For the most part, he was good ," Glenn said, via Rich Cimini of ESPN. The incident stopped the joint practice for 10 minutes. Stiggers, 24, entered the NFL as a fifth-round pick of the Jets in 2024 after not playing college football. He played one season for the Toronto Argonauts of the CFL. Stiggers has appeared in 29 games for the Jets, seeing action on 503 special teams snaps and 297 on defense.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears sign OL Wesley French
summary: The Bears added some depth to their offensive line on Tuesday.
full_text: ' The Bears added some depth to their offensive line on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed Wesley French to their 90-man roster. They waived safety Brandon Hill in a corresponding move. French signed with the Colts as an undrafted rookie in 2022 and played in every game for Indianapolis during the 2023 season. He spent 2024 on injured reserve and was on practice squads in Dallas and Cleveland last year. Hill signed with the Bears a few days ago. His departure comes on the same day that the Bears announced Coby Bryant will miss four to six months after knee surgery, so they may have another move in mind to bolster their safety options.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings name Kyler Murray their starting quarterback
summary: Murray has won Minnesota's QB competition over 2024 No. 10 overall pick J.J. McCarthy.
full_text: The Vikings' quarterback competition is over. Minnesota has named Kyler Murray its starting quarterback, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Murray, the No. 1 pick of the 2019 draft, signed a one-year deal with Minnesota in the offseason with the thought of earning the starting role over J.J. McCarthy. That has now happened before the first preseason game, setting up Murray to take all of the starters’ reps over the next month in preparation for the regular season. Murray started five games for Arizona last year, completing 68.3 percent of his passes for 962 yards with six touchdowns and three interceptions. In 2024, he started all 17 games, recording 3,851 passing yards with 21 touchdowns and 11 interceptions with a 68.8 percent completion rate. Notably, Murray has a no-tag clause in his contract, which means he is set to become a free agent next March. McCarthy, the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 draft, will now go into his third season as a backup after dealing with injuries and poor performance in his first two years. He started 10 games for Minnesota last year, completing 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He also took 27 sacks, which worked out to a high 10.0 percent sack rate. His passer rating was just 72.6. Minnesota’s first preseason game is set for Saturday at 1 p.m. ET against the Giants.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Commanders sign LB Curtis Jacobs
summary: The Commanders announced the signing of defensive tackle Byron Cowart on Tuesday morning and they added another player to the defense in the afternoon.
full_text: The Commanders announced the signing of defensive tackle Byron Cowart on Tuesday morning and they added another player to the defense in the afternoon. Linebacker Curtis Jacobs is the newest addition to the 90-man roster in Washington. The Commanders cut two players when they signed Cowart, so they did not need to make any more corresponding moves. Jacobs appeared in three games for the Titans last season and played 39 special teams snaps. He had four tackles in nine games for the Patriots in 2024. Jacobs's most recent playing time came with the UFL's DC Defenders. He had 42 tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a fumble recovery in 10 games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Klint Kubiak: Fernando Mendoza will get "plenty of experience" on Thursday vs. Cardinals
summary: No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is officially set to make his preseason debut on Thursday night.
full_text: No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is officially set to make his preseason debut on Thursday night. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters in his Tuesday press conference that Las Vegas' starters will play in this week's matchup against the Cardinals, which means Kirk Cousins is set to be the first QB on the field. But Mendoza, Kubiak said, will get "plenty of experience in the game." "Look forward to seeing him out there with his teammates," Kubiak said. "A lot of guys we need to evaluate — he’ll get plenty of reps ." Kubiak did not disclose his exact plans for playing time this week, but there is a chance Mendoza will take some snaps with the first-team offensive line. Generally, Kubiak said he's seen Mendoza continue to grow throughout training camp. "It’s been a really impressive training camp as far as how he’s prepared," Kubiak said. "And then he goes out there to practice and things don’t happen on the drawing, on the paper in the playbook exactly as they do on the field. So, I think he’s done a good job of adjusting. And with all of our players, we just ask that as they gain experience as they make mistakes, they don’t make the same mistake twice. I think he’s done a good job of that and now it comes to live bullets, with a live pass rush and that will be a whole ‘nother animal." Kickoff between the Raiders and Cardinals is slated for 8:00 p.m. ET on Thursday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: ESPN's Matt Miller faces misdemeanor charge from June car crash
summary: At a time when the Missouri Attorney General is investigating allegations against ESPN NFL draft analyst Matt Miller for fantasy-football leagues that allegedly didn't pay out winnings to contestants, another legal issue has emerged.
full_text: ' At a time when the Missouri Attorney General is investigating allegations against ESPN NFL draft analyst Matt Miller for fantasy-football leagues that allegedly didn't pay out winnings to contestants, another legal issue has emerged. Via Brendon Kleen of Awful Announcing , Miller has been charged with failing to drive on the right half of a roadway , resulting in an accident. The charge is a misdemeanor. Miller is due in court on September 21. The June 2026 collision resulted in serious injuries for Miller, including the amputation of an arm. In the aftermath of the accident, online complaints emerged regarding his fantasy-football leagues. Miller is on leave from ESPN while he recovers. ESPN reportedly will address the legal issues at the appropriate time .
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers won't play many starters on Thursday night
summary: The Titans plan to play their starters in Thursday's preseason opener against the 49ers, but they won't have many first-stringers lined up against them. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said at a press conference on Tuesday that the team will be sitting most of its starters.
full_text: The Titans plan to play their starters in Thursday's preseason opener against the 49ers, but they won't have many first-stringers lined up against them. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said at a press conference on Tuesday that the team will be sitting most of its starters. "There won't be many starters playing ," Shanahan said. "We'll see, with injuries today and stuff — and that doesn't mean none. But we've got to balance that out. We haven't told the players yet, so we'll wait until we do that with them this afternoon." Shanahan's decision was likely impacted by Tuesday's joint practice between the teams, but the 49ers have several players that would likely be sitting due to injury even if they went with a different plan. Wide receiver Mike Evans suited up for practice on Tuesday for the first time in over a week while running back Christian McCaffrey and defensive end Nick Bosa headlined the list of players who remained out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Bosa has soreness, tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee
summary: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has missed five consecutive practices.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has missed five consecutive practices. Coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that Bosa was experiencing soreness as he returns from a torn ACL in his right knee. On Tuesday, Shanahan added tendinitis to the explanation for Bosa's recent absence. "Just soreness, tendinitis," Shanahan said, via video from his news conference. "It's a pretty normal thing with ACLs. Talking to our guys, they say it happens with about 90 percent of the [time]. So, it's a normal thing. We've got to be smart here week to week, but no concerns about it being any more than that." Bosa injured his knee in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26. Bosa, 28, has not had a double-digit sack season since 2023, which is the last time he played all 17 games. He has played only 17 games over the past two seasons, totaling 11 sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chargers OT Rashawn Slater dealing with flare-up in his knee
summary: Chargers left tackle Rashawn Slater missed his fourth straight practice on Tuesday and the reason for it involves his surgically repaired left knee.
full_text: Chargers left tackle Rashawn Slater missed his fourth straight practice on Tuesday and the reason for it involves his surgically repaired left knee. Slater tore his patellar tendon in practice a little over a year ago and he told reporters on Tuesday that he has been out since last week because of a flare-up in the same knee. Trey Pipkins and Branson Taylor have seen increased reps at left tackle with Slater out of practice. Slater said he doesn't know when he'll be back on the field and called the absence part of the process of getting where he needs to be for the start of the regular season “Nothing crazy,” Slater said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. “Nothing that’s concerning .” The longer it takes before Slater's back on the field, the likelier it is that others will start to have some concern about his availability in September.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Vrabel dances around question regarding lessons learned from offseason counseling
summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel hasn't faced many questions during training camp about the aftermath of the offseason controversy involving himself and former ESPN/The Athletic reporter Dianna Russini.
full_text: ' Patriots coach Mike Vrabel hasn't faced many questions during training camp about the aftermath of the offseason controversy involving himself and former ESPN/ The Athletic reporter Dianna Russini. While there haven't been many/any developments that would lend themselves to more questions, the situation still hovers — and it could move back to the front burner based on future events. Or if the Patriots struggle out of the gates . On Tuesday, Vrabel got a question about the one tangible impact of the situation on his job: The counseling session that caused him to miss the third day of the 2026 NFL Draft. Here's the specific inquiry, from the transcript distributed by the Patriots: "You said this offseason that you were seeking counseling. I wanted to follow up on that and see what you learned from that counseling, and how did you balance that personal commitment with getting ready for this season?" Vrabel's answer avoided the specific reason for the counseling, while pivoting to a more broad-brush reply. "I think we always look at improvement," Vrabel said. "As we talk about getting ready for the next season, we always look at improvement and ways that we can improve individually and how we can improve as a team. It’s really critical that we continue to do that on and off the field. I believe in that. I believe in everything that we can do to help this football team, to help our coaches, to help myself and everybody else included. This journey that we are going to go on is going to be completely different than the one we went on last year. That’s all of our jobs, is to prepare for it now. So, really focused on our improvement individually and as a team, and that’s something that we can do today. You look at the O-line, and we talk about them and their ability to play together as a unit. There are so many combination blocks that they are involved in, and we have to be better. Again, five O-linemen have to be able to sustain a line of scrimmage, and I just walked into that meeting room and said, 'How do we improve? How do we improve our combination blocks?' We are not asking you to block everybody 1-on-1. So, I think we all have areas that we can improve on, and that includes the coaches." In other words, Vrabel isn't inclined to get into something that happened several months ago. He has moved on, the team has moved on, and barring The Athletic publishing its internal investigation of Russini (if it ever does) or Russini telling her story publicly, everyone else will move on, too. That's how most controversies fade into the background. If there's nothing new to address, there's eventually nothing more to discuss.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears S Coby Bryant had knee surgery, will miss 4-6 months
summary: The timeline for Bears safety Coby Bryant's return to action has gotten a lot longer.
full_text: The timeline for Bears safety Coby Bryant's return to action has gotten a lot longer. Head coach Ben Johnson said on Tuesday that Bryant had knee surgery late last week. Bryant is set to miss four to six months, which is far longer than the original timeline of two to three months that accompanied initial news of his injury. If the recovery moves at the short end of that spectrum, Bryant could be back for the end of the regular season and any playoff games that the Bears might play. It's not anything that the Bears are going to be able to count on, however, and that's a big blow to the defense after the Bears moved quickly to sign Bryant off his Super Bowl win with the Seahawks. The Bears listed the recently signed Xavier Woods behind Bryant on their initial depth chart. Dillon Thieneman was listed as a starter with Bryant and Josh Blackwell, Brandon Hill, Anthony Johnson, and Marlen Sewell are also in reserve roles.
author: Josh Alper

title: Myles Garrett has swelling in his knee but is at "85 percent"
summary: Myles Garrett missed his second consecutive practice, standing and watching the Rams' joint practice with the Cowboys on Tuesday.
full_text: ' Myles Garrett missed his second consecutive practice, standing and watching the Rams' joint practice with the Cowboys on Tuesday. Coach Sean McVay revealed after the practice that the pass rusher is dealing with swelling in his knee. McVay said Garrett is at "85 percent" with no setbacks in his rehab, but the Rams chose to err on the side of caution by holding him out. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year missed four practices last week with what McVay called "lower-body soreness." Garrett played all 17 games each of the past two seasons and has missed only four games over the past six seasons. The Rams acquired Garrett in a blockbuster offseason trade with the Browns, set the NFL's single-season sacks record with 23 last season. He has 125.5 sacks in his nine NFL seasons.
author: Charean Williams

title: CBS moves Ross Tucker to No. 2 booth with Ian Eagle
summary: With J.J.
full_text: ' With J.J. Watt moving from the No. 2 booth at CBS to the top spot vacated (for now, possibly for good) by Tony Romo, CBS had to replace Watt's spot. On Tuesday, CBS announced that former NFL lineman Ross Tucker will take the spot alongside Ian Eagle. Tucker, who played pro football for the better part of a decade, has been calling college and pro games for CBS since 2018. It's a significant leap for Tucker, who had been on the No. 6 broadcast team at CBS before the current bump. And if Watt ends up remaining in the No. 1 spot through 2026 and beyond, Tucker has an opportunity to stick in the second spot at CBS.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets CB Qwan'tez Stiggers released from hospital after collapsing in practice
summary: Stiggers left Tuesday's joint practice with the Buccaneers in an ambulance
full_text:
New York Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers is out of the hospital and recovering at home following an incident at Tuesday's practice, the team announced. Stiggers collapsed on the sideline during the joint training camp session with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and was taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital, coach Aaron Glenn said. The Jets have not announced a diagnosis.
Stiggers, who started four games for the Jets in 2025, received an IV on the practice field before he was stretchered into the ambulance, according to ESPN . The teams halted practice for 10 minutes while New York's medical staff attended to Stiggers.
"Our guys did a hell of a job -- just like most medical staffs around this league do in situations like that -- and they took the necessary steps just to make sure that we do everything we can to be on board when it comes to those situations," Glenn said after practice . "He was able to talk. I want to make sure that I go and see him after this just to make sure I'm good with everything, but for the most part, he was good."
The frightening scene unfolded ahead of Stiggers' third year in the NFL . He appeared in 29 games over his first two seasons and started four games for the Jets last year. He serves as both a backup cornerback and a special teams stalwart and set career highs in every statistical category in 2025 with 27 tackles, one tackle for loss, three pass breakups and two fumble recoveries.
Stiggers arrived in New York by way of the CFL. When the Jets selected him in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft , he became the first player to be drafted directly from the CFL since 1999. Prior to his lone season in Canada -- during which he was recognized as the CFL's Most Outstanding Rookie -- Stiggers spent one year in the Fan Controlled Football league. He did not play college football .
author: Carter Bahns

title: Can J.J. McCarthy and Anthony Richardson be saved? History offers a reason for hope -- and plenty for concern
summary: The NFL gives failed first-round QBs second chances; it rarely gives them second careers
full_text:
There comes a point with every struggling young quarterback when patience starts to look a lot like stubbornness.
For J.J. McCarthy , the Vikings have finally reached that point. A season ago, Minnesota was still trying to figure out exactly what it had in the former No. 10 overall pick , and even after a rough start to the 2025 campaign there were enough flashes to make the conversation more about development than the search for the next franchise QB. Now McCarthy is heading into Year 3 with just 10 NFL starts, and the Vikings have named Kyler Murray their starter .
Meanwhile, Anthony Richardson has reached an even more precarious point in the conversation in Indianapolis. Three years after the Colts selected him fourth overall, Daniel Jones is entrenched as the starter, and Richardson has spent this summer battling Riley Leonard for the backup job. Richardson is still only 24 years old and remains one of the most physically gifted quarterbacks in football, but the organization that drafted him is no longer willing to wait for those gifts to turn into consistent quarterback play.
Which raises a much more interesting question than whether McCarthy or Richardson can still be "fixed": What does history say happens after an NFL team decides a first-round quarterback's talent is no longer worth waiting on?
The answer, after going through more than a decade of quarterback data, is not encouraging. The NFL frequently gives former first-round QBs another opportunity; it almost never gives them another franchise. And while McCarthy and Richardson have arrived at essentially the same career crossroads, the data suggests the problems they need to solve from here are very different.
To get some idea of what McCarthy and Richardson are up against, I went back through recent first-round quarterbacks and looked for players whose original teams had effectively stopped treating them like the franchise saviors by the end of their third NFL season. This wasn't about missing games because of injury or getting benched for a week. The organizational decision had to be obvious: replace him, trade him, release him or otherwise enter the following season with somebody else as the intended starter.
Seven recent quarterbacks fit the mold: Josh Rosen , Dwayne Haskins, Sam Darnold , Zach Wilson , Mac Jones , Justin Fields and Kenny Pickett . Trey Lance and Paxton Lynch are useful supporting examples, but neither established themselves as their team's starter long enough to really answer the same question.
So what happened next for those seven QBs is a good reminder that effectively being declared a bust by the team that drafted you in the first round (and often in the first 10 picks) doesn't necessarily mean your NFL career is over.
Made 10+ additional starts
Later had a top 16 EPA/dropback season
Clearly reestablished as a franchise QB
Five QBs eventually started another game. Darnold, Jones and Fields each accumulated at least 10 more starts, and Fields got two different organizations to give him meaningful opportunities after Chicago decided to move on.
NFL teams don't suddenly forget why these guys were first-round picks; the arm talent, athleticism or college production -- many of the reasons the player was a high selection to begin with -- coupled with the belief that you are the GM or coach to fix this mess often lead to second, third and sometimes fourth chances when common sense and the eye test might dictate otherwise. Actually becoming a franchise quarterback again is another matter.
Only Darnold and Mac Jones subsequently produced a top 16 season in EPA per dropback with at least 200 dropbacks, and Jones' case requires some context. He was legitimately good filling in for Brock Purdy in San Francisco in 2025, posting a +0.07 EPA per dropback -- 12th among qualifying quarterbacks -- along with a 76.0 PFF passing grade. That's a real statistical rebound, but it hasn't yet turned him back into somebody's unquestioned QB1.
That leaves Darnold as the one clear success story, and even his career arc shouldn't put McCarthy and Richardson at ease about their NFL futures. Darnold didn't leave the Jets and immediately turn into the quarterback we saw in Minnesota. He posted a -0.16 EPA per dropback with Carolina in 2021, made six starts the following year and then spent 2023 backing up Purdy in San Francisco.
His breakthrough finally came in 2024, four seasons after his final year with the Jets. Darnold finished 14th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback, earned an 80.3 PFF passing grade and subsequently turned that season into another starting opportunity in Seattle -- and at $105 million over three years, it now looks like one of the best bargains in the league. Darnold's career shows that a former first-round QB can rewrite his story, but his path looks much more like an exception than a blueprint -- and it took years to get there.
That's the first lesson for McCarthy and Richardson. The NFL gives failed first-round quarterbacks second chances. It just doesn't give them many second careers.
The more interesting part of the exercise came from looking beyond who survived and asking what actually changed for the quarterbacks who managed to turn things around after failed first chances. That's where the data become more instructive than simply pointing at Darnold or Baker Mayfield and declaring that quarterbacks sometimes need a change of scenery.
The successful reclamation projects didn't suddenly become different players; more often, they found ways to improve -- sometimes dramatically -- the one or two weaknesses that had been holding them back.
Final NYJ season → 2024 MIN
* EPA/DB = EPA per dropback; TWP = turnover-worthy play rate; P2S = pressure-to-sack ratio
Darnold didn't eliminate turnover-worthy plays or suddenly become much better at avoiding sacks. He became more accurate, his big-time throw rate increased by 3.3 percentage points and he started generating far more production from those throws. It's also worth remembering just how bad the situation had become around him by his final season in New York: Darnold played through a shoulder injury while a Jets offense short on weapons and offensive line help sputtered through the final year of the Adam Gase era.
Jones followed a different path. His big-time throw rate barely changed between his disastrous final New England season and his 2025 run with San Francisco, but his adjusted accuracy improved by nearly eight percentage points and his turnover-worthy-play rate fell by 2.8 points.
Jones certainly contributed to his own demise in New England, but the environment around him didn't help: he played in three different offensive systems in three seasons, including the ill-fated Matt Patricia/Joe Judge arrangement in 2022, before Bill O'Brien took over in 2023. The Patriots also paired a pocket-dependent quarterback with a shaky offensive line and one of the league's least productive passing offenses. Jones didn't suddenly become a more dynamic quarterback in San Francisco; he became a much more consistent one.
Mayfield, who falls outside the strict Year 3 cutoff but is too relevant as a reclamation success to ignore, offers yet another path. His adjusted accuracy barely moved between his ugly 2021 season in Cleveland and his resurgence in Tampa Bay, and neither did his big-time throw rate. But his pressure-to-sack rate improved by nearly 11 percentage points, eliminating one of the problems that had consistently put Cleveland's offense behind schedule.
That's the encouraging part of this exercise. Reclamation doesn't necessarily require rebuilding a QB from scratch, and the circumstances surrounding the original failure matter, too. Sometimes a healthier quarterback, a better supporting cast or a more stable coaching situation can help, but the successful reclamations still required the player to improve in the one or two areas that had previously held him back. And that's where the cases for McCarthy and…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Bears' Coby Bryant to miss 4-6 months after knee surgery
summary: Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during practice
full_text:
Bears safety Coby Bryant will miss four to six months after he underwent surgery on his knee, coach Ben Johnson announced on Tuesday. The extended absence comes as an unpleasant surprise for Chicago, as Bryant was not initially expected to require surgery for the hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture he suffered during a training camp practice.
Bryant, 27, was visibly emotional when he sustained the injury and had to be carted off after going down during a one-on-one drill, per Adam Hoge . The Bears are hopeful that Bryant will be available in the playoffs should they clinch a spot in the field.
Chicago signed Bryant, formerly of the Seahawks, to a three-year, $40 million deal this offseason, hoping to fortify its secondary with 2025 starting safeties Kevin Byard and Jaquan Brisker, both free agents. Byard signed with the Patriots , Brisker with the Steelers .
A fourth-round pick out of Cincinnati in 2022, Bryant thrived when Mike Macdonald arrived in Seattle in 2024 and moved him from cornerback to safety. Over the past two seasons, Bryant recorded seven interceptions (and returned one for a touchdown), 139 tackles, 13 passes defended, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. He started all 15 games he appeared in last season, as well as all three of the Seahawks ' playoff games en route to their Super Bowl triumph.
Chicago drafted Oregon safety Dillon Thieneman 25th overall in April, and he is likely to start at one safety spot. Cam Lewis could be next up to take Bryant's starting spot early in the season.
The Bears open their 2026 season on Sept. 13 -- less than six weeks away -- against the Panthers .
This is a significant loss for the Bears in more ways than one.
First, Bryant, the player, is an ascending talent with a nose for the football, the speed and agility to cover, and the strength to really thump opposing pass catchers and runners. His versatility is a sign of where the game is going at the safety position. According to Pro Football Focus, Bryant played the vast majority of his snaps (908 to be exact) at free safety last year, including playoffs, but he also played 177 snaps as a box safety and 60 snaps as a slot cornerback.
The Bears finished 29th in yards allowed per play last year, but survived thanks in large part to a league-leading 33 turnovers forced. Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen were certainly looking forward to having more down-to-down success and not having to rely so heavily on turnovers -- which can be finicky year over year -- and Bryant was a big part of that.
Second, the Bears are already thin in the secondary. Safety Elijah Hicks is on the PUP list with a shin injury, and standout nickel back Kyler Gordon is also on the PUP due to a calf injury that has had him sidelined all offseason. It's been a frustrating run for Gordon, who played in just five games, including the playoffs, last year due to calf and groin issues.
"Obviously, he's frustrated," general manager Ryan Poles said. "We're frustrated."
C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who played significant snaps for Chicago last year, joined the Bills this offseason. Behind Bryant, Thieneman, Hicks and Lewis on the depth chart are either undrafted rookies or journeymen who haven't played much. It makes sense that Chicago could pursue outside help.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Christian McCaffrey, Alec Pierce and more
summary: Keep track of every major injury, setback, and recovery timeline across the league as teams prepare for the upcoming season
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn delivered some troubling news on Tuesday, as first-round pick tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss some time after "having a little setback." There's not an exact timetable for his return, although Glenn doesn't think Sadiq will miss the season opener. The rookie had offseason hernia surgery.
The No. 16 overall pick was the top tight end in his past draft, setting career highs with 51 catches for 560 yards and eight touchdowns for the Oregon Ducks last season. No FBS tight end caught more touchdowns than Sadiq. He was expected to make an immediate impact on this Jets offense, but New York does have another capable tight end in Mason Taylor.
McCaffrey missed Monday's practice with what the team called "tightness," which obviously doesn't provide much in the way of information. CMC is coming off a season during which he led the NFL with 413 touches, then recorded 37 more in two playoff games. He has a history of breaking down following seasons with huge workloads, so any missed practice time is obviously worth monitoring.
Pearsall is expected to undergo season-ending surgery on his ongoing PCL injury that has been an issue since last season. Niners general manager John Lynch said that Pearsall is expected to make a full recovery.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
Bosa missed Saturday's practice with "soreness," and on Tuesday 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the star pass rusher is considered week to week due to tendinitis in his surgically repaired knee.
Allen, who had been enjoying a strong start to his first NFL camp, was carted off the field on Saturday after colliding with Kaiir Elam on a special teams drill. ESPN later reported that test conducted on Allen revealed a shin bruise. Nothing was torn or broke, so he appears to have dodged a bullet.
During Saturday's practice, Johnson went down and was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was aided off the field. He was also seen clutching the area around his Achilles. Despite being carted to the locker room, ESPN reports that Gardner-Johnson merely suffered a lower calf strain, so he avoided any serious injury.
Johnson, 28, was enjoying a solid start to training camp. A seven-year veteran, Johnson's NFL accolades includes a Super Bowl win with the Eagles and leading the NFL in interceptions back in 2022.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
Atlanta brought its Aug. 4 practice to a close after Walker went down with a leg injury. It is feared to be a torn ACL for the second-year edge rusher. His Falcons teammates took knees and surrounded him while trainers evaluated him, and he was then carted off the field. Walker sustained the injury in an 11-on-11 two-minute drill at the Falcons' non-padded practice.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
Former first-round pick Xavier Legette reportedly went down hard on his back and head while attempting to make a catch during drills on Tuesday. After remaining on the turf for some time, the wideout was helped up and carted off the field, per WCNC .
While it doesn't appear Legette suffered a serious, season-ending injury, it was another scare for a team that has already suffered too many losses in training camp. Legette is still looking to live up to his No. 32 overall pick billing. In 15 games played last year, he caught 35 passes for 363 yards and three touchdowns.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
Jordan is dealing with a hamstring injury that head coach Kellen Moore said could go into the regular season. Moore added "we'll see" as the Saints are continuing to evaluate the issue. New Orleans has already lost one defensive lineman for the season and can scarcely afford to lose another contributor up front.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
The Lions signed former Panthers center Cade Mays to a three-year deal worth $25 million this offseason to replace Graham Glasgow. However, Mays suffered a wrist injury that will force him to miss a "significant period of time," per head coach Dan Campbell. Mays will return at some point this year, "but it will be down the road."
Campbell told reporters that new running back Isiah Pacheco suffered an MCL sprain in practice, but that he is expected to be ready for the season opener vs. New Orleans.
Brown told NFL Media that he dislocated his thumb at a Patriots practice. Brown returned to practice and caught several passes. "Thumb out of place," he said. "You keep going." This is certainly going to be an important injury to monitor.
Bryant suffered a hyperextended knee, bone bruise and small fracture during practice. While his initial recovery timeline of eight to 10 weeks would have put him on track to…
author: Jared Dubin

title: Vikings name Kyler Murray starting quarterback over J.J. McCarthy
summary: The Vikings' QB battle has ended prior to the beginning of the preseason
full_text:
The quarterback battle in Minnesota has come to a swift conclusion, as the Vikings have named Kyler Murray their new starter over former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy . Head coach Kevin O'Connell informed the team of his decision on Tuesday. This battle was expected to last into the preseason, but O'Connell called the contest four days before the Vikings are scheduled to take the field against the New York Giants . As for the status of McCarthy, O'Connell said he is slotted in as the backup and "he's ready to go."
"There's moments in time where you know there's comfort from Kyler in the scheme,'' O'Connell said. "He had some really high completion days where he was able to show some really, really good understanding of just putting the ball in play, playing with great timing, rhythm. You guys have seen him be explosive when there's opportunities there, but you've also seen him check the ball down and put the ball in play and get us from a first-and-10 to a second-and-3. And then, as you continued to look at the body of work through those 10 days, what jumped out is what could be."
Murray will be the Vikings' fourth different Week 1 starting quarterback over the last four years. He was always viewed as the favorite to win this job over McCarthy, who became the only first-round pick since 1970 to finish last in the NFL in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in his first season. While Minnesota did rally to finish with a 9-8 record last year, the Vikings still missed the playoffs thanks to an underperforming offense.
Despite the demotion, the Vikings still believe McCarthy has a bright future ahead.
"He's still a guy that's only played 10 games,'' O'Connell said. "He's shown improvement off of last year. Even in this training camp with the work he's put in and his comfort level, just growing a little bit day in and day out. Very excited to continue to get to work with him every single day, coach him. "As he knows, he's holding the pen on his story and we're gonna support him and try to just help him continue to improve at the most difficult position in sports. He's gotta also understand, this isn't just a long-term mindset, which we want to have always for a player of his caliber and a young player like him, but it could be an immediate response needed. J.J.'s the kind of guy that'll be ready to rock and roll, I know that."
Murray was released by the Arizona Cardinals this offseason following seven years with the franchise. The former No. 1 overall pick won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2019, made two Pro Bowls, and took Arizona to the postseason once, but his play dipped in recent years. Murray has missed 30 out of a possible 68 games over the last five seasons, and his last winning season came back in 2021. In all, Murray went 38-48-1 during his time with the Cardinals.
Still, it's possible Murray is rejuvenated by this change of scenery. In Minnesota, he finds multiple upgrades he did not have in Arizona. For example, Murray has a star wideout for the first time since DeAndre Hopkins . Justin Jefferson is one of the best pass-catchers in the game, and just became the third player to ever begin a career with six straight seasons of 1,000 yards receiving. He's not the only weapon either, as Minnesota has a solid supporting cast which includes Aaron Jones , Jordan Mason , Jordan Addison , T.J. Hockenson and Jauan Jennings .
Murray also has the backing of a Brian Flores unit that finished No. 3 in total defense last season (282.6 yards allowed per game) and No. 7 in scoring defense (19.6 points allowed per game). If Murray can be an efficient distributor of the football, this Vikings team can return to the postseason.
It's curious that the Vikings made this decision before the team's first preseason game , and that O'Connell didn't want to give his two quarterbacks a chance to compete with live reps. Sometimes it's the preseason where quarterback battles are decided, and now the NFL world is left with just one legitimate quarterback battle to follow this month with the Cleveland Browns . Tua Tagovailoa may have the Atlanta Falcons job wrapped up since Michael Penix Jr . hasn't even been cleared for 11-on-11 work.
Ian Rapoport of NFL Network/ESPN said on "The Pat McAfee Show" that Murray and McCarthy pushed each other during this competition, but it did feel like the veteran was ahead. While the timing of this decision is surprising, what it does is give Minnesota's offense clarity, and the opportunity to practice full time with the new starting quarterback. No need to give McCarthy reps with the starting offense anymore.
In an ironic twist of fate, the Vikings are hoping Murray can be their " Sam Darnold ." Minnesota of course allowed Darnold to walk in free agency last offseason, and he was picked up by the Seattle Seahawks . Not many believed the journeyman could replicate a 14-3 season, but that's exactly what Darnold did as he helped Seattle not only win the NFC West and secure the No. 1 seed in the conference, but get over the hump entirely and win a Super Bowl .
There are some obvious differences between Darnold and Murray. One was coming off the best season of his NFL career while the other is coming off arguably his worst. But O'Connell just needs someone to come in and run his system efficiently -- not be Superman.
Reports from camp didn't indicate Murray was lighting up the practice field, and something to watch over the next month is how he adapts to O'Connell's timing-based passing attack. It's a bit different from what Murray has run in the past, and he needs to stay on time and in rhythm for it to work. Now that the competition has been decided, he has time to settle in.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: A.J. Brown beats Sauce Gardner in 1-on-1 training camp rep: Reaction draws fiery response from Colts CB
summary: Gardner set the record straight after his defensive mishap
full_text:
The New England Patriots invested heavily into wide receiver A.J. Brown with the blockbuster trade that went down June 1, and if his highlight play from training camp on Tuesday is any indication of what is to come this season, the move will pay off for the reigning AFC champions. In a joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts , Brown beat star cornerback Sauce Gardner in emphatic style on a 1-on-1 route.
Brown stopped on a dime on a sit route, and when he turned back to receive the ball, Gardner's feet slipped and caused him to stumble onto his hands. Brown hauled in the pass, turned upfield and would have forced Gardner to make an open-field tackle if the play was live.
A.J. Brown just DUSTED Sauce Gardner in 1v1s🔥 Patriots fans in attendance LOVE IT - @CLNSMedia pic.twitter.com/0g1GBXTSjf
Video of the play made the rounds on social media and generated a strong reaction to Brown's ability to get separation on the third-highest-paid cornerback in the NFL . Many have been quick over the last handful of months to jeer Gardner because of the calf injury he sustained last season, the immense amount of time he missed after joining the Colts and the sizable trade package Indianapolis gave up to acquire him. His snafu in coverage of Brown only added fuel to that fire.
Gardner pushed back against the cacophony of taunts aimed in his direction.
"all this from a 1on1 rep? 😂 & a 8 yard sit route at that? its a reason that's the only one yall saw 😴🔒" Gardner said in a since-deleted post .
When healthy, Gardner is among the stiffest defenders in the league. The 24-year-old displayed as much when he won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2022 and opened his career with back-to-back selections to the All-Pro first team. But his production slipped slightly in the final stages of his New York Jets career, and his injury battle last season further prevented him from returning to the top of the elite ranks.
Gardner remains one of the faces of the cornerback position, though, and if there is anything meaningful to glean from one play in training camp, it could be more telling of a potential exemplary season for Brown than a down year for the Colts' defensive back.
While Brown racked up the third-most catches of his career, scored seven touchdowns and posted his sixth 1,000-yard season in his final run with the Philadelphia Eagles , he also raised concerns over his athletic trajectory. He averaged just 2.2 yards of separation on his routes in 2025, which is on the lower end of his already modest-at-best career mark. Pair that with his history of lower-body injuries, and there exist concerns that his best years are behind him.
If Brown can replicate the kind of route-running ability he displayed on that rep against Gardner, though, he can be the exact kind of difference-maker the Patriots seek in the passing game.
author: Carter Bahns

title: 'We've been breaking that rule for eight years:' NFL rule change leads to funny confession from one head coach
summary: The NFL is now allowing head coaches to designate someone else to throw the challenge flag, but Zac Taylor has been doing it for years
full_text:
The NFL will be undergoing a slight rule change this year when it comes to coaching challenges. For the first time ever, each team's head coach will be allowed to delegate the job of throwing the red challenge flag to someone else on the staff.
Under the old rule, the head coach was in charge of throwing the flag, but there's now some leeway.
"The head coach or head coach's pregame challenge designee can initiate a challenge by throwing a red flag onto the field of play before the next legal snap or kick," the new rule states, via ESPN .
The NFL might want to start calling this the "Zac Taylor" rule, because apparently, the Bengals head coach was already doing this. The Bengals hired Taylor in 2019, and during his first year on the job, he decided to let his chief of coaching staff, Doug Rosfeld, throw the flag. That's how the team has handled things ever since.
"We've been breaking that rule for eight years because I've never thrown a challenge flag," Taylor said during his press conference Tuesday .
According to Taylor, he let the officiating crew know before each game that Rosfeld would throw the challenge flag, and no one ever took issue with that.
"They ask you that in pregame, who's got the flag," Taylor said. "It's never been an issue. I didn't even know it was frowned upon. I know there's other coaches in the league, I'm not the only one who's done that. I saw they implemented a new rule, so maybe we'll get a retroactive fine or something."
Although head coaches can now designate someone else to throw the challenge flag, most will likely stick to the routine they know. For Taylor, that means he won't be throwing the flag, and he explained why during his press conference.
"It's easier for me [not to be in charge of it]."
The Bengals coach said after an offensive series, he'll sometimes be talking to Joe Burrow or other offensive players. When he's doing that, he can't see everything happening on the field. That's where Rosfeld comes in. As Taylor's right-hand man, he's watching the field at all times.
Although Rosfeld holds the challenge flag, Taylor is always nearby if a situation comes up where the team might have to throw it.
"They always made it clear to me that I have to be next to Doug," Taylor said. "I guess if we ever need to sneak one by them when I was back there [talking to Joe] and they couldn't get me in the headset, Doug could have done it, but that's never come up. It's just part of our routine now. I feel better with Doug having it."
After throwing the flag for so long, Rosfeld is apparently on top of his game.
"He's on it," Taylor said. "He's paranoid. He doesn't want to miss it. I've yelled at him plenty of times."
In 2019, Rosfeld explained how he handles each challenge.
"When that situation arises, I move toward the referees," Rosfeld told The Athletic . "I make sure I get to know them before the game and know their names and make sure they know that I have the flag so that I can quickly get it down on the ground in front of them."
The Bengals' system seems to be working, because the team won five challenges last season, tied for the third-most in the NFL.
The NFL is now implementing a rule the Bengals have essentially been using since 2019, and it will be interesting to see how many other coaches end up letting someone else throw the flag.
author: John Breech
