title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: It’s game week (kinda)
summary: The wait is over. For the first time in the 2026 season, the Cincinnati Bengals will take the field against someone other than themselves. The Bengals will host the Detroit Lions on Thursday evening in Paycor Stadium. The starters will be playing, though they won’t see the whole game—possibly not even anything after the first […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco (16) and quarterback Joe Burrow (9) chat during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Tuesday, Aug. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The wait is over. For the first time in the 2026 season, the Cincinnati Bengals will take the field against someone other than themselves. The Bengals will host the Detroit Lions on Thursday evening in Paycor Stadium. The starters will be playing, though they won’t see the whole game—possibly not even anything after the first drive or two. We’ll still get a good look at the starters, and then we’ll get a pretty good look at the depth behind them. Here are a few things I’ll be keeping an eye on: Stay Healthy This is the only thing that matters. I don’t care if they win or lose. I don’t care if everyone plays terribly and the entire fan base gets a terrible sense of dread. I don’t care about any of it. All I care about is the guys who go out on the field and come off with nothing more than the typical bumps and bruises. The Bengals have something special going. The offense has never been in doubt, but the defense is completely overhauled. With so much more talent and depth on the defensive line, and with Bryan Cook added to a healthy secondary, the defense could complement a top-tier offense deep into the postseason. If everyone stays healthy. That starts Thursday. Offense doesn’t miss a beat The Bengals’ starting offense in 2026 is going to be the same starting offense that walked off the field in 2025—on paper. The offensive line is the best Joe Burrow has had in his career. Burrow has the best wide receiver duo in the league in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and the rest of the receivers and tight ends all have a role to play. I’d like to see the Bengals’ offense come out on the field and look like I expect them to look when the season starts. An opening-drive touchdown would be nice to see. Defensive line improvement The defensive line in 2025 included Trey Hendrickson, BJ Hill, TJ Slaton and Myles Murphy. Hendrickson is gone, but Hill, Slaton and Murphy are still here. Only Murphy is on top of the depth chart in 2026 on the defensive line, and that could have something to do with Shemar Stewart’s knee injury. The rest of the starting defensive line is comprised of new starters brought to Cincinnati via free agency or trade. Dexter Lawrence is the new face of the defense, and was acquired via trade with the Giants. They also brought in Jonathan Allen, who is starting next to Lawrence, and Boye Mafe, who is starting opposite of Murphy. This is the most improved position group on the team. It would be nice to see a little something from them against the Lions. Burrow under center, multiple tight ends? There has been a lot of talk about the new defense, but there has also been quite a bit of news released from camp about Burrow’s increased presence under center. If the Bengals are intending to put Burrow under center more often, it could open up entire new branches of the playbook. The same could be said for the reports that the Bengals have been running 13 personnel in camp, meaning there is one wide receiver, one running back and three wide receivers. With multiple options at tight end, including Mike Gesicki, Erick All and a couple more, the offense could look totally different than what we’re expecting. Will we see it in the preseason? Most teams like to keep things pretty vanilla in the preseason so as not to give anything away, but we might see a play or two. What will you be looking for on Thursday? Sound off! Relevant Song Lyrics: It’s those changes in latitudes, changes in attitudes Nothing remains quite the same With all of our running and all of our cunning If we couldn’t laugh we would all go insane. *I’m in Florida

summary: Ja’Marr Chase has become one of the NFL’s premier receivers since getting drafted to the Cincinnati Bengals and reunited with Joe Burrow. full_text: Ja’Marr Chase has become one of the NFL’s premier receivers since getting drafted to the Cincinnati Bengals and reunited with Joe Burrow. He is up there with the top names in the sport, as fellow LSU teammate Justin Jefferson also sits atop the leaderboard for top wide-outs in the league. However, Chase has his eye on setting an NFL record instead of just becoming the clear-cut top WR1 in the league. In a recent sit-down after a training camp practice, Chase made it known he is targeting the NFL single-season record of 23 receiving touchdowns set by Randy Moss in 2007. Ja’Marr Chase isn’t worried about topping JSN or Justin Jefferson for WR yardage crown anymore But there’s 1 last individual goal Chase needs: 23 TDs, to break NFL single season record. pic.twitter.com/ldeP5D9NRE — Cameron Wolfe (@CameronWolfe) August 9, 2026 If Chase could make this happen, not only would he be seen as the clear-cut No. 1 receiver in the NFL, but the Bengals would likely also be having a great season in the Queen City. With the connection that Burrow and Chase have, though, it seems more likely this could eventually happen than it didn’t. Let’s hope it does. We have needed something major to cheer for the last few seasons, and this would be a win-win all around.

summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have some questions at cornerback. While DJ Turner II appears to be a breakout star, the other primary boundary cornerback, Dax Hill, has been sidelined with hamstring tightness. In training camp, that is the perfect opportunity for a player lower on the depth chart to prove themselves. With Hill sidelined, DJ Ivey […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - OCTOBER 26: Cincinnati Bengals cornerback D.J. Ivey (38) during the game against the New York Jets and the Cincinnati Bengals on October 26, 2025, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals have some questions at cornerback. While DJ Turner II appears to be a breakout star, the other primary boundary cornerback, Dax Hill, has been sidelined with hamstring tightness. In training camp, that is the perfect opportunity for a player lower on the depth chart to prove themselves. With Hill sidelined, DJ Ivey and rookie Tacario Davis have had extended opportunities to show coaches what they can do. Going against two of the best receivers in the NFL in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is not only good practice work for them, but a chance to show defensive coordinator Al Golden what they can do against the best of the best. As of now, it appears Ivey is doing the most with the opportunity.Bengals News: 1 Bengals training camp bright spot won’t surprise fans “Ivey has made the most of his time running with the first team, with a pass breakup on a deep post from Burrow to Higgins on Tuesday, then in perfect position to break up another deep ball for Higgins on Thursday. He hasn’t been picked on consistently or caught out of step.” Ivey has appeared in 36 games since becoming a seventh-round pick in 2023. If camp is any indication, he could be in line for an even bigger role this season. Bengals Veteran Emerges as Preseason Trade Candidate “Slaton is currently listed as one of the backup defensive tackles on the Bengals’ depth chart, but he could soon be lapped by players like Landon Robinson and Kris Jenkins. Slaton is on an expiring contract, and it would save the Bengals nearly $7 million by making a move.” Suddenly, the defensive tackle room has become crowded. After two big offseason additions paired with two premium draft picks in recent years, could Slaton be the odd man out? New experienced, vocal leaders are setting a tone for the Bengals defense “Adding high-level talent who have done it before, you’ve seen it on the tape and seen it in their careers,” coach Zac Taylor said. “You add to that the humans they are and the leaders they are. Not only did we add a lot of really talented players, they’re really good in the locker room and aren’t afraid to lead and help everyone else get to the next level.” There is a different feeling around the Bengals’ defense this offseason and with the players they brought in, it seems that championship experience was a big reason why. The Black Cloud Hanging Over Zac Taylor and the Bengals Entering 2026 Zac Taylor spoke candidly about the failures of the last three seasons and the impact it has had on him. Heading in to a season where he could be coaching for his job, it appears he is ready to attack 2026 with some tenacity. Bengals Release Uniform Combination for Preseason Week 1 against Detroit Lions The Bengals open their preseason at home and we now know the uniform combination they will wear.

title: Browns sign TE Dae’Quan Wright from Eagles, place DB on IR
summary: The Cleveland Browns signed big-bodied tight end Dae’Quan Wright out of Ole Miss to bolster the group’s depth. Wright (6’-4”, 255 pounds) is an athletic tight end but has been inconsistent as a blocker. He went undrafted in April’s NFL draft and then signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was recently waived. In a corresponding […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 10: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dae'Quan Wright #45 is shown with the ball during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 10th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns signed big-bodied tight end Dae’Quan Wright out of Ole Miss to bolster the group’s depth. Wright (6’-4”, 255 pounds) is an athletic tight end but has been inconsistent as a blocker. He went undrafted in April’s NFL draft and then signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was recently waived. In a corresponding move, the Browns placed CB Damarri Mathis on IR. In Tuesday’s practice, Mathis was carted off the field. Wright began his college career at Virginia Tech and then entered the transfer portal. He chose Ole Miss, where he played the past two seasons. In his college career, he played in 47 games with 113 receptions for 1,603 yards, a 14.2-yard-per-catch average, scored nine touchdowns, averaged 34.1 yards per game, and scored 54 points. In 2025, he was named Second Team All-SEC. Scouting report on Wright on NFL.com : “Wright is a high-cut, tight-hipped tight end who can stretch the field vertically but lacks fluidity and bend for crisp route breaks from speed. He builds speed to threaten defenses, working the vertical limbs of the route tree. He can gain an advantage on linebackers when aligned outside. He’s big and strong enough to improve as a run blocker but needs better technique and commitment in that area. Wright projects as a Day 3 pick who should fight for a role as a TE3/4.“ Currently, the Browns tight end group consists of Harold Fannin, Jack Stoll, Blake Whiteheart, Brenden Bates, and fellow rookies Joe Royer and Ryan Carsen. Royer has not been present during training camp due to what has been described by the team as a personal reason. The Browns will kick off the preseason on Saturday at 1 p.m. on WYTV-33.

title: Browns DC: It is the players that make every scheme work
summary: Cleveland Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg is not walking into an easy situation in 2026.  Not only will this season be his first as a defensive coordinator, but Rutenberg is following Jim Schwartz, who is considered one of the league’s best at calling a defense, which was on display over the past three seasons in […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg of the Cleveland Browns watches a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Cleveland Browns defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg is not walking into an easy situation in 2026. Not only will this season be his first as a defensive coordinator, but Rutenberg is following Jim Schwartz, who is considered one of the league’s best at calling a defense, which was on display over the past three seasons in Cleveland. That hasn’t seemed to bother Rutenberg much so far, as he has had his hands full during training camp: Installing the new defensive system . Seeing what new defensive end Jared Verse brings to the table . Watching his best linebacker, Carson Schwesinger, miss the past week of practice with an injury. Dealing with seemingly non-stop injuries at defensive tackle . Figuring out how best to work rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren into an already talented secondary . Rutenberg appears to be holding up well – going against an offense led by the league’s worst quarterback room every day in practice probably helps – but he also comes across as a coach who won’t let his ego get in the way of calling a good game. That was evident on Tuesday when Rutenberg pointed out that a defense is only as good as its players ( quotes via a team-provided transcript ): “The key is players. Players make every scheme, whether you’re disguised or not, cover three, cover one, it doesn’t matter, everybody runs similar skills. It’s about getting guys to understand what we’re trying to do, which they’ve done at the highest level, and giving players opportunities to be successful in whatever coverage or scheme we’re in. “I can’t give away the secret sauce, can I? But again, it comes down to players understanding their job and finding their inches within the scheme. That’s what great players do: they prepare hard, they study hard, they anticipate and react. When they know they can take their shot, they take it. Otherwise, they play fundamentally sound football.” Rutenberg is also smart enough to admit he does not know everything and if a mistake is made, fix it and then get going again: “I’m learning every day. It’s awesome. We’ve got a great mentor in Todd, an unbelievable defensive staff, and a great group of defensive players, and together we’re constantly learning. If a mistake happens – own it, fix it and keep it moving. If good stuff happens, celebrate it, embrace it and keep it moving.” Fairly or not, Rutenberg will be compared to Schwartz this fall, especially if something goes wrong. But based on what the defense has shown so far, it looks as if the Browns will be in good hands when the defense is on the field.

title: Browns offseason once again proving GM Andrew Berry right
summary: We may never know what changed, beyond the fact that the team actually had a full complement (and more) of picks, between the first few NFL drafts for GM Andrew Berry and the one that came in 2025. It could be as simple as the number of high draft picks, once depleted by the failed […]
full_text: Andrew Berry, general manager, and Jimmy Haslam, owner, chat at the Browns mini camp in Berea on April 21, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co We may never know what changed, beyond the fact that the team actually had a full complement (and more) of picks, between the first few NFL drafts for GM Andrew Berry and the one that came in 2025 . It could be as simple as the number of high draft picks, once depleted by the failed trade for QB Deshaun Watson , but Berry’s rookie class last year likely saved his job . After being retained while HC Kevin Stefanski was fired , the big question, besides the quarterback position, was whether Berry could do it again in the NFL draft. The 2026 NFL draft grades all pointed to a very strong “yes” answer to that question, but that was before the players hit the field. Now, with training camp in full swing, it seems like that early answer is now being solidified into a “yes” poured into concrete. The cement has not set yet; that will only come as regular season games take place, but so far Berry’s 2026 draft class is creating a ton of excitement: OT Spencer Fano has moved into the starter’s role at left tackle and is holding his own against star DE Jared Verse WR KC Concepcion is rarely dropping passes, making acrobatic catches, and is a threat any time the ball is in his hands WR Denzel Boston just took over as the starting “X” receiver after an entire offseason of just wowing people S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is impressing teammates and being used as a versatile chess piece that can create problems for any offense For any draft class, four studs would be a huge win. After the second round, Berry added a number of talented players who need some development. OT Austin Barber has shown flashes of being a bully-type right tackle. OL Parker Brailsford was at least competing for the starting center job before getting hurt, while LB Justin Jefferson has made some plays and seems locked into an important special teams role as a rookie fifth-round pick. TE Joe Royer has been absent due to personal reasons, while QB Taylen Green is a raw developmental project, and TE Carsen Ryan , the team’s final pick, is fighting for a roster spot. With preseason games just around the corner, Browns fans will get to see more and more of the rookie class as Berry’s new youngsters get a chance to prove him right, in a big way, for the second straight season. title: Browns roster concern on the defensive side of the ball could be a big one
summary: In the NFL, the worst thing to happen in a game on the defensive side of the ball is to hand over games by allowing the other team to run against you at will. Especially up the gut. In the past few years under DC Jim Schwartz, this didn’t happen much against the Cleveland Browns […]
full_text: DT Maliek Collins #96 (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the NFL, the worst thing to happen in a game on the defensive side of the ball is to hand over games by allowing the other team to run against you at will. Especially up the gut. In the past few years under DC Jim Schwartz, this didn’t happen much against the Cleveland Browns defense. RELATED: D-LINE LOOKING TO BE VIOLENT In years past before Schwartz arrived, opponents ran up the middle all the time when Joe Woods ran the defense. The main reason was he set up the defense in the 4-2-5 quite a bit. The elimination of that third linebacker placed a huge hole in the center. Under Schwartz’s scheme, the linebackers were there for run support and to cover tight ends and running backs. This meant the defensive line had to hold its own and plug running lanes as well as rush the passer. Rarely did linebackers or safeties blitz. The idea was for everyone to play their spot on the field. The right athletes The other issue with a porous middle is the players themselves. Playoff teams are stout against the run in their interior. The Browns’ DC Mike Rutenberg this year will follow Schwartz’s alignment regarding the defensive line and linebacker group. This should continue to get better at stopping the run. But it takes players. Make that, healthy players. Right now, there is a lot of uncertainty with the interior defensive line. Gone is the dependable Shelby Harris, who is now with the New York Football Giants. Each practice session in training camp reveals that the Browns DT room is fairly thin. It is uncomfortable. There is sentiment that this might become the final training camp for former second-round draft pick Michael Hall, Jr. (6’-3”, 300 pounds). He has had enough time to find his place on this roster, and at no time has he been seen as a starting defender. In his two seasons in the league, he has played in 17 games and has just three starts. 25 total tackles and 2.5 sacks do not justify his salary, and in the end, it may justify keeping him. He suffered a right knee injury during OTAs this spring, which may expedite his departure. Last year, Hall tore his MCL with a knee dislocation against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 11. This is a guy who has never been hurt at any level and now can’t stay on the field. One of the starting DTs, Maliek Collins (6’-2”, 310 pounds), was a splash signing at a need position in last year’s free agency period. He is a former third-round draft pick of the Dallas Cowboys and signed a two-year deal with Cleveland. This means this is his contract year. Collins was a beast on the field and proved valuable against the run , and surprisingly added 6.5 sacks and 15 pressures from the interior. But he suffered a season-ending quad injury in Week 13 against the San Francisco 49ers that landed him on IR and required surgery. To start this year’s training camp, Collins was placed on the PUP list. Last year, Collins was referred to as a “secret superstar ,” and now this year, he has been mentioned as one player who may not return if the team allows him to enter free agency. The backup department Sam Kamara and Kalia Davis are guys who are considered quality depth players. But both are dealing with injuries on their own. Kamara (6’-0”, 272 pounds) has been with the Browns off-and-on since 2022. He has been signed, released, signed to the practice squad, brought up to the main roster, then released, and the cycle just continues with similar scenarios. He has played in 22 games in four seasons with a single start. Basically, a career backup. The Browns like him because he can bounce to the outside if needed. On August 3, Kamara was carted off the field during a practice session. His injury remains undisclosed. Davis (6’-2”, 310 pounds) was another free agent signing. As with Kamara, he left practice in early August with a lower-body injury and has been limited to watching from the sidelines. The Browns list him as day-to-day. He has an extensive injury history in the NFL as well as in college. Last year’s first-round pick, Mason Graham (6’-4”, 315 pounds), has missed some practices due to minor inconveniences. It was revealed that last season he played with a cracked and broken rib sustained late in his rookie year after making a tackle, but played anyway. That has had time to heal during the offseason. Our own Jared Mueller gave this analysis on the team’s injury front: So, out of the first six players listed on the Browns depth chart at defensive tackle, everything written so far has been about five of these athletes. Only Adin Huntington has been spared the injury plague. Backups have been signed recently to help this room just in case somebody can not start the season on a healthy note, but the franchise does not want to release him. Elijah Chatman (6’-0”, 278 pounds) is a guy who is a bit light for the position and has just three starts for the Giants the past two years. He has 24 total tackles, 1 sack, 4 pressures, and 0 missed tackles. Travis Bell (6’-0”, 310 pounds) was a seventh-round pick of the Chicago Bears, with the Browns being his sixth team. He has played in two NFL games, but won a championship with the Louisville Kings of the UFL this spring. He had 38 total tackles, 6 tackles for loss, and 1 sack. Coziah Izzard (6’-3”, 305 pounds): Izzard went undrafted in last year’s NFL draft before signing with the Kansas City Chiefs after a stellar college campaign at Penn State, where he was referred to as “an athletic freak.” He spent time on their practice squad and was later waived. He then spent time with the New Orleans Saints and Arizona Cardinals and was waived last week. Patrick Jenkins (6’-2”, 287 pounds) is now on his sixth team, two in the UFL. He played in all 10 games for the Columbus Aviators with 22 total tackles, 6 tackles for loss, and 1.5 sacks. Izzard and Jenkins have yet to play in an NFL game. The grand total of all four of these backup players is 24 NFL games played, two starts, and 113 defensive snaps, but plenty of UFL games played. Painful reality : Too thin at DT Most coaching staffs keep four defensive tackles and five defensive ends. This year, the Browns may need to keep about eight defensive tackles on hand: four on the main roster, and another four on the practice squad. Having several good players is essential because Rutenberg will want to rotate his defensive tackles in each game . This means despite not being a starter, the remainder of this group will get a good number of snaps during the year. So far in training camp, Huntington and Chatman are getting quite a few first-team reps . None of the injuries to these DTs appear to be serious, but it is definitely a thing for this year’s Browns defensive front. The Browns might want to bring in another unsigned free agent that has game experience just in case something happens. Attrition hits every club, but this year Cleveland has been hit pretty hard and early. But who is still out there? Greg Gaines (6’-1”, 312 pounds) Age: 30 NFL experience: 7 years Total tackles: 186 Tackles for loss: 16 Sacks: 14.5 Forced fumbles: 0 Fumble recoveries: 2 Pass defenses: 0 Pressures: 51 QB hits: 35 Knockdowns: 17 Hurries: 17 Missed tackles: 11 DaQuan Jones (6’-4”, 320 pounds) Age: 34 NFL experience: 12 years Total tackles: 372 Tackles for loss: 34 Sacks: 20.0 Forced fumbles: 4 Fumble recoveries: 3 Pass defenses: 7 Pressures: 51 QB hits: 63 Knockdowns: 33 Hurries: 32 Missed tackles: 30 Folo Fatukasi (6’-4”, 318 pounds) Age: 31 NFL experience: 8 years Total tackles: 195 Tackles for loss: 28 Sacks: 7.0 Forced fumbles: 1 Fumble recoveries: 1 Pass defenses: 7 Pressures: 38 QB hits: 24 Knockdowns: 14 Hurries: 16 Missed tackles: 12 How worried are you about the DT position for the Browns roster? title: What Browns player could be a surprise cut?
summary: With each new season comes a new roster and a series of important decisions that will take shape throughout training camp. Each year, certain position groups are loaded with talent, forcing the team to make difficult and sometimes unexpected cuts. Looking at the Cleveland Browns’ 2026 roster, which position groups could force the team to […]
full_text: With each new season comes a new roster and a series of important decisions that will take shape throughout training camp. Each year, certain position groups are loaded with talent, forcing the team to make difficult and sometimes unexpected cuts. Looking at the Cleveland Browns’ 2026 roster, which position groups could force the team to make some of its toughest decisions? Tylan Wallace, Wide Receiver Wallace was brought in to add depth to the wide receiver room while also contributing on special teams. After the team drafted some young, exciting talent at wide receiver in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston , there is the potential that Wallace could find himself on the outside looking in. His familiarity with the current Browns coaching staff and versatility as a receiver should improve his chances, but he’ll need to continue proving himself throughout training camp to secure a spot on the 53-man roster. Jack Stoll, Tight End The final roster is always a numbers game, and certain position groups have to take a hit to benefit other groups. That could be the case for the tight ends, which might leave Stoll off the list. Since he is more of a blocking tight end, Cleveland could choose to prioritize other skill sets when putting together the final roster. Stoll will need to prove his value in the preseason to earn a spot. Daniel Thomas, Safety Thomas was brought into a group that has been a bit of a mixed bag over the last few seasons. There is some competition at the position this season, and the Browns may opt to prioritize younger talent they believe offers greater upside than a player like Thomas. Only time will tell what Cleveland ultimately prioritizes at the position. Let me know what you think in the comments – What Browns player could be a surprise cut? Join the conversation! title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 33
summary: It is Day 33 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: DALLAS, TX - CIRCA 1978: Defensive end, Ed Too Tall Jones #72 of the Dallas Cowboys in action against the Atlanta Falcons during an NFL football game circa 1978 at Texas Stadium in Dallas, Texas. Jones played for the Cowboys from 1974-78 and 1980-89. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 33 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. It’s time to have some fun as we get to Day 33 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the greatest fourth-quarter comebacks in Cowboys playoff history. Dallas trailed the Atlanta Falcons entering the final period, but the “Duel in Dixie” game would show that Dallas was never out the game, even when all things looked lost. Sunday, January 4, 1981 — 4:00 p.m. ET Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium, Atlanta, Georgia Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Atlanta Falcons 27 The Cowboys faced a transitional season during which Roger Staubach had retired, leaving Danny White to replace one of the most respected quarterbacks in NFL history. Despite this, Dallas managed to finish 12-4, but Philadelphia won the NFC East, forcing them to begin the postseason in the Wild Card round. After defeating the Los Angeles Rams, Dallas travelled to face an Atlanta team that had also gone 12-4 and earned the NFC’s top seed. Atlanta quickly demonstrated why it had won nine consecutive games during the regular season. Tim Mazzetti opened the scoring with a 38-yard field goal before Steve Bartkowski connected with Alfred Jenkins for a 60-yard touchdown. Dallas answered with a Rafael Septién field goal, but the Falcons held a 10-3 advantage after the opening quarter. White’s five-yard touchdown pass to Billy Joe DuPree brought the Cowboys level, but Lynn Cain’s one-yard scoring run quickly gave Atlanta the lead. The Falcons nearly added more points before halftime, but Steve Wilson intercepted Bartkowski to keep the deficit at 17-10. The situation became even more difficult after halftime. Preston Pearson caught a short pass and broke into Atlanta territory, but he was chased down and lost a fumble at the Falcons’ 15-yard line. Atlanta took advantage when Bartkowski found William Andrews for a 12-yard touchdown, extending the lead to 24-10. The fourth quarter brought history as Dallas embarked on a comeback. A long possession that spanned the third-quarter break culminated in Robert Newhouse’s one-yard touchdown that reduced the deficit to seven. However, an interception by Atlanta safety Tom Pridemore resulted in another Mazzetti field goal, leaving Dallas trailing 27-17 late in the fourth quarter and with a significant challenge ahead. White responded by directing a 62-yard touchdown drive. He completed the series with a 14-yard pass to Drew Pearson, cutting Atlanta’s lead to 27-24 with 3:04 remaining. The Dallas defense then forced the quick stop it desperately needed, giving White one final opportunity. Here we go. With the season on the line, the Cowboys began their drive from their own 30-yard line, determined to move the ball. Pearson delivered the decisive play, breaking through Atlanta’s coverage and catching White’s 23-yard touchdown pass with just 47 seconds remaining. This game belongs on the countdown because it proved the Cowboys could remain a serious postseason threat after their legendary quarterback’s retirement. White was facing enormous expectations, yet he responded to a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit by leading three touchdown drives. The performance helped establish him as Staubach’s replacement and began a run of three consecutive NFC Championship Game appearances with White as the starter. #Cowboys vs #Falcons 1980 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Atlanta Falcons 27 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/f9bXt9cmDY — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 11, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Ed “Too Tall” Jones helped create the defensive stop that gave Dallas its final possession. His sudden movement before an Atlanta snap caused confusion along the Falcons’ offensive line, but he avoided crossing the line of scrimmage and helped end the drive. title: Biggest winners from the Cowboys’ joint practice with the Rams
summary: After eight training camp practices, it was time for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys to get their first true test. Dallas traveled over to Woodland Hills to take part in a joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams. Coming off a 12-win season in which they made it to the NFC Championship Game before losing to […]
full_text: After eight training camp practices, it was time for the 2026 Dallas Cowboys to get their first true test. Dallas traveled over to Woodland Hills to take part in a joint practice with the Los Angeles Rams. Coming off a 12-win season in which they made it to the NFC Championship Game before losing to the Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks, the Rams had arguably the best offseason of any team in the league. Los Angeles made two big moves to upgrade their defense, acquiring the best defensive player in football, edge rusher Myles Garrett, along with stud cornerback Trent McDuffie. The Rams were already ultra-talented, but these offseason moves cemented them as the Super Bowl favorite. Currently, the Rams are the odds-on favorite to win Super Bowl LXI at +500. The Buffalo Bills, the team with the second-best chance according to Vegas, are double the odds at +1000. Clearly, the Rams were going to be a big test for the Cowboys in their first joint practice of the year. It may be extremely early, but pacing yourself against the Super Bowl favorite can be very valuable at this time of year. Dallas’ offensive line did catch a bit of a break as the Rams decided to hold Myles Garrett out of the practice. No Myles Garrett for the Rams today — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 11, 2026 While there was no video allowed during the team portion of the practice, we did get plenty of reporting on what went down between the two teams. Dallas had some impressive performances in their first real test of training camp. To the surprise of many, it was the defense who stood out most. According to multiple reports, here are the biggest winners from today’s joint practice. 1) Dallas’ pass rush A big test for the Cowboys’ defense today was whether they would be able to get consistent pressure on Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford. It sure seems like Dallas was able to do just that. title: 6 Cowboys that need a strong preseason start
summary: For the most diehard of Dallas Cowboys fans, their preseason begins on Tuesday, as the team scrimmages against a bona fide conference contender, the LA Rams. Paired with a Saturday visit to another NFC West contender, the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, for the real preseason game number one, and this is a huge […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 09: Phil Mafah #37 of the Dallas Cowboys runs the ball against the Los Angeles Rams in the second half of a NFL Preseason 2025 at SoFi Stadium on August 09, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the most diehard of Dallas Cowboys fans, their preseason begins on Tuesday, as the team scrimmages against a bona fide conference contender, the LA Rams. Paired with a Saturday visit to another NFC West contender, the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, for the real preseason game number one, and this is a huge week for Brian Schottenheimer’s team to put their competitiveness to the test. The Cowboys have been doing so against themselves for a sustained period of time in Oxnard already, which can develop a feistiness that shows a team is ready for some live competition against another opponent. Dallas potentially reached this point in their final practice before Tuesday’s Rams scrimmage on Sunday, with coach Schotty rallying the team together, unhappy with the start to that day’s work, and making them do conditioning afterwards. Brian Schottenheimer did not like the way the Cowboys started practice on Saturday, and he let them hear it: "get you're f—ing heads out of your a$$!" he hollered after huddling the entire team together. "Circuits! Let's f—ing go!" …the fans loved every bit of it. pic.twitter.com/5Cz1wk7zF6 — Mike Leslie (@MikeLeslieWFAA) August 9, 2026 Let’s take a look at six players, three offense and three defense, that need a strong start to the preseason later this week to continue their fight for a spot on the final roster, a role on gamedays, or even a starting job. WR Anthony Smith Wide receiver has become the quickest position to become a pet cat of Cowboys fans in recent years, an annual tradition to hang your cowboy hat on even when a lot of these receivers that stand out in the summer don’t make the team. Anthony Smith, as the team’s seventh-round pick, came into his rookie camp with every trait to be this next pet cat, but has been outshined a little by other under-the-radar pass catchers so far. One of the things working in Smith’s favor is his unteachable speed, which has more of a chance to start standing out with live reps against real opponents. Many of the highlight reel catches coming out of Cowboys camp have been contested with defensive backs in good position, but without full contact or always having pads on, the receivers are winning a lot of reps. Separation is still king when it comes to prolific passing offenses though, and Smith’s speed will give him a chance to separate from defenders who have authority to play at full speed. If the rookie out of Eastern Carolina, starting with the Rams scrimmage or at the Seahawks, can make a big play over the top, it will go a long way in a bottom of the WR depth chart competition that’s seen UDFA Camden Brown and Jonathan Mingo stand out so far. LT Nate Thomas A wrinkle of the Cowboys having incredible continuity on offense is how the coaching staff will find unique ways to challenge players still expected to start come the regular season, but ones that could use some competition behind them to bring out their best play. The best example of this so far is the way the Cowboys have declared something of a competition at left tackle between expected starter and former first-round pick Tyler Guyton, and Nate Thomas. The best case scenario has played out so far in Oxnard, with Guyton finding consistency and playing more than well enough to distance himself from Thomas. This doesn’t mean that, starter or not, Thomas won’t have a role – starting four games last season. Having Schottenheimer as well as Klayton Adams back as OC, with his expertise in both offensive line and tight end coaching, gives the Cowboys a chance to get really creative with different OL combinations when they want to get into heavier personnel. So far, we’ve heard more about rookie fourth-round pick Drew Shelton getting these creative types of looks than we have Thomas. Rookie tackle Drew Shelton spent some time with the tight ends in individual drills for when the Cowboys go to their jumbo formation. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) August 9, 2026 What Thomas does with these preseason reps and how much versatility he can show, as well as just how well he protects the Cowboys backup quarterbacks from the left tackle spot will be very important to keep an eye on come Saturday and beyond. RB Phil Mafah Phil Mafah and Jaydon Blue have been neck and neck in their fight for the primary RB spot behind Javonte Williams so far. We’re highlighting Mafah here because he profiles more similarly to Williams, where as Blue has a different skill set entirely with home run ability on the ground or in the pass game. i asked Klayton Adams about the competitiveness in the backup RB battle, and the #Cowboys OC has plenty of praise for Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis and Israel Abanikanda. this stuck out, though: “the guy that probably doesn't get as much credit as he deserves right now is Phil… pic.twitter.com/SXEGdFYyYv — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 5, 2026 With that said, the Cowboys are seeing the value in the year two jump Mafah has shown in camp so far, turning heads with long runs on a near daily basis. The next step to see just how much the Cowboys value last year’s seventh-round pick is seeing how they incorporate him into a game script in a preseason game. Dallas will likely be out to keep things fairly vanilla and not give away too many wrinkles of their scheme, which means even more potential for reps in the “base” run game grinding a back like Mafah between the tackles – where he’s looked good in camp. How much this type of rushing approach will remain in front of mind for the offense once all of the starters, mainly the firepower at wide receiver, are on the field is another question entirely. Strong preseason reps are always worth taking seriously though, and if Mafah stays hot and becomes a star of this preseason for the Cowboys, it will be harder and harder to ignore the fact he could have a real role on Sundays this season. DL LT Overton LT Overton is in an interesting spot as a promising draft pick out of Alabama for the Cowboys defensive line. Overton has been active as a run defender as a down lineman, which was always going to be his calling card compared to any high upside in pass rush. Where the Cowboys did just make a splash in the interior pass rush department is with Quinnen Williams’ extension. It may be William’s ability to penetrate the pocket that went the longest way in landing this deal, but make no mistake that run defense should be expected to come with the price the Cowboys paid as well. The same goes for last season’s big pickup at DT Kenny Clark, and the Cowboys also added veteran Jonathan Bullard and 1-tech Otito Ogbonnia this offseason. This stacks the depth chart pretty considerably against Overton getting meaningful reps as a rookie, but the preseason should see plenty of opportunity for him to get on the field. Wrote down LT Overton’s No. 99 down four times in the practice. Productive day in the run game for the rookie from Alabama. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) August 8, 2026 The Cowboys best true pass rush in camp has come from standup players off the edge, which could create a premium on keeping defensive linemen that can hold the point of attack and occupy blocks while setting a hard edge. Overton fits this description, and having reps against two physical NFC West teams like the Rams and Seahawks this week will put his first-year readiness to the test. LB Tyrus Wheat The Cowboys have come a long way from that faithful late night win in Pittsburgh in 2024 when Tyrus Wheat was a defensive starter due to injuries, and that is a very good thing. That doesn’t mean that a depth player like Wheat still doesn’t have value, but this training camp is likely the toughest uphill battle Wheat has faced to…

title: One Cowboys star has been dominating camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys decided that George Pickens will play the 2026 season on the franchise tag for a one-year price of $27.3 million. Pickens cordially agreed, putting to rest any potential contract drama and directing all the attention back onto the football field. That is just where he wants it, because on the field, the […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys runs after the catch during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys decided that George Pickens will play the 2026 season on the franchise tag for a one-year price of $27.3 million. Pickens cordially agreed, putting to rest any potential contract drama and directing all the attention back onto the football field. That is just where he wants it, because on the field, the 25-year-old receiver has been absolutely dazzling. The decision to tag him has been a point of contention for many. He is a great player, and coming off a career season during his first year with the Cowboys. The team should have a pretty good sense of what they have with him by now. So, why not just lock him down long term? The front office has opted to wait, for reasons that are not completely known. Maybe it is to challenge him to string together another strong season to solidify what will ultimately be a pricey investment. Maybe they want more time together to ensure any apprehensions that Pittsburgh had are no longer a concern. Or, knowing how this front office operates, maybe they have alternative plans about how to allocate resources, and he could end up being future trade bait. Who really knows their intentions? For now, Pickens is showing people in Oxnard that he is the real deal. It is still early, but he is the clear camp standout, regularly putting highlight after highlight on tape for all the onlookers. He is completely locked in with the offense, showcasing a burgeoning chemistry with Dak Prescott. The trust he has built with Prescott has made him a frequent recipient of contested passes. Dak just knows he has to put it up there and there is a good chance Pickens is coming down with it. Whether he is leaping vertically to snag one-handed catches, or just coming away with the football with defenders smothered all over him, he never ceases to impress. Pickens’ biggest strength is dominating 50/50 balls, and right now, he is putting on a clinic. He is very physical at the line of scrimmage, always putting defenders in catch-up scenarios. When it is time to go after the ball, his tracking is elite, and his body control is Baryshnikov-ish, using very subtle, last-second adjustments with his hands. He attacks the ball with intensity, consistently outfighting any defender draped all over him. This has been especially evident from his ongoing battles with second-year corner Shavon Revel Jr., who, despite having great positioning and long arms, still finds himself on the wrong end of many contested battles. Revel Jr. is actually playing quite aggressively and making him work for it, but Pickens just has an amazing catch radius and a nice wingspan of his own to pluck balls away from defenders. It has been quite a spectacle. Pickens’ dominant camp so far has fans reeling with optimism about just how great this offense can be. Combined with receiving counterparts like CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson, who are also both having a strong camp, the receiving group looks quite menacing. Now, with a full year in this scheme and even more evidence that he is the real deal, Pickens and the Cowboys are poised to have one of the greatest offenses in the league this year. Ultimately, this summer has proven that the franchise tag was not a distraction, but rather a launchpad. If the front office wanted to see if Pickens could handle the pressure of playing for his next contract, he is answering that challenge by putting on a great show in Southern California. By turning potential contract tension into pure camp dominance, he has transformed a risky one-year gamble into what looks like a guaranteed nightmare for NFL defenses. title: 6 reasons the Quinnen Williams extension is a big win for the Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys locked down a massive piece of their defense by signing their new stud defensive tackle to a three-year, $106 million extension, ensuring the team’s most disruptive force hangs around through the 2030 season. It was an uncharacteristically early move for a front office notorious for waiting things out, but taking action now […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 23: Quinnen Williams #92 of the Dallas Cowboys participates in warmups prior to a game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys locked down a massive piece of their defense by signing their new stud defensive tackle to a three-year, $106 million extension, ensuring the team’s most disruptive force hangs around through the 2030 season. It was an uncharacteristically early move for a front office notorious for waiting things out, but taking action now is a big win for the organization as it helps them in a multitude of ways. Today, we’ll run down all the reasons this was a great move for the Cowboys. Reason #1 – immediate cap relief, roster flexibility Before the extension, Williams was carrying base salaries of $21.6 million and $25.5 million, respectively, over the next two seasons. With a new deal, the team now has immediate salary cap relief, freeing up roughly $35 million over the next two years. This immediate cap savings gives the front office the flexibility to keep the roster loaded with talent as they continue to maximize the window with Dak Prescott. This could mean a lot of different things. Maybe they take on another pricey salary as teased by the front office, indicating that they are looking to make another deal. Maybe it means they’ll have room to afford George Pickens down the road, or, at the very least, slap that second franchise tag on him until they work towards a final decision. Again, flexibility. Reason #2 – cost control against a rising market If you look around, defensive tackles around the league are getting paid, and paid handsomely. The Philadelphia Eagles gave Jordan Davis a three-year, $78 million deal in March, only to turn around and extend Jalen Carter to a four-year, $152 million deal last month. The Tennessee Titans gave Jeffrey Simmons a three-year, $106 million deal in June. Teams are recognizing the importance of a bona fide interior stud, and they don’t come cheap. Rather than waiting around while Williams still has time on his new deal, they opted to re-up now and lock him to the current market price. Reason #3 – share the reward The Cowboys get the 2026 price for a player who is now under team control for the next five years, meaning that relative costs will keep going down. While the team reaps those savings later, Williams is rewarded with a pay raise over his previous deal and more guaranteed money. It’s an early extension, but it’s one of those cases where both sides benefit. Reason #4 – protecting their investment Williams comes as one of the returns from the Micah Parsons trade. Giving up Parsons was incredibly difficult, but the team has secured a high-level player at a huge position of need for half a decade. There’s no longer any uncertainty about whether he’d be sticking around for the long haul. The Cowboys really wanted him, and after having him in the building for eight months, they want him even more. Regardless of how this trade is viewed down the road, the team has assured itself that they’re getting something good out of it. Reason #5 – he’s a sure thing Early or not, locking up a player to a big deal is a huge commitment. The Cowboys went from guaranteeing very little to a lot, which can be risky if things don’t pan out. But Williams doesn’t bring those concerns with him. He’s extremely talented, overpowering blockers with leverage, as he’s never a player who can be neutralized. He’s very durable, never missing more than three games in any season over his seven years in the league. And he comes with no drama. He’s a high-character player who never has any issues, meaning the team stands a great chance to max out their investment. Reason #6 – perfect for the new coach Christian Parker wasn’t a piece of the puzzle when Williams first arrived, but he has to be excited to have such a great player on his defense. The defense as a whole has undergone a massive overhaul, with the recent remodeling of the defensive tackle position being a big part of it. He not only gets a stud player, but he gets a guy gifted enough to offer the versatility that Parker requires out of his big men. He can line up at different spots, shut down the run game, and collapse the pocket from the inside out. Elite talent at defensive tackle is crucial for a Parker defense, so they win in the trenches with fewer guys. Securing Williams for the long term is not only a nice way to preserve the future, but it also shows the team is ready to roll right now in doing what they can to give them a strong roster. Short-term cap relief and bigger savings over time are nice, but the Cowboys are showing they are indeed willing to invest in their big playmakers, even if it’s not always the players we think it is.

title: Horse Tracks: Will Sean Payton outsource replay challenges?
summary: The only real significant rule adjustment this year for officiating is a wrinkle allowing head coaches to designate another staff member to initiate challenges. The idea, I think, is a pretty good one. Head coaches get emotional and sometimes the challenge flies before the prefrontal cortex gets fully engaged after a bad call. Tapping another […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 22: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos throws a challenge flag during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The only real significant rule adjustment this year for officiating is a wrinkle allowing head coaches to designate another staff member to initiate challenges. The idea, I think, is a pretty good one. Head coaches get emotional and sometimes the challenge flies before the prefrontal cortex gets fully engaged after a bad call. Tapping another cooler-headed coach on the shoulder to handle the responsibility seems sound. While Payton isn’t by any stretch of the imagination as emotional as some coaches we’ve seen in Denver (Vic Fangio, anyone?), I honestly wonder if his ego will let him outsource playcalling to Davis Webb and challenges in the same year. I’m not even sold that he needs to or would even want to. As the head coach, he needs to keep his finger on the pulse of the game as a whole. He needs to be not only thinking of the play that happened, but also what the consequences of that challenge will mean for however much time remains in the game. If a designee challenges a play and it fails, that could heavily limit their options later in a close game. I think a guy like Payton would never want to put anyone else in that position. That would be just setting someone up to earn his ire. I’m curious to hear what the community thinks on this. Is Payton pretty decent with challenges in your eyes? Would this move help him or hinder him as our head coach? Hit up the comments and let us know what you think. title: Broncos Owner and CEO Greg Penner says PSLs are “the furthest thing from our minds right now”
summary: PSLs or Personal Seat Licenses are a hot-button topic in Broncos Country right now. First, what exactly are PSLs? They are a one-time fee to secure the exclusive right to purchase season tickets for specific seats. It has become a new trendy thing in the sports landscape recently. The Buffalo Bills are doing PSLs for […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: Chief Executive Officer Greg Penner of the Denver Broncos ownership group looks on before the AFC Championship Game at Empower Field at Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images PSLs or Personal Seat Licenses are a hot-button topic in Broncos Country right now. First, what exactly are PSLs? They are a one-time fee to secure the exclusive right to purchase season tickets for specific seats. It has become a new trendy thing in the sports landscape recently. The Buffalo Bills are doing PSLs for their newly opened Highmark Stadium and reportedly made nearly $260 million dollars Greg Penner said the Broncos haven’t even got to deciding on PSLs yet pic.twitter.com/A5gtL5VMLC — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 11, 2026 The outrage amongst Broncos fans started when Team President Damani Leech was asked at the start of training camp if a decision had been made when it comes to implementing PSLs. Leech noted that most, if not all, new stadiums built in the past 10+ years had them issued and that they are a “pretty likely thing to happen” , but did say no formal decision had been made at that time. “As you know, I think every stadium in the last 10-plus years that’s been built, there have been PSLs issued. So it seems like it’s a pretty likely thing to happen, but we haven’t made any formal decisions on that.” Well, on Tuesday, Denver Broncos Owner and CEO Greg Penner met with the media and was also asked about PSLs. Unlike Leech, who made it sound like a formality, Penner told reporters that PSLs are “the furthest thing from our minds right now” and that they have so many steps before they reach that point. “Really, it’s the furthest thing from our minds right now. We’re so focused on… We’ve had so many steps before that as I just mentioned. It’s still a preferred site but it’s not finalized that we’re going to be in that location. Obviously, that’s where we really want to be. So really, we haven’t even gotten to PSLs yet. Our season ticket holders are vital to our organization and we’re going to keep them informed every step of the way once we get there.” While Penner did avoid the question, it sure does seem like Leech showed the Broncos’ hand a bit there. PSLs are becoming a normal thing in the sports landscape, and as he put it, “It’s a pretty likely thing to happen”, which sucks for Broncos season ticket holders who will need to pay an extra fee just to have the right to purchase season tickets. As for the Broncos’ new stadium, while they continue to make progress on that, Penner told reporters that there’s still a lot of work to do and “We can’t do it by ourselves”. “Yes, we’re making some progress, especially on the things that are really in our control. You all saw the property that we closed on yesterday which was an important step. Really good progress with our architect and also the master plan. This is a process for some of the other steps that we need a lot of collaboration with different groups whether it be the CBA process, Denver Water relocation, city approvals—there’s still a lot of work to do and the 2031 timeline is aggressive. We can’t do it by ourselves. He added they want to have the stadium built and open by the 2031 season, which is an aggressive timeline, and added that they want to keep the Broncos home in Denver. “I don’t know that it’s been more frustrating than I thought. We went into this knowing [that] if you’re going to do a project of this scale, and we knew when we started focusing on this site specifically, that it was going to be more challenging, but we also really want to stay in Denver if we can and deliver a stadium in this market that is a vital part of the downtown. But if you’re doing a project in an area like that, it’s just harder. So I think we went in with our eyes wide open about the challenges, and we’ll keep working through it.” So, as fans, we just need to wait and see how this progresses. It’s going to involve a lot of money being traded hands, purchases, probably lawyers, and compromises by all parties if they want to get this done. It sounds like they’re making progress, but still have a few remaining hurdles before they can reach the finish line. Hopefully, the Broncos can remain in Denver and bring the local fans a brand new stadium and experience they deserve for being one of the best and most loyal fan bases in sports.

summary: Throughout training camp, several players on offense have received a lot of praise and rave reviews. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has impressed early on. full_text: DENVER , CO - DECEMBER 21: Evan Engram (1) of the Denver Broncos walks on the field before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, December 21, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) Throughout training camp, several players on offense have received a lot of praise and rave reviews. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has impressed early on. Additionally, second year wide receiver Pat Bryant continues to make his case to see more playing time. Both figures to play an important role for the offense this year. What we haven’t heard a lot about is the progression of the Broncos’ tight end group. Denver opted to bring back every player from the room last season—a move a lot of fans across Broncos Country weren’t too high on. They also added Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft. It’s unlikely either rookie will make a large impact in their first year in the NFL. Instead, the Broncos are hoping their core group of veterans can take a much-needed leap this season. One of those players is tenth-year pro Evan Engram . Touted as a potential joker for Head Coach Payton’s offense, Engram’s first season in Denver was relatively quiet. To help reach new heights offensively, the Broncos will need more production from Engram in ‘26. Entering his second year with the Broncos, Head Coach Sean Payton believes the longtime veteran is much more comfortable with the offense. And in turn, that feeling will boost his confidence and help him be more of a factor on offense this season. “I think there’s a level of confidence relative to where he’s at and what he’s doing. You could see him play faster with that foundation. I feel that. Then that thing called confidence comes when you’re consistently doing it and I think we’re all seeing that. That’s good,” stated Payton. While he was the third-most targeted player in Denver’s passing game last season, Engram’s production didn’t match the offseason hype. On 76 targets, he reeled in 50 catches for 461 yards and only 1 touchdown. Only nineteen of those catches moved the chains. All some of the lowest marks of his career. Even so, quarterback Bo Nix remains optimistic about Engram’s ability to have a big impact offensively for their upcoming gridiron campaign. Nix praised the longtime veteran’s ability to be a threat in the passing game. Though also acknowledged he has seen more growth and involvement from him as a run blocker. “I think his ability to provide strength in the run game is what’s showing right now. He’s a willing blocker. Last year we used him a little bit more as a vertical pass threat, but I think him getting in the box and blocking is going to open more things up,” stated Nix on what he has seen from Engram to date. The Broncos are a strong five-deep at the wide receiver position. On top of that, second-year running back RJ Harvey figures to be an important part of Denver’s passing plans just like he was as a rookie. Where Engram eventually ends up in their offensive target share remains to be seen, but hopefully, he is able to make more of an impact this season.
author: Christopher Hart
