title: Chiefs News: Defense getting synced up has ‘been a little slow-moving’
summary: The latest The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense features the biggest changes the team made this offseason, with a new offensive coaching staff and a new lead running back. However, there is plenty that is brand new on the Chiefs’ defense as well. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is focused on getting his unit in sync and […]
full_text: Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo helps players run through drills at practice during training camp on July 21, 2024, in St. Joseph, Missouri. (Emily Curiel/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense features the biggest changes the team made this offseason, with a new offensive coaching staff and a new lead running back. However, there is plenty that is brand new on the Chiefs’ defense as well. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is focused on getting his unit in sync and provided an update on how that process is going during his press conference on Tuesday. Steve Spagnuolo admits Chiefs’ new-look defense is moving slower than he’d like | The Kansas City Star Getting everybody in sync is taking a little too long. “It’s not as quickly as I’d like to, to be honest with you,” Spagnuolo said. “It’s been a little slow-moving. And (safety) Alohi Gilman, he’s new. It’s not like you have guys around some of these young corners that have been through it.” Spagnuolo’s unit is set to have at least six new base starters in 2026, including three in the secondary. In years past, mainstays like Trent McDuffie or Bryan Cook might have been around to help teach on the fly. Five Observations from Tuesday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/11 | The Mothership 2. Safety Jaden Hicks had another strong day. Hicks, who made a handful of noteworthy plays during Monday’s practice, was back at it on Tuesday with another impressive performance. Specifically, the third-year safety made a strong pass-breakup on a tight window throw near the sideline during 11-on-11 drills before logging a diving pass-breakup down the field a little bit later. ‘Patrick Mahomes Loves Him’ — Tyrann Mathieu Reveals Chiefs Rookie Who’s Taken Training Camp ‘By Storm’ | Pro Football Sports Network According to Tyrann Mathieu, who played with Mahomes from 2019 to 2021, the quarterback is very happy with what he’s seen from the young receiver so far, and the coaches are also impressed by his practices during camp. “One of our homegrown kids, Cyrus Allen, has taken it by storm. Pat loves him, coaches love him. He was banged up a little bit, so he didn’t really practice while I was there, but me and him had a bunch of conversations, and he asked all the right questions, too”, said Mathieu. Kansas City Chiefs 2026 preview: Kenneth Walker, rookie class bolster rebound bid | Pro Football Focus Reason for pessimism Part of the reason for the Chiefs’ struggles in 2025 was a lack of production at wide receiver. Marquise Brown led the group with just 587 receiving yards, while Rashee Rice’s 77.2 PFF receiving grade was the best among the team’s wide receivers. Xavier Worthy also took a step back from his rookie season, with his PFF receiving grade falling from 71.6 to 66.3 and his yards per route run dropping from 1.51 to 1.25. Rice is expected to be available in Week 1 after missing significant time in each of the past two seasons. His career average of 2.29 yards per route run highlights his status as Kansas City’s most productive wide receiver, but the Chiefs need him to stay on the field in 2026. Retired NFL DL says Patrick Mahomes should sit out the season opener | Chiefs Wire During a recent appearance on CBS Sports HQ, NFL Analyst and former defensive lineman Leger Douzable discussed whether Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes should sit out the first few weeks of the regular season. “I wouldn’t even play him Week One, maybe even Week Two; you sign Justin Fields or trade for Justin Fields to come in to potentially start in the beginning of the season until Patrick Mahomes is truly healthy,” said Douzable. “My thing is, if Mahomes isn’t 100%, I would not risk putting him out there. They just signed him to an extension, so he could be there for, it seems, forever. Why would you risk him?” Chiefs OT Jaylon Moore Is Welcoming the Challenge From Rising Rookie Kahlil Benson | Sports Illustrated Now that Simmons is healthy and in the best shape of his life, the only starting spot available to Moore is on the right side. Although he’s predominantly played left tackle throughout his NFL career — including over 90% of his combined snaps in San Francisco — Moore is more than willing to adjust to a new spot on the offensive line. “Honestly for me, throughout my career, I’ve been back and forth,” Moore said. “It’s good to get the reps on either side because at any point, anything can happen. And it’s good to make sure that every one of our guys are able to play multiple different positions and be able to play wherever your number is called.” Around the NFL Bears safety Coby Bryant to miss 4-6 months after knee surgery | The Athletic The Bears’ prize of free agency, Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million contract in March. In his limited time with the team, he had already impressed the Bears both on and off the field. He made an outstanding interception earlier in camp, while his teammates and coaches have raved about his work habits and leadership. “I love his play style,” defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said last month. “I think it epitomizes the way we want to play the game.” First-round rookie Dillon Thieneman is the other starting safety, and a major plus of having a Super Bowl-winning safety like Bryant was his ability to help Thieneman grow. Now, that challenge will fall to a different player. Vikings name Kyler Murray starting QB over J.J. McCarthy | ESPN The deal includes $101 million guaranteed with $63.35 million guaranteed at signing, according to sources. Williams also received a signing bonus of $31.85 million, a source said. The $35.3 million annual average is the second highest among defensive tackles. Williams, 28, had been signed through 2027 in a four-year extension worth $96 million that guaranteed him $66 million from the New York Jets in 2023. He is now signed through 2030. Chargers OC Mike McDaniel plans to play ‘hot hand’ out of RB group | NFL.com “Bad news, fantasy owners,” McDaniel said via Kris Rhim of ESPN. “Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level. Bad news is I can’t tell you which games those are.” McDaniel spoke glowingly about running back Hampton early in training camp, noting how much the second-year back has grown. Hampton still profiles as the lead running back, with three-down upside, but McDaniel’s comments underscore that there are few true workhorses in the NFL in 2026. title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 12: Steve Spagnuolo talks tackling
summary: The 12th practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place Tuesday morning in St. Joe on a nice day; the sun peeked out through clouds here and there on a cooler-than-typical August day in the Midwest. Fans, players and coaches have lucked out with the weather throughout this year’s time at camp. The team […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Steve Spagnuolo before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 12th practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place Tuesday morning in St. Joe on a nice day; the sun peeked out through clouds here and there on a cooler-than-typical August day in the Midwest. Fans, players and coaches have lucked out with the weather throughout this year’s time at camp. The team released an unofficial depth chart ahead of Saturday’s preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams . Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo smiled through a question about it during his post-practice press conference on Tuesday, revealing the author of the unofficial depth chart: Vice President of Football Communications Brad Gee. “[L’Jarius Sneed has] been in the league for a while; Nohl [Williams] has too,” Spagnuolo said about the lineup. “It’s probably why Brad did it that way.” “Neither LJ nor Delane has really practiced very much, so we’re way down the road on all that,” Spagnuolo elaborated. “Health will be a big issue, continuity, how many reps they’ve had going in, and we’ll see when we get to the first game.” Now that your overreactions to the published depth chart are for naught, let’s go through what we learned from practice on Tuesday: Attendance report Right guard Trey Smith continued to sit out of practice, recovering from a hip injury off to the side. Same goes for linebacker Drue Tranquill (back spasms), cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee), and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (Physically Unable to Perform list). Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (Hamstring) was back in pads at one point last week, but was not on the field and on the sideline during Tuesday’s work. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (Knee) continued to fully participate in practice, along with rookie wideout Cyrus Allen (Shin bruise). Wide receiver Xavier Worthy (Shoulder) was in pads, but did not partake in the contact periods of practice. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane participated further in practice, taking on wide receivers in the one-on-one periods and playing during seven-on-seven periods. In the full-team portions of practice, it still appeared that Delane would be on the sideline and cornerback Melvin Smith Jr. would take his place. Wide receiver Jimmy Holiday, who has worked with the first-team offense due to receiver injuries, left practice early in the front seat of a cart, according to Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com . Spagnuolo is eager to see tackling, getting off blocks in preseason When Spagnuolo was asked about what he is eager to see from his unit in live action on Saturday, he made his priority clear. “Always, the first one is tackling,” Spagnuolo shared. “And that’s probably preceded by what we call block destruction and getting off of blocks.” The defensive coach went on to focus in on Monday’s performance from the defense at camp, wanting more out of the physical points of practice. “Yesterday, I didn’t like the fact that a lot of run plays — and we’re getting a lot more run plays than we used to — a lot of those run plays were going right down the middle of our defense,” Spagnuolo said. “Now we’re not tackling, and it’s not live, but I would like to see us be a little bit more physical, so I’m looking for the physicality, the tackling and the block destruction; those would be the most important things.” With first-round pick Mansoor Delane still donning a yellow, non-contact jersey in practice, there is a lot to learn about him as a player. Spagnuolo wants to ensure the defense’s reputation of having sure-tackling players in the back end continues. “I think we’ve had a secondary, a defensive backfield that has tackled pretty well over the years,” Spagnuolo reflected. “I’d like these new guys to come in and embrace that and be good on the back end, so I’ll be looking for that.” A note on the reserve linebackers With veteran linebacker Drue Tranquill sitting out of practice due to back tightness, there has been more opportunity for others to play the WILL linebacker position next to Nick Bolton in the Chiefs’ starting defense. The two running the role the most are second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa and veteran Jack Cochrane. “With Drue down, some other guys are getting a lot of reps,” Spagnuolo acknowledged. “I like what Jeff has been doing; Jack is a jack of all trades… he plays every spot there, whether we’re in sub or in base.” With Bassa, Spagnuolo believes the experience he has gained so far in the NFL has helped him carve out a role. “It makes a huge difference when you can come here to St. Joe after your second wave of OTAs,” Spagnuolo said. “They feel more comfortable; when they get tired, it isn’t as taxing because you know a little more about the defense.” Other practice notes Check out the live thread from the feed for observations from today’s practice! The Chiefs will presumably be back in pads for Wednesday’s practice, starting at 9:15 a.m. on the grass fields at Missouri Western State. It will likely be the last full-contact session before the team prepares for this weekend’s exhibition at Arrowhead Stadium.

title: Chiefs’ Steve Spagnuolo ‘always had an affection’ for Emmanuel Ogbah
summary: As Kansas City Chiefs training camp practice got going on Tuesday morning, a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter hit the public and revealed who will be taking the one vacant spot on the team’s 90-man offseason roster. Kansas City will reportedly be signing veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah, a former member of the Chiefs during […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 17: Emmanuel Ogbah #90 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts after a play during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos Thursday, Oct. 17, 2019, in Denver. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Kansas City Chiefs training camp practice got going on Tuesday morning, a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter hit the public and revealed who will be taking the one vacant spot on the team’s 90-man offseason roster. Free-agent defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah is signing a one-year deal with the Chiefs; per source. It’s a reunion. Ogbah won a Super Bowl with them in 2020. pic.twitter.com/hZp0zQePeh — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 11, 2026 Kansas City will reportedly be signing veteran defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah, a former member of the Chiefs during the 2019 season. That was his fourth year in the league; the 32-year-old is now entering his 11th season with 48 career sacks to his name. The reunion has been a long time coming; defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo revealed his affinity for Ogbah during a post-practice press conference on Tuesday. “I always had an affection for E,” Spagnuolo said. “It was disappointing, the one year we had him in 2019, I thought he was really coming on, then he got hurt so we didn’t have him at the end of the year.” In his lone season with the Chiefs, Ogbah started four games — including the last three he appeared in before tearing his pectoral and being placed on the Reserve/Injured list. He earned 5.5 sacks in 10 games. In the years since, Ogbah has primarily played with the Miami Dolphins , but most recently spent a season with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025. He played in 13 games, starting three of them but only earning half a sack. In 2024, he was a 16-game starter in Miami, racking up the second-most tackles in his career (49) with five sacks and nine quarterback hits. “I’ve always been periodically in touch with him,” Spanguolo revealed. “If he is a part of our group, I’ll be excited about that.” Ogbah projects to slide in as a reserve defensive end, supplying veteran depth behind the young, inexperienced players currently in the starting lineup. Fourth-year player Felix Anudike-Uzomah is likely the most threatened for playing time, although second-year lineman Ashton Gillotte has been out of practice with a hamstring for over a week.

title: Now healthy, Chiefs tight end Jake Briningstool is ready to compete
summary: Immediately after the 2025 NFL Draft, the Kansas City Chiefs agreed to terms with former Clemson tight end Jake Briningstool as an undrafted free agent. Briningstool reportedly secured $264,000 in guaranteed money. After making some waves in the early portion of camp — including a few crucial plays with the team’s starters — Briningstool suffered […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 08: Jake Briningstool #88 of the Kansas City Chiefs on set during a production shoot at The University of Kansas Health System Training Complex on June 08, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Immediately after the 2025 NFL Draft, the Kansas City Chiefs agreed to terms with former Clemson tight end Jake Briningstool as an undrafted free agent. Briningstool reportedly secured $264,000 in guaranteed money. After making some waves in the early portion of camp — including a few crucial plays with the team’s starters — Briningstool suffered a hamstring injury that ended his summer early, and he was placed on the Reserve/Injured list at the final cutdown date. Although the Chiefs used a return designation to keep Briningstool’s rookie season technically alive, he did not appear in a game in 2025. A year later, he seems to again be climbing the team’s depth chart in his second training camp at Missouri Western State University. Good hands by Briningstool against Conner 1 on 1 pic.twitter.com/g7gy15KkzG — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 10, 2026 He has already gotten further in the process than he did as a rookie. “It feels great to be able to be out here and compete,” Briningstool said after Monday’s practice, “and actually put the pads on. Last year, I got hurt before we even put the pads on. Just being able to come out here and learn a lot from the other guys and be able to showcase what I can do — it’s been great. I’ve been excited to be back out here.” Although he was not able to see the field last season, the learning went on for Briningstool. “Last year for me,” he continued, “as frustrating as it was, I think it was a way God showed me just to be able to take a step back and do what it takes to be a pro. I think just being able to take a back seat and watch the guys in front of me and be able to just watch how they attack every single day, the stuff that they do off the field and how it translates onto the field. So, I think I really had an up-close view to be able to see that, and I can be able to translate that into my own way and use it for myself.” That included a close-up view of arguably the best to ever practice Briningstool’s craft. “Travis Kelce,” he remarked, “just being able to be so close to him, the Hall of Fame career that he’s had, it’s been a blessing for me to watch him, study him, and just be able to play alongside him.” Briningstool will finally get a chance to play in front of Chiefs fans on Saturday in the preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams . He expects a strong performance from the entire tight ends room. “I think the biggest thing is we’ve had a super competitive camp,” he observed. “Guys have been working hard. I think we have a talented team, so we’re just excited to go out there and showcase what we’ve been working on. I’m looking forward to it, and I know all the other guys are too. We’re excited for Saturday.”

title: Chiefs Mailbag: Answering your questions after two weeks of camp
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! More than half of the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University is now in the rearview. Let’s see what is on readers’ minds before the Chiefs take […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Josh Thompson #62, Pete Nygra #50 and Kahlil Benson #70 walk toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! More than half of the team’s training camp at Missouri Western State University is now in the rearview. Let’s see what is on readers’ minds before the Chiefs take the field for their first preseason contest on Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams . saintschiefsfan asks: Right tackle Kahlil Benson. I have massive questions about him. Are we really going to trust a tryout rookie to protect the franchise? Aside from quarterback Patrick Mahomes health, this is by far the biggest story in camp. Benson’s run with the starters at now two positions has been the most surprising development in camp. We also need to keep in mind that it is still early in the process to say that Benson has earned the team’s trust. I see the work he has gotten in camp as a ramp-up for a long look in the preseason, likely at both right tackle and right guard. I expect Benson to play a heavy snap count in all three exhibitions. It also is not hyperbole to say no individual Chiefs player has more riding on the preseason than Benson. When he goes against starters, he needs to hold his own and look like he belongs. When matched up against other teams’ deep depth, Benson needs to dominate. He has been a great story, and the Chiefs clearly want to give him a chance to earn a starting nod. However, I do not expect Benson to have a long leash if he looks overwhelmed in the preseason. He may very well open Week 1 at right tackle — or work his way out of consideration very quickly. Andyreidsmustache_ asks: Has Garrett Nussmeier shown any signs he could challenge Justin Fields for the QB2 position? By most accounts, Nussmeier has performed well in camp and shown strong improvement from what beat reporters saw from him in the offseason program. However, virtually every reported highlight still has the rookie throwing to the team’s deep depth skill players. There are no signs that the Chiefs are thinking of Nussmeier supplanting Fields as Patrick Mahomes’ primary backup. Nussmeier should get plenty of opportunities to play in the preseason, but I don’t think there’s anything he could realistically do to move ahead of Fields on the depth chart. Nussmeier’s primary goal is to play well enough to scare the Chiefs into thinking he could be claimed on waivers if they try to sneak him onto the practice squad. Strong play in the three-game exhibition slate (paired with showing his smarts in the film room) would give Nussmeier a good chance to be the Chiefs’ primary backup passer in 2027. With backup quarterbacks commanding salaries exceeding $5 million, a cost-controlled option on the bench would be valuable. kcabogado asks: What’s the level of concern regarding cornerback Mansoor Delane’s injury? Will he be available to play and when? And overall, based on camp performance so far, how much of an impact are we expecting from rookie pass rusher R Mason Thomas this year? I don’t think you can put the concern level on Delane at zero, but there have been some promising signs. In Monday’s practice, Delane participated in pads for the first time in 7-on-7 action (while still wearing a yellow non-contact jersey). General manager Brett Veach seemed optimistic about Delane’s full participation in the near future later Monday in an interview on Sirius XM . Veach also confirmed that the rookie injured his shoulder blade. Pretty exciting update from Brett Veach on Mansoor Delane today on Sirius XM: "With Mansoor, he had a shoulder blade injury right towards the end of OTA’s. We don’t think it’s going to be long term or anything but that has to just completely heal. But there’s nothing limiting… — HBTC (@hbtCHIEFS) August 10, 2026 Arrowhead Pride ’s Caleb James had some good notes about Thomas after visiting camp this week. For his rookie season, we are going to have to judge whether Thomas is seeing the field in obvious passing situations rather than the raw number of snaps played. It will be hard to justify playing Thomas over better fits in run defense in many first- and second-down situations. The player Thomas is most compared to is Nik Bonitto of the Denver Broncos . Bonitto has never had a season snap count higher than 61%. RoyalsFanBill asks: Who are the 3 TEs the Chiefs start the year with. I suspect that Travis Kelce guy is safe. Beyond that, preseason action will be very important for the position. We know that Mahomes is probably going to have a light workload (if any) in the preseason. I don’t expect to see much of Kelce either until the games matter. I have a hard time seeing the Chiefs moving on from veteran Noah Gray given the inexperience in the rest of the room. That said, Gray had a brutal 2025 season, and some reports from camp have not been encouraging. With the Chiefs tight against the salary cap entering the season, Gray’s non-guaranteed $4.7 million base salary is one of the few realistic moves to open spending room. Gray will likely play with whichever starters suit up on Saturday. The order behind him among Jared Wiley, Jake Briningstool and Trey Watson is one of the most important things to watch. Prime opportunities for a similar player in Briningstool could be interpreted as bad news for Gray. I am not sure if the Chiefs will keep three or four tight ends on the opening 53, but the in-house options probably are competing with players on other teams as much as with each other. With the Chiefs having their highest waivers priority since 2013, I will also not be surprised if Veach does some late shopping at the position. PettyMahomes asks: Is wide receiver Cyrus Allen going to be a good Rashee Rice replacement for 2027? Allen and Rice probably both will always be best when lined up in the slot, but they are very different players. We have already had a major injury scare with Allen. His listed 5-11 and 183-pound frame is never going to be well suited for the yards-after-the-catch role that Rice has feasted on when available. Mahomes has appeared to have a connection with Allen, who is probably already a better pure route runner than Rice will ever be. I compared Allen to Emmanuel Sanders after the draft, and we have already seen reports that the Chiefs see similarities to now Washington Commanders wideout Stefon Diggs (also a one-time fifth-round selection). I don’t know that former Chiefs second-round pick Skyy Moore ever would have developed into a serviceable NFL player, but Kansas City’s coaches did him no favors early in his career. They instantly ignored the route running he showed at Western Michigan and tried to force return-game work on him while hoping for a Tyreek Hill clone. The team seems to have learned a lesson and is allowing Allen to simply be himself. The sample size is small, and health is always a wild card. But Allen shows definite signs that he could be in the starting lineup at some point this season — and enter 2027 as a surefire starter. Uberdirt asks: Is rookie running back Emmitt Johnson pushing Kenneth Walker for playing time? And is Andy Reid going to actually call more running plays? If the Chiefs aren’t going to call more run plays, they have wasted their time at training camp with the number of ways they have practiced using the revamped running back room. The Chiefs didn’t sign Walker to essentially leave a sports car parked in the garage. He is going to be heavily involved in the offense both as a runner and a pass catcher. Whether Johnson is a major part of a new focus on the run game remains to be seen. At camp, second-year man Brashard Smith has widely been reported to be Walker’s immediate backup and…

title: Chiefs News: Nick Bolton draws from Tyrann Mathieu for leadership
summary: The latest The 2021 season for the Kansas City Chiefs was the final year of safety Tyrann Mathieu’s run with the team. It was also the rookie year for linebacker Nick Bolton. The second-round pick from Missouri was just a part-time playmaker for the defense that year before ascending to the full-time middle linebacker position […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 30: Linebacker Nick Bolton #54 and safety Tyrann Mathieu #32 of the Kansas City Chiefs get set on defense, during training camp at Missouri Western State University on July 30, 2021 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Peter G. Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest The 2021 season for the Kansas City Chiefs was the final year of safety Tyrann Mathieu’s run with the team. It was also the rookie year for linebacker Nick Bolton. The second-round pick from Missouri was just a part-time playmaker for the defense that year before ascending to the full-time middle linebacker position in 2022. Now a pillar of the unit that Mathieu was when he first arrived in the league, Bolton draws from that year together to lead his young teammates. Nick Bolton hopes to elevate his leadership with lessons from Tyrann Mathieu | The Kansas City Star When mentoring second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa, Bolton relayed a message that the “Honey Badger” gave him as a rookie. “You have to take advantage of every opportunity you get,” Bolton said. “You can’t count how many you’re going to get, but every one that you do get, make it count. “Tyrann gave me that same message when I was a rookie. He’s the original 32. I’m just trying to wear it how he wore it.” Five Observations from Monday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/10 | The Mothership 4. Safety Jaden Hicks had a memorable practice. Hicks was a defensive standout on Monday with multiple impact plays, which included an interception over the middle during a 7-on-7 period and a diving pass-breakup amidst 11-on-11 red zone drills. The third-year safety has a major opportunity in front of him with former safety Bryan Cook no longer on the team, and at least so far, Hicks appears to be off to a strong start. First Look: Rams open 2026 preseason taking on Chiefs in Kansas City | The Rams McVay last Saturday said rookie quarterback Ty Simpson “definitely will” play in the preseason opener, but he hasn’t decided whether fourth-year quarterback Stetson Bennett IV will. Early in training camp, McVay said CJ Daniels was one of the players he was excited to see as training camp practices and the preseason progressed. Cornerback Cam Lampkin has had a strong camp so far. Isiah Pacheco’s latest injury is unfortunate reminder for Chiefs fans | Arrowhead Addict 3. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes made a handful of classic throws. Mahomes showed off a handful of the off-balance throws for which he’s synonymous on Saturday, firing a pair of near identical passes across his body while on the run to a receiver in the middle of the field. Mahomes found Andrew Armstrong on the first instance, followed by a throw to Nikko Remigio a little bit later. The three-time Super Bowl MVP, who has participated in every 11-on-11 segment of training camp so far, spoke following practice about his progress as he continues to work his way back from last season’s knee injury. NFL Host reveals a disappointing Kansas City Chiefs player on offense | Chiefs Wire “It’s a simple question because everybody’s wondering about the Kansas City Chiefs offense: can they be explosive or not? Once again, we just talked about the run game. Can they have that explosive passing game again? It all depends on if they can trust and count on Rashee Rice,” said Eisen. Kansas City Chiefs Day 11 Training Camp Takeaways: Mansoor Delane takes a step forward, Bieniemy returns, Cyrus Allen has ‘it’ | A to Z Sports There are two things that stand out most to me when watching Allen work. First, he seems to have that feel for finding open space on the field that’s so successful when paired with a quarterback like Mahomes. It was demonstrated in this 7-on-7 drill, where he found open space behind LBs Nick Bolton and Jack Cochrane in the corner of the end zone. The second thing that stands out to me is that he works back to the football. He’s not always just waiting for the ball to arrive in a specific spot. He’s working to ensure that he makes the reception or draws a penalty flag. Around the NFL Christian McCaffrey sits out practice with ‘tightness,’ 49ers not concerned | The Athletic Star running back Christian McCaffrey joined a host of San Francisco 49ers teammates on the sideline at Monday’s practice, missing his first session of training camp with what the team called “tightness.” The 49ers declined to specify where McCaffrey is experiencing the tightness, but offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said after practice that the team is not concerned about the injury. “No, just managing,” Kubiak said. “A little sore, but he’s doing fine, so we’re just managing him as we go.” Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal | ESPN The deal includes $101 million guaranteed with $63.35 million guaranteed at signing, according to sources. Williams also received a signing bonus of $31.85 million, a source said. The $35.3 million annual average is the second highest among defensive tackles. Williams, 28, had been signed through 2027 in a four-year extension worth $96 million that guaranteed him $66 million from the New York Jets in 2023. He is now signed through 2030. Colts QB Anthony Richardson ‘not necessarily sure what’s going on with’ offseason trade request | NFL.com “I haven’t really talked to my agent about that recently, I haven’t really talked to anyone about that recently, so I’m not necessarily sure what’s going on with that,” he said this past weekend, via the Indy Star. Reports out of Indianapolis training camp don’t bode well for Richardson’s prospects of winning the backup job behind starter Daniel Jones. Head coach Shane Steichen said Sunday that Richardson and Riley Leonard would split snaps in Thursday’s preseason kickoff against the New England Patriots, but who will start the game has not yet been decided. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Andy Reid talks injuries, Bieniemy’s return after Monday’s Chiefs practice Reid said it was good to have his long-time assistant coach back on the field, for many different reasons. “He’s back in the fold, and I don’t think he missed a step,” Reid said. “He was out there getting after it, and that’s a positive for the offensive side.” “I talked to him several times a day, so I knew he was coming back if everything worked out the way it had been,” Reid revealed. “The primary thing is that Mia’s stable and in good hands; she’s doing well, so that was the primary thing,” Reid emphasized. “That’s where we stand with it.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list 90.9 The Bridge on X: Follow @909thebridge

Left tackle Rashawn Slater missed practice for the third consecutive day on Monday, despite Jim Harbaugh telling reporters that he was “right on track” returning from his torn patellar tendon. title: This could be the Chargers’ biggest strength
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers will look different on defense this season after defensive coordinator Jesse Minter became the head coach of the Baltimore Ravens. Chris O’Leary has taken the reins, where he will now inherit a defense that looks a bit different in the front seven. However, the changes could result in building the Chargers’ […]
full_text: EL SEGUNDO, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Ahkeem Mesidor #90 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs a pad drill during the Los Angeles Chargers Training Camp at The Bolt on July 30, 2026 in El Segundo, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers will look different on defense this season after defensive coordinator Jesse Minter became the head coach of the Baltimore Ravens. Chris O’Leary has taken the reins, where he will now inherit a defense that looks a bit different in the front seven. However, the changes could result in building the Chargers’ best position group. “The offseason didn’t bring any sweeping changes for the Chargers defense. Dalvin Tomlinson, 32, was their most notable signing to bulk up the interior, and they lost a few pass rushers, Odafe Oweh and Da’Shawn Hand, but largely maintained the status quo. Los Angeles did, however, spend a first-round pick on Akheem Mesidor, the ACC sack leader in 2025 with 12.5,” NFL.com contributor Bobby Kownack wrote. “There’s enough pass-rushing depth that Mesidor won’t have to take on too much too soon. More importantly, he has some stellar mentors in Tuli Tuipulotu, who was sixth in the NFL last season with 13 sacks, and nine-time Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. The hope is for a seamless transition from Mack to Mesidor alongside Tuipulotu as the leaders of the L.A. edge rush.” Mesidor has been one of the best players in training camp so far, which is a great sign of what’s to come. The Chargers expect the first-round pick out of Miami to start right away and be one of the team’s top pass rushers. If Mesidor can warrant attention from opposing offensive lines, it could also open things up for Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack, freeing them up from more attention so they can get after opposing quarterbacks with ease. BFTB community, how do you feel about Mesidor’s start in training camp? Let us know in the comments section below.

title: Sleeper starting candidate for each position battle during Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp
summary: Inspired by the early buzz surrounding rookie Hezekiah Masses coming out of Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp, let’s take a look at a few sleeper candidates who could climb up the Raiders’ depth chart and win a starting job at each of the team’s position battles. QB: Aidan O’Connell To be honest, O’Connell is a […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 20: Malik Benson #19 of the Las Vegas Raiders practices during an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inspired by the early buzz surrounding rookie Hezekiah Masses coming out of Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp, let’s take a look at a few sleeper candidates who could climb up the Raiders’ depth chart and win a starting job at each of the team’s position battles. QB: Aidan O’Connell To be honest, O’Connell is a lot more likely to start for another team than he is in Las Vegas. The team’s “position battle” at quarterback is really centered more around when the coaching staff feels Fernando Mendoza is ready for NFL action, rather than a true competition between Mendoza and Kirk Cousins. So, even if O’Connell is sharp this summer, that probably just makes him more likely to get traded. But, by process of elimination in this exercise, there is a sliver of hope that he could be behind center against the Miami Dolphins. WR: Malik Benson The Silver and Black have a wide-open competition for their third wide receiver spot, with second-year pros Jack Bech and Dont’e Thornton Jr. being the early favorites. But those two shouldn’t be very far ahead of the rest of the depth chart, leaving the door open for Benson. The sixth-round pick also fits Klint Kubiak’s profile at the position , sacrificing size for the versatility to line up in the slot or on the boundary and the potential to make an impact at every level of the passing game. The biggest question is if Kubiak would want something different with the offense’s WR3 spot, since Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Benson have similar skill sets. G: Jordan Meredith Listing Meredith feels like cheating since he’s started 19 games over the last couple of years in Las Vegas. However, the early favorites to land the two starting guard spots in 2026 seem to be Spencer Burford, Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers, pushing the two-year starter into the “sleeper” category. If the young guys aren’t getting the job done in camp, Meredith’s experience could give him an edge, seeing as the organization likely doesn’t want to take chances when it comes to protecting Mendoza. RT: Trey Zuhn III Zuhn could easily be listed in the section above, as his versatility combined with the Raiders’ need for improved offensive line play leads to a few avenues for him to crack the starting lineup. The rookie will probably get more reps at guard this summer since both of those first-string roles are up for grabs, but don’t sleep on him being in the mix at right tackle alongside DJ Glaze and Charles Grant. The Texas A&M product was one of the best pass protectors in College Football last year to potentially provide some extra Mendoza insurance. That being said, Zuhn would have to prove that he can overcome a lack of length to hold down the edge and be up to par as a run-blocker. DT: Tonka Hemingway Like the majority of positions mentioned here, defensive tackle is anyone’s game in Las Vegas. The biggest competition or question mark is at nose tackle (assuming the switch to a 3-4 base scheme), but it’s not as if Thomas Booker IV, Jonah Laulu and Adam Butler are game-changers on the interior defensive line. While Hemingway isn’t an option at nose, he doesn’t have the size and strength for the position, but he has been the biggest standout among the defensive tackles so far in training camp. The South Carolina product has the athleticism and pass-rush skills to generate interior pressure, and the work he did in the weight room this offseason has caught the coaching staff’s eye to potentially become a more complete player. CB: Hezekiah Masses As mentioned above, Masses is one of the early winners in training camp. While the expectation was that second-year pro Darien Porter and rookie Jermod McCoy would duke it out for the second starting cornerback spot this summer, Masses has thrown his name into the mix. He was a standout during OTAs and minicamp, earning some first-team reps during the spring, and that carried over into the Raiders’ first training camp practice. The Cal product isn’t particularly sticky in coverage, but he led ACC cornerbacks with five interceptions last season, and Las Vegas’ secondary could use someone who can create turnovers. FS: Dalton Johnson Free safety is a tough position to predict because the Silver and Black don’t have a clear deep defender on the roster. Fellow rookie and former Arizona Wildcat Treydan Stukes seems to be the early favorite and profiles as someone who could take over that spot , but Stukes primarily lined up at nickelback in college and Johnson actually had more career snaps at free safety ( 362 versus 39 , per Pro Football Focus ). So, there is a world where Stukes takes the nickel spot from Taron Johnson, and the other former Wildcat defensive back lines up on the backend of the defense this season.

title: Las Vegas Raiders Summer Scouting: ILB Rankings
summary: I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2024; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns running back Jaydon Blue (23) and Clemson Tigers linebacker Sammy Brown (47) in action during the game between the Texas Longhorns and the Clemson Tigers in the CFP National Playoff First Round at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | Jerome Miron-Imagn Images I broke down the 2027 scouting classes in my early summer scouting series, and the room has a ton of potential with a long list of potential standout players. I broke down the offense and defense in articles and I suggest reading those for a broad aspect of the room. The Raiders do have some talent on the interior OL, and I’d expect Las Vegas to add more in 2027 as John Spytek does. Las Vegas will likely be looking to add another linebacker in the 2027 draft after taking Tommy Eichenebrg and Cody Lindenberg in the 2024 and 25 classes. Both are quality depth and elite special teams players, but the Raiders do lack linebacker depth after Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean, with Dean being injury prone. Las Vegas will look to run 1-2 linebacker sets, and that limits their needs for a third backer, but the 2027 class focuses on a ton of depth, and Las Vegas can afford to keep adding talent to a position that’s seeing a rise in talent. These rankings are extremely early, and they will evolve over not only the summer but the next 8-10 months throughout the season, and into draft season. Some lists will feature 10, 15, 20, or more ranked prospects but I’ll include others on the list below to note. Kyngston Viliamu-Asa, Notre Dame – 6’3/230, R-So The “anchor” of the Notre Dame defense, Viliamu-Asa is recovering from a torn ACL in late 2025, and if he’s healthy off the injury his 2026 season could be the one to skyrocket him into the top of the class fully. Viliamu-Asa is coming off a 2025 with 50 tackles, 8 TFL, and 3 sacks while adding an interception, 5 PBU, and 2 FF. An elite athlete, Viliamu-Asa is learning as a pass defense linebacker, but he’s an exceptional forward moving linebacker. The sophomore takes phenomenal run angles, fires downhill quickly, and his agility is elite. Viliamu-Asa plays physical, has a great frame, and he’s able to work off blocks well, with an ability to take down runners with ease having a sub 8% missed tackle rate in his career. Viliamu-Asa is an exceptional athlete, his hips are fluid, and he does a good job with his first and second steps able to turn and run with tight ends, slot receivers, and covers the ground well in zone. Notre Dame has produced good linebackers in recent years, and KVA should follow. Sammy Brown, Clemson – 6’2/240, Jr A former top recruit, Brown has followed his high school film up with two strong seasons at Clemson with a career 186 tackles, 25 TFL, and 10 sacks with another 8 PBU, an INT, and forced fumble. Brown is stout, he’s physical, aggressive, smart, and pretty much every other trait you want in a linebacker. Brown has elite play recognition, he fires on the ball, and shows an incredible first step trigger with good long speed as well to play sideline to sideline. Brown is strong, he’s able to work off defenders, stay consistent in coverage with good physicality, and also tackles exceptionally well, though there’s some inconsistent angles or over pursuit as well due to his aggression. I’d also like to see him better his game in terms of play action, double moves, and turn down the immediate reaction as he’s athletic enough to take a second to react instead of try to be proactive 100% of the time. A freak athlete, Brown pairs that with intelligence, and if he can find consistency there’s a super high ceiling. Ben Roberts, Texas Tech – 6’3/25, R-Jr The Red Raiders lost standout linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, and likely improved at the position. While Roberts may not have the turnover production of Rodriguez, he’s an exceptional player as well. Roberts has a career 280 tackles, 15 TFL, and 5 interceptions with another 6 PBU and 7 FF in 42 games, and he’s a physical defender. Roberts is massive, and he’s strong. A good coverage defender as well, Roberts has fluid hips, good foot speed, and he diagnoses passing lanes well to get in front of the ball and make a big play. I do have some concerns at times with his long speed, not showing an ability to match with quicker receivers that can gain a step, and he also needs to do better with his hands to work off defenders. The Junior is extremely smart, understands both phases of the game, and stepping into the MIKE role will do a ton for his stock, good or bad. Rasheem Biles, Texas – 6’1/220, Jr Biles is a freak of nature and should be an impactful player for Texas. The former Pitt standout has 185 tackles, 32 TFL, and 10 sacks in his career with another 3 interceptions, 15 PBU, and 3 FF with 5 defensive touchdowns. I can knock Biles for his length issues only so much, and it might limit him in the SEC which will push him down. That said, Biles is an elite athlete, he’s a ball of lightning and he uses his speed/athleticism to his advantage to play a big nickel type role similar to previous Pitt linebacker Kyle Louis. Biles triggers to the ball well, has great hip and lower body flexibility, and he moves similar to a safety. Biles does struggle at times vs bigger tight ends and he can be pushed around in the box as well at times. There’s a ton of potential in diverse systems, similar to the Raiders, and if he can succeed in the SEC I’d expect a big year. Cole Sullivan, Oklahoma – 6’3/320, Jr Oklahoma has three linebackers that should all hear their names called in April of 2027 with Sullivan the top name. The former Michigan linebacker, Sullivan has an elite frame and he uses it to his advantage with exceptional length and strength to play both phases. Sullivan is smart, he pairs this with an elite first step, high end trigger, and good lateral agility to work thorugh defenders and slice through blocks. Sullivan has advanced hand combat skills, he shows the ability to have hand combat skills similar to pass rushers, and Sullivan also has elite lower body agility to dip and run the hoop while working through lineman with leverage. He’s a functional blitzer, but does best in coverage with good instincts, length, and an ability to breakdown passing lanes and windows. Sullivan will need to improve his overall tackling, and show more consistency, but the sky is the limit in a system that strains the linebacker. Christian Alliegro, Ohio State – 6’4/245, R-Jr Alliegro is tasked to replace Sonny Styles & Arvell Reese, and the former Wisconsin badger is coming off 53 tackles, 9 TFL, and 4 sacks in 2025. He has an elite size profile, with good length to pair with a ton of athleticism. Alliegro is an exceptional athlete, he fires off the snap, has the best trigger in the class, and Alliegro uses his athleticism to his advantage with good bend, hip flexibility, and twitch to beat lineman as a blitzer/run defender. Alliegro can use his athleticism in the pass game, with fluid hips and an ability to flip and run with defenders while showing an ability to seal passing lanes. He’ll struggle to come away with the ball, losing his angle, or being pushed out at times by tight ends which is surprising at his size. In the run game, I’d like to see Alliegro clean up the tackling, improve his angles consistently, and also limit how aggressive he is where there’s a ton of moments he’ll abandon his gap, over pursuit, or simply be out of position. Alliegro is an athlete, but his inconsistent mental game, though it should improve at Ohio State, could limit his future. title: Raiders depth chart: Decamerion Richardson silently climbing
summary: Ahead of their first preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals, the Las Vegas Raiders released their initial depth chart for the 2026 NFL season. Typically, there isn’t much to glean since coaches don’t want to show their hand before the regular-season opener. However, the Raiders have several position battles during training camp, and there were […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - MAY 20: Dareke Young #81 and Decamerion Richardson #25 of the Las Vegas Raiders practice during an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on May 20, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of their first preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals, the Las Vegas Raiders released their initial depth chart for the 2026 NFL season. Typically, there isn’t much to glean since coaches don’t want to show their hand before the regular-season opener. However, the Raiders have several position battles during training camp , and there were a handful of surprises on the two-deep that can provide some insight or takeaways on how those competitions are playing out. Raiders unofficial depth chart ahead of Thursday's preseason opener. pic.twitter.com/j3vGxE7PqA — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) August 11, 2026 Richardson over McCoy When it comes to Las Vegas’ cornerback situation, most of the attention has been on Hezekiah Masses’ rise to compete with Darien Porter for a starting spot , with Masses leapfrogging fellow rookie Jermod McCoy on the depth chart. That was confirmed with the fifth-rounder getting the second-string spot behind Porter. But there was a surprise at the position because McCoy isn’t the other backup corner; Decamerion Richardson is. It seems like Richardson has quietly been having a good camp, and there have been reports about him getting some run with the starting defense. Albeit, those notes are typically buried at the bottom of camp reports because the battle between Porter and Masses has been drawing the most attention. Regardless, the third-year pro has made a strong enough impression on the coaching staff to currently be ahead of McCoy, who is very talented but has been on a pitch count while recovering from the torn ACL that caused him to miss all of last season at Tennessee. Between Eric Stokes, Porter, Masses, Richardson and McCoy, the Raiders have a problem on the perimeter of the defense, but it’s a good problem to have! There’s a lot of young talent that seems to be rising during training camp, but the math might not work out to be able to keep all of them on the 53-man roster. If all of them play well during the preseason, then maybe there’s an opportunity to swing a trade and address another position. Hemingway Starting Heading into camp, it looked like Thomas Booker IV and Jonah Laulu would be the starting defensive tackles since those two were the primary starters last year. However, neither is a first-stringer on the initial depth chart, with Adam Butler and Tonka Hemingway sitting at the top. Butler isn’t surprising since he’s the most experienced player at the position, but Hemingway is a little eyebrow-raising. The South Carolina product only played in nine games with zero starts and 195 defensive snaps, per Pro Football Reference , as a rookie last season. However, anyone who has been paying attention to training camp knows that he’s been one of the most improved players on the roster. So, this just confirmed the reports and speaks highly to the work he put in during the offseason. Bech over Benson Malik Benson has been another rising star early in camp, as he’s been forming a strong connection with Fernando Mendoza and received first-team reps when Jalen Nailor was held out of practice. Meanwhile, Jack Bech had a quiet start to the summer but has reportedly been making more plays recently. It’s still early, so Bech can’t get too comfortable. But he does have the upper hand at becoming the third wide receiver in 11 personnel. For those curious/also within the wide receiver room, Dont’e Thornton Jr. is also listed with the second-team offense right now. Zuhn (backup) Right Tackle Part of the reason John Spytek used a third-round pick on Trey Zuhn III is the offensive lineman’s position versatility. He played both left tackle and center in college, and was considered a candidate to switch to guard as a pro prospect. On top of that, the Raiders’ coaching staff was moving the Texas A&M product around during the spring and training camp, seemingly playing a different position every day. So, the fact Zuhn was listed as a right tackle is interesting for a few reasons. That likely means he’s competing with DJ Glaze for a starting spot rather than factoring into the mix for the battle at guard. It’s also worth noting that Glaze had an up-and-down start to camp, and Zuhn didn’t take his first snaps at right tackle until about a week or so into practices this summer. Additionally, this is a strong sign that Charles Grant, who was viewed as a potential contender to push Glaze, isn’t a significant competitor or is at least viewed as the third option on the right edge. Grant was listed as the backup left tackle behind Kolton Miller and hasn’t gotten much, if any, run on the other side of the line based on the training camp reports. Stukes Free Safety Another rookie whose best position was in question after getting drafted, Stukes was primarily a nickelback at Arizona. However, after trading for Taron Johnson, the Raiders needed more help at free safety this offseason. That led to some questions about where the former Wildcat would line up, and the initial depth chart has him slotted behind Isaiah Pola-Mao at free safety. So, another takeaway here is that Stukes is still listed as a backup, which was a hot topic of discussion during the first week of camp. However, he’s been working with first-team defense more recently, rotating on the backend of the defense with Pola-Mao. In other words, that competition is still alive, and we got some clarity on what the plan is for the second-round pick. Nickelback Clarity On that note, there was some talk about Johnson playing safety, and it could still be the case that he’s going to take on a versatile role for the Silver and Black this season. However, he was listed as the starting slot corner, which, along with Stukes being slotted as a safety, confirms that the veteran is the team’s primary nickelback right now. Also, don’t sleep on Greedy Vance making the team. He’s had a couple of interceptions off Mendoza to make a name for himself, and the 2025 undrafted free agent is right behind Johnson on the two-deep. That’s another young corner/defensive back who could alter the math when it comes to cutdown day. Specialists’ Standing The only real surprise among the specialists was seeing Alex Ward listed ahead of Tyler Duzansky on the depth chart. According to The Athletic’s Sam Warren , Duzansky began camp as the first-team long snapper, but that appears to have flipped over the last couple of weeks and is something to keep an eye on during the preseason. (This is me sending out the bat signal for you, Ray…). Also, the first depth chart confirmed that Matt Gay is ahead of Kansei Matsuzawa in the kicker competition. Baring a change, it seems like the Raiders are going to take advantage of Matsuzawa being eligible for the IPP exemption on the practice squad.

The Dolphins made the trade to avoid Wallace hitting the waiver wire, and now he will have a chance to jump start his career in Miami. full_text: John Madden is the person most often credited with this old football truism: When you have two starting quarterbacks, you really have no starting quarterbacks. Right now, as we all know, the Minnesota Vikings are marinating in that reality. Time is running out for Kevin O’Connell to make a decision between J.J. McCarthy and Kyler Murray when it comes to who will take snaps for his team in the 2026 season. Right now, you could ask 10 people who’s winning the battle, and you might get five people on each side. I’m highly interested in how well Murray’s predilection for off-schedule plays will mix with O’Connell’s passing game , which is high art and science at its best, while McCarthy has left me a bit cold outside of the occasional splash play. But that’s just me. Regardless of who wins this battle, the Vikings have some things to figure out. After 2024’s 14-3 regular-season record and a wild-card demolition at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams, the franchise saw the best and the worst that Sam Darnold had to offer, and let Darnold walk. While Darnold was busy on a Super Bowl campaign with the Seattle Seahawks, the Vikings were left with McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer, and the 9-8 record one would expect from that particular group. Brian Flores’ defense was its usual wrecking ball, ranking third in DVOA , while O’Connell’s offense dropped all the way down to 29th , from 15th the year before. Back in January, O’Connell talked about the disappointment that comes with a season that ends without a postseason opportunity. “Getting a chance to watch a lot of the football this past weekend – as we thought it would – it definitely stung to not be a part of it,“ he said. ”But what we’ve got to understand is we didn’t do enough to get into the playoffs, and that’s something that is not going to be acceptable for me or our team or our organization in any year. Going into it the way that we always try to do, which is to give ourselves an opportunity to win a championship and bring our great fan base and our ownership a championship. “Improvement starts with me. Have already started that process of going through, layer by layer, every aspect of doing my job. Our coaching staff, and what we do schematically, how we prepare our team, how we build our offseason, how we build our training camp, to try to make sure that we’re the best possible team in 2026 that that we can be.“ Obviously, Point 1 when it comes to a brighter future for these Vikings is finding the one guy who can perform consistently under center. Beyond that, though, it’s crucial for everybody on the roster to bring their best, and that’s just as true of the lesser-known players as it is for the stars. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems on the 2026 Vikings roster — one underrated veteran, one underrated free-agent acquisition, and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: RB Jordan Mason When the Vikings signed former San Francisco 49ers running back Jordan Mason to a two-year, $10.5 million contract with $7.23 million guaranteed before the 2025 season, O’Connell seemed to think that he may have had the NFL’s next great thunder and lightning duo in Mason and Aaron Jones, and that he could make things really interesting by putting both guys on the field together. “Maybe we activate some two-back groupings where we’ve got Jordan and Aaron in the game at the same time,” O’Connell said in 2025 as training camp started . “There’s a lot of things schematically that we’re going to try, and then as we get toward the season, what gives us advantages? What allows us to play the most multiple way that all circles back to the number one question of, ‘What makes the quarterback’s job easier, and [is] more likely to be quarterback friendly to apply to our whole system?’” In the end, this didn’t quite work out as expected. Per Pro Football Focus, Jones and Mason were on the field at the same time last season for exactly four plays. There was a 1-yard Jones run against the Chicago Bears in Week 1, an 11-yard J.J McCarthy scramble in that same game, a Leonard Floyd sack of McCarthy in Week 2 against the Atlanta Falcons, and a 31-yard Jones run against the Detroit Lions in Week 9. Jones played just 12 games last season due to injuries, and it was Mason who really stood out in the end. In his first year with the Vikings, the 5’11”, 223-pound Mason ran the ball 159 times for 758 yards (4.8 yards per carry), six touchdowns, 31 forced missed tackles, and 22 runs of 10 or more yards. What really impressed about Mason’s tape is how he can intersperse nice straight-line speed and killer jump cuts with all the power you’d expect from a back his size. What that means for his deployment in the 2026 season is to be determined, but Mason has proven that you don’t need to get too creative with him — just give him the ball, and watch the bodies fly. . @Vikings RB Jordan Mason can make guys miss, and outrun them, all day long. But he's at his best when he adds violence to the equation. pic.twitter.com/xabps1wnm5 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 10, 2026 Underrated free agent: CB James Pierre In the Vikings’ 24-21 Week 4 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers last season, Pittsburgh cornerback James Pierre had just 19 coverage snaps, but he made the most of them. Those coverage snaps included two Carson Wentz targets to receiver Jalen Nailor that Pierre broke up — one on the Pittsburgh 2-yard line with 2:20 left in the game, and one from the Minnesota 20-yard line with 1:02 remaining. Brian Flores, who was the Steelers’ senior defensive assistant & linebackers coach in 2022 before he became the Vikings’ DC in 2023, clearly paid attention. It’s certainly one reason the team signed the former undrafted free agent from Florida Atlantic to a two-year, $8.5 million contract with $3.715 million guaranteed this offseason. Pierre got more reps as the season went along and Darius Slay’s injury situation became more complicated. Overall in 2025, Pierre allowed just 16 catches on 35 targets for 163 yards, 75 yards after the catch, one touchdown, one interception, 10 pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 57.2. It was Pierre’s best season to date, and he proved to be the kind of cornerback every team wants — the big (6’2”, 185-pound) defender who can tangle up opposing receivers in both press and off coverage. Given the amount of zone coverage Flores likes to call behind all his crazy fronts and concepts (the Vikings played zone on 75.6% of their snaps last season), having someone who can run with and track opponents in off coverage is especially important. When in off coverage last season, Pierre allowed a ridiculous seven catches on 25 targets for 3.6 yards per catch, and nine pass breakups. Pierre is coming into his age 30 season, and he’s never been an NFL full-time starter — he maxed out with 415 defensive snaps for the Steelers in 2021, and he had 408 in 2025 — but this reunion with Flores could lead to bigger and better things. Based on the tape, he has everything to become Minnesota’s No. 1 guy opposite Isaiah Rodgers, with Byron Murphy in the slot. James Pierre had his best season in 2025. Now, the Vikings — who were pretty sick of Pierre denying their receivers last season — have the benefit of his prowess. pic.twitter.com/JpacrZcYWB — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 10, 2026 Underrated draft pick: CB Chuck Demmings There is another cornerback name to watch as the preseason rolls along, and that’s Chuck Demmings — another smaller-school (the Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks) guy who has skills which would seem to transcend that status. The Vikings took the 6’1”, 190-pound Demmings with the 163rd overall pick in the draft, and the rookie is already making quite the splash with his unique personality. A compilation of #Vikings rookie Chuck Demming’s inspirational quotes pre practice this year. pic.twitter.com/5GPVzvfJCi — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 9, 2026 I spoke with Demmings at the…

title: Processing Over Stats: Why Murray Beats McCarthy
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ most pressing question of 2026 training camp has a front-runner: Kyler Murray. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show — a Vikings 1st & SKOL production on the Bleav Network — host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano break down the quarterback competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy, roster bubble […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings’ most pressing question of 2026 training camp has a front-runner: Kyler Murray. On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show — a Vikings 1st & SKOL production on the Bleav Network — host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano break down the quarterback competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy, roster bubble battles, offensive line questions, and some rising stars worth watching before the preseason opener against the New York Giants. The central argument from Forness is not about flashy stats — it’s about processing. “The processing of both quarterbacks is going to be the differentiator in this quarterback competition,” Forness said. While McCarthy has had flashes, Forness sees a fundamental inconsistency: “McCarthy is not doing enough to show that he has improved significantly from, quite frankly, a really poor overall 2025 season.” ESPN’s Dan Graziano reportedly confirmed Murray is the “clubhouse leader,” and Forness agrees — but he frames the ceiling realistically: “If whoever starts is QB 16, this team could be a Super Bowl threat.” Key Points from This Episode: QB Competition: Murray leads, per ESPN’s Dan Graziano. Forness argues McCarthy’s processing remains at a sub-starter level despite some better moments in recent practices. Kevin O’Connell’s telling quote: “There have been some new layers to our offense… it might be a small detail, but it’s important and it affects the visual outcome of the play.” Forness believes this context explains many of Murray’s surface-level miscues. Tai Felton & Ivan Pace Jr.: Forness admits he was wrong on Felton: “He deserves a lot of credit for that.” Pace’s improved lateral coverage and multiple PBUs have also turned heads. Tight End Battle: Gavin Bartholomew has emerged as a top-three Mr. Mankato candidate with explosive seam routes, putting pressure on Ben Yurosek despite Yurosek’s solid camp. Offensive Line: Donovan Jackson expected to take a big step; Will Fries enters fully healthy for the first time. Blake Brandel’s snap precision is the key watchpoint. Charles Demmings: Forness projects a Mekhi Blackmon-style role — roughly 300 snaps as CB4, rotating in behind Byron Murphy Jr., Isaiah Rodgers, and James Pierre. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins: Could be a secret weapon as a 285–290-pound edge rusher who disrupts 13 personnel, after leveling Josh Oliver in a Wednesday full-team drill. Jake Golday, Elijah Williams, and the safety depth will be focal points in Thursday’s full preseason preview. Demond Claiborne remains off Forness’s 53-man roster projection due to pass-catching and pass-protection concerns — his only path is winning a return job. Win ceiling with Murray: “If the defense plays great and Murray plays average, 13, 14 [wins].” The show also touched on center Blake Brandel’s importance — Forness floated a potential mid-season extension if snap placement holds up — and the versatility of Jamal Adams in Brian Flores’s defense, calling Flores “an incredible play caller” who will deploy Adams across multiple roles. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The Real Forno Show is must-listen audio for any Vikings fan who wants genuine analysis, real debate, and the kind of honest accountability — including Forness openly admitting he was wrong on Tai Felton — that’s increasingly rare in sports media. New episodes drop regularly on the Vikings 1st & SKOL network via Bleav. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . What do you think? Does Kyler Murray have enough in the tank to lead the Vikings to a deep playoff run in 2026, or is the processing edge overstated?

full_text: Feb 8, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) against the Seattle Seahawks during Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Christian Gonzalez has been in the headlines throughout the offseason, mostly due to his unresolved contract situation. On Tuesday, he made news again — for two reasons. The first was him being a surprise absentee from the New England Patriots’ joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts. While that Gonzalez-less session was ready to begin, meanwhile, his ranking on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026 list as voted by his peers was announced. The Patriots’ standout cornerback checked in at No. 28, significantly higher than his 84th ranking the previous year. No. 28 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/4tjvqgGgSL — NFL (@NFL) August 11, 2026 Gonzalez making a sizable jump and being recognized by the rest of the league comes as no surprise. A Pro Bowl selection, he was one of the best cornerbacks in football in 2025 and played a crucial role in helping the Patriots return to the Super Bowl. “He’s super smart. Elite technique. He can get his hands on guys,” said Panthers quarterback Bryce Young about Gonzalez, who he faced in Week 4 of last year’s regular season. “It looks so easy for him,” added former Bills CB Tre’Davious White. “He goes up and gest the best guy each and every week, and that’s what you want from your top corner. Very competitive. Christian is a baller.” While not the most productive player from an interception perspective, Gonzalez nonetheless has earned the respect from players around the NFL. Last year’s playoffs showed why. Not only did he catch the game-clinching interception against the Broncos in the AFC Championship, he also would have had a strong case for game MVP had New England not lost Super Bowl LX to Seattle. “He’s a gifted player. He’s a special player. He’s a special teammate,” said Patriots punter Bryce Baringer. “It’s just awesome to see him do his thing. He’s a lockdown dude.”
