title: Christian Gonzalez practice absence raises questions amid ongoing contract talks
summary: When the New England Patriots took the Gillette Stadium fields on Tuesday for their joint session with the Indianapolis Colts, Christian Gonzalez was nowhere to be seen. The star cornerback did not make a late entry either; for the first time this training camp, he missed practice. Gonzalez’s absence comes in light of his ongoing […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) walks to the practice field during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the New England Patriots took the Gillette Stadium fields on Tuesday for their joint session with the Indianapolis Colts , Christian Gonzalez was nowhere to be seen. The star cornerback did not make a late entry either; for the first time this training camp, he missed practice. Gonzalez’s absence comes in light of his ongoing contract negotiation with the Patriots. Naturally, it raised questions whether or not the two were related. According to a report by Greg Bedard of the Boston Sports Journal, they were not. Gonzalez apparently sat out the session due to a “minor injury sustained at the end of Monday’s practice.” The 24-year-old appeared to hurt his ankle during that particular session, trying to defend a touchdown pass from Drake Maye to Romeo Doubs. He did not receive any medical attention on the field and left the session with no obvious limitation. Speculation nonetheless ran high on Tuesday, especially with Gonzalez seemingly throwing oil on the fire on social media later during the day: #Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez chose some interesting lyrics in his latest Instagram story… “Should have been done by now” (📸 christian.gonzalez3 IG) pic.twitter.com/LPRtEJy5DF — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) August 11, 2026 The post captioned with the phrase “Should have been done by now” appears to be a potential reference to contract talks that have been going on for multiple months without any results. And if Ian Rapoport of NFL Network is to be believed, no conclusion to the saga is in sight yet. “It’s interesting to me that yesterday they agreed to terms with Hunter Henry on a new contract extension, and then the next day Christian Gonzalez is not practicing,” Rapoport said on Tuesday. “There’s a good chance [Devon] Witherspoon gets done, I think. I don’t know about Gonzalez, whether it’s going to be this year or next year. But, the timing is certainly something that I took note of today and is interesting.” Tight end Hunter Henry, who is being represented by the same agency as Gonzalez, put his signature under a two-year, $16 million extension on Monday. The team captain was scheduled to enter free agency next March; Gonzalez remains signed through 2027 after the team exercised the fifth-year option in his rookie contract earlier this offseason. According to Patriots owner Robert Kraft, however, the team has a record-breaking contract on the table for the fourth-year defender just waiting to be signed. Gonzalez replied to Kraft’s statement by saying that “we don’t want to handle [it] in the media.” His teammates, meanwhile, are trying to go about their business as usual even with Gonzalez missing from practice. “As great as Gonzo is, we have an expectation on our team in general that there is no drop-off,” said safety Dell Pettus on Tuesday. “Everybody’s expected to come in and compete at the highest level that they’re able to compete at. We love having Gonzo out there and if he’s just not able to go for whatever reason it is that day, whoever comes in next is supposed to come in and be held at the same level as he is. Love Gonzo, need him out here every day we can, but whoever’s next up, we expect the same greatness out of them.” With the Patriots holding a closed-doors walkthrough on Wednesday, Gonzalez’s next possible public appearance could come on Thursday night during the preseason opener against the Colts.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Tommy DeVito finding his ‘flow state’ as Patriots QB2
summary: Tommy DeVito was a member of the New York Giants at this time last season. The quarterback did not join New England until Aug. 27, when the Patriots claimed him off waivers. DeVito went on to spend all season as a third-stringer behind starter Drake Maye and veteran backup Joshua Dobbs. While DeVito learned New […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JUNE 09: Tommy DeVito #16 of the New England Patriots runs drills during a minicamp at Gillette Stadium on June 09, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tommy DeVito was a member of the New York Giants at this time last season. The quarterback did not join New England until Aug. 27, when the Patriots claimed him off waivers. DeVito went on to spend all season as a third-stringer behind starter Drake Maye and veteran backup Joshua Dobbs. While DeVito learned New England’s offense behind the scenes, his work on the practice field came in scout-team situations. Now elevated to the primary backup in Year 2, DeVito has finally gotten on-field practice experience in the offense and seen tremendous growth in his game since this spring. “It’s a different world,” DeVito said. “It’s one thing to be in the classroom and be in it and learn and everything, but it’s another thing to get reps in it. Because last year, I didn’t get reps in the offense. My first reps were during OTAs (this year). So to be able to actually take everything from the classroom and bring it to the field and physically feel mistakes, that’s personally how I learn my best.” The results are showing on the practice fields as well. Over the last several training camp practices, DeVito has impressed operating the second-team offense, highlighted by a handful of perfectly thrown deep balls. In Friday’s intra-squad scrimmage, DeVito found DeMario Douglas downfield for a 40-plus-yard completion. The last two days, he connected twice with Kyle Williams and needed just one throw — a long touchdown to Mack Hollins down the right sideline — to find the end zone in his one-minute drill against the Indianapolis Colts. “The talent always been there but he’s just in a flow state right now,” safety Dell Pettus said of DeVito. “Like, he looks fantastic. I love practicing against him. When you practice against like two great quarterbacks, two quarterbacks who are very talented, it makes you better and makes the defense better because you know you have to be at the top of your game.” The Patriots ultimately hope they don’t need to see DeVito uncork it downfield this season. But having a strong insurance plan behind Maye is valuable, something DeVito experienced firsthand as a rookie when he was elevated up the depth chart and went on to win three straight games. “That whole prepare like a starter thing was very real to me my rookie year when I was young,” DeVito said. “So I treated that as such whether you’re the two or the three, because even two years ago when I was in New York, I was the three one week, and then the next week, I was starting. You’ve always got to stay ready. So I just keep that mindset.” Through the offseason program and 14 training camp practices, his head coach likes what he’s seen from the quarterback who wears two gold chains. “2 Chains is doing a nice job,” Vrabel said Tuesday morning. “He continues to learn, and with it being a new system, I think it got his attention a little bit better, as opposed to saying, ‘Hey, I know what this is,’ and kind of taking it for granted. I think he’s really done a nice job.”

title: 7 performances of note from the Patriots’ joint practice with the Colts
summary: In preparation of their preseason opener on Thursday, the New England Patriots hosted the Indianapolis Colts on the practice fields on Tuesday. The two teams got together for a two-hour joint session behind Gillette Stadium, an intense affair that saw multiple big plays being made on both sides. To recap practice, please head over to […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 11: Hunter Henry #85 of the New England Patriots reacts during a joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images In preparation of their preseason opener on Thursday, the New England Patriots hosted the Indianapolis Colts on the practice fields on Tuesday. The two teams got together for a two-hour joint session behind Gillette Stadium, an intense affair that saw multiple big plays being made on both sides. To recap practice, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye for better or worse. Standout of the day QB Tommy DeVito: Drake Maye had a good overall practice, but we give DeVito the edge as our “standout of the day” in part because unlike the starter he managed to end his own one-minute drill with a touchdown. That play — a laser to Eli Raridon for six — was not the only strong one the Patriots’ QB2 had on Tuesday, though. DeVito also hit some deep shots down the field, connecting with Kyle Williams and Mack Hollins for big plays. No matter who was in the lineup with him — Efton Chism and Hunter Henry also caught passes from him — he made sure to found them. It was another impressive outing from a player who was buried on the depth chart during his first year in New England in 2025, but has a stranglehold of the No. 2 spot right now. “It’s a different world,” said DeVito about his development since last sesaon. “It’s one thing to be in the classroom and be in it and learn and everything, but it’s another thing to get reps. Because last year, I didn’t get any reps in the offense; my first rep was during OTAs. So, to be able to actually take everything from the classroom and bring it to the field — physically learn mistakes — that’s personally how I learn my best. So, it’s good for me.” Other performances of note QB Drake Maye: The Patriots’ starting quarterback did not have a perfect day — his final pass in a one-minute drill was underthrown and picked off — but he still can feel good about it. Maye, after all, looked very good early on and threw big-play passes to A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Overall, he completed 15 of 23 pass attempts with that INT during 11-on-11 work, and went 4-of-6 in 7-on-7s. WR DeMario Douglas: Even though he was the target on Drake Maye’s ill-fated pass attempt late during the one-minute drill, Douglas had another productive practice. He looked very good during 1-on-1s, with his speed, quickness and leaping ability an issue for the Colts’ DBs. Furthermore, he was Maye’s favorite target during the one-minute segment that ended with the interception; before the pick, Douglas caught two of his QB’s passes. TE Hunter Henry and TE Eli Raridon: The Patriots’ top tight ends had a busy day right out of the gate, with both actively involved during an early-down portion. Maye had two big-play connections with Henry, one on a wheel route and the other down the seam. He also hit Raridon on a play-action crossing pattern for a sizable gain. The pair also produced with Tommy DeVito running the show: both caught touchdowns from the backup QB, including a tight-window touchdown throw to Raridon. Run defense: Christian Barmore was a limited participant, and maybe his absence contributed to the issues, but the Patriots run defense did not have its best day. The Jonathan Taylor-led Colts very much dictated the flow on the ground from start to finish. Not all was bad — Dre’Mont Jones had a tackle for loss against Taylor at one point — but there is obvious room for improvement, especially and unsurprisingly on the edge. CB Kobee Minor: With Christian Gonzalez absent for undisclosed reasons, Minor was elevated to a starting role opposite Carlton Davis replacement Kindle Vildor. However, the sophomore struggled to take advantage of the opportunity: he was flagged for defensive pass interference on a deep pass attempt and subsequently pulled in favor of rookie Karon Prunty. Other players worth mentioning include edge defender Elijah Ponder, who had a strip sack during 11-on-11s. Meanwhile, safety John Saunders Jr. registered an interception against Colts backup QB Riley Leonard during the same segment. Elsewhere, Will Campbell went a perfect 2-0 during his 1-on-1 battles with edge Arden Key. Tuesday’s joint sessions in the books, the Patriots will not hit the practice fields again until the weekend. Of course, in between, they are set to take on the Colts in both teams’ preseason opener. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, Aug. 13.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots training camp recap: Drake Maye ends strong Colts joint practice on sour note
summary: The New England Patriots welcomed the Indianapolis Colts to Gillette Stadium on Tuesday for what turned out to be a productive and competitive joint practice. Here’s what went down on the practice fields. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 120 minutes (10:15 a.m.-12:15 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the mid 80s To no surprise, the joint practice […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 11: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots throws during a joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots welcomed the Indianapolis Colts to Gillette Stadium on Tuesday for what turned out to be a productive and competitive joint practice. Here’s what went down on the practice fields. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 120 minutes (10:15 a.m.-12:15 p.m. ET) Conditions: Sunny, temperatures in the mid 80s To no surprise, the joint practice between the Patriots and Colts featured full pads and ran just about two hours long. The focus was on full-team and situational work — ending in the red zone and end-of-game situations. Attendance Absent: CB Christian Gonzalez (new), S Mike Brown (new), WR Kyle Dixon Limited: CB Carlton Davis III, DL Christian Barmore, CB Charles Woods, LS Julian Ashby, OT Morgan Moses PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez was a surprise absence for joint practice on Tuesday. Gonzalez remains in the middle of contract negotiations, but did appear to take a hard fall on Monday in coverage against Romeo Doubs. Several players then remained limited, which included Christian Barmore after he missed the last two practices. “Just still trying to get him back knowing that we have some time, and it’s a long season,” Mike Vrabel said prior to practice. “He’s played a lot of football, and he’s played a lot of football for us. He was disruptive for us. We just have to make sure that we are smart about what we are doing right now.“ Takeaways Drake’s day: It was an overall strong day for Drake Maye and the Patriots starting offense, as the quarterback seemed to largely work in clean pockets and found explosive plays through the air to A.J. Brown (hole shot), Romeo Doubs (downfield fade) and both of his tight ends, Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Unfortunately for Maye, his day ended with a sour note in his final end-of-game drive. After quickly moving the ball downfield with two completions to DeMario Douglas, a scramble, and quick out to Efton Chism, Maye moved off his spot and underthrew a seam shot to Douglas which was intercepted by Colts safety Cam Bynum in the end zone. “I thought we did some good things and I think we got to finish off better,” Maye said. “That’s speaking on my part in the two-minute drill. But, I really think it’s we challenge our guys to be try to be consistent throughout the day and I think they responded to that.” Defensive struggles: Daniel Jones and the Colts offense meanwhile found success in their end-of-half drive, connecting with tight end Tyler Warren three times to move down to the 5-yard line. With two seconds left on the clock, Jones got the ball out before the Patriots all-out pressure got home and found Josh Downs open against Marcus Jones along the goal line for a touchdown. Jones and the Colts moved the ball fairly well the rest of the afternoon against a secondary that was down Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis, while Jonathan Taylor and their run game largely had the advantage. 1-on-1 highlights: Practice started with a bang, as the first 1-on-1 rep with both teams on the field saw A.J. Brown align opposite Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner. Advantage Brown, as the receiver nearly put Gardner on the ground on a comeback route to draw a loud reaction from the crowd. A.J. Brown just DUSTED Sauce Gardner in 1v1s🔥 Patriots fans in attendance LOVE IT – @CLNSMedia pic.twitter.com/0g1GBXTSjf — Patriots on CLNS (@PatriotsCLNS) August 11, 2026 Other standouts included: DeMario Douglas going up to high point a seam route over Justin Walley and survive the ground. Efton Chism III easily separating from Robert Carter Jr. downfield and hauling in a full-extension diving catch. Kyle Williams also creating easy separation off the line of scrimmage on multiple reps. Tommy 2 Chains: Patriots backup quarterback Tommy DeVito continues to string together positive practices, and he turned in another one against the Colts. DeVito started early by connecting on a deep post touchdown to Kyle Williams, who split a pair of Colts defenders for their second long ball connection in as many days. DeVito was also sharp working the underneath and effective finding his tight ends in the red zone hitting Eli Raridon and Hunter Henry for scores. In his end-of-game drive, DeVito needed just one play as he found Mack Hollins deep down the right sideline for a score. Getting another play inside the five, he then connected with Raridon for another touchdown. “2 Chains is doing a nice job,” Vrabel said. “He continues to learn, and with it being a new system, I think it got his attention a little bit better, as opposed to saying, “Hey, I know what this is,” and kind of taking it for granted. I think he’s really done a nice job.“ Other notes: A.J. Brown (3 catches on 5 targets), Romeo Doubs (2 catches on 2 targets), and DeMario Douglas (3 catches on 4 targets) continued to be the top three receivers working with Maye. Brown struggled with footing on numerous occasions and while Doubs created separation on his touchdown receptions in the red zone, the receiver seemed to struggle to get away from Indianapolis’ corners for most of the day. Efton Chism III (3 catches on 3 targets) continued to work in with both of the top offense. Kyle Williams (1 catch on 2 targets) was targeted downfield by Maye but was tangled up by the cornerback. Kayshon Boutte (1 catch on 4 targets) connected just once with Maye. Rhamondre Stevenson had an impressive touchdown connection with Maye on a downfield corner route with the QB fading away. Busy day for rookie Eli Raridon with four catches in 11-on-11 work — including one play-action crosser from Maye. New England’s top offensive line remained the same and seemed to hold up well in pass protection while the run game work seemed hit-or-miss. Caleb Lomu was back at left tackle with the second unit while mixing in at right tackle for a limited Morgan Moses. Most of the Patriots’ defensive pressure appeared to come up the middle courtesy of Milton Williams and Cory Durden. Primarily working with the second-team, rookie Gabe Jacas did pop in the backfield on one instance. Elijah Ponder also drew a hold and batted down a screen. With no Gonzalez or Davis, New England opened with Kindle Vildor and Kobee Minor in their secondary before Karon Prunty replaced Minor, who drew a DPI, in the end-of-game period. The secondary largely struggled — specifically in red zone 7-on-7s until Marcellas Dial recorded a pass breakup. New England’s second string defense ended practice on a high note as John Saunders Jr. recorded an interception off of Riley Leonard in a one-minute drive. Safety Peter Manuma was in coverage. Andy Borregales went 5-of-7 in live field goal work with both misses coming from 50 yards. Top punt coverage team: Reggie Gilliam, Namdi Obiazor, Terrell Jennings, Chad Muma, Elijah Ponder, Khalil Jacobs, and Dell Pettus (personal protector). Top kick return pairings: Terrell Jennings/Kyle Williams and Lan Larison/Efton Chism. One dust up during the day following a live kick return that ended near a sideline. Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins appeared to be nearby while Colts DE Durrell Nchami lost his helmet and appeared to throw a punch. Preview Following their joint practice with the Colts, the Patriots will hold a closed walkthrough on Wednesday; neither fans nor media will be present for the session. On Thursday, the two teams will then square off inside Gillette Stadium for their preseason opener. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET, with Drake Maye not expected to see any action .

title: Drake Maye not expected to play in Patriots preseason opener
summary: The New England Patriots will play their first football game of the season on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts, but don’t expect their starting quarterback to take part in the action. As head coach Mike Vrabel said during a press conference ahead of his team’s joint practice with the Colts on Tuesday, he does […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 14: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Gillette Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots will play their first football game of the season on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts, but don’t expect their starting quarterback to take part in the action. As head coach Mike Vrabel said during a press conference ahead of his team’s joint practice with the Colts on Tuesday, he does not anticipate Drake Maye to take the field in the first preseason game. “I wouldn’t anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday, but that’s all subject to change,” Vrabel explained. “That’s kind of where my mindset is right now, standing here today. Really, it’s just important that we get the work in and get things accomplished that we’re looking to get accomplished. That can always change, but I wouldn’t anticipate that happening right now.” Maye not playing in the preseason opener would be a change of course for the third-year quarterback. He played six snaps in his first ever NFL game as a rookie against the Panthers in 2024, followed by a 14-snap outing in last year’s preseason opener versus the Commanders. If he indeed sits out the Colts game, the quarterback role will be split by current backup Tommy DeVito and seventh-round rookie Behren Morton against Indianapolis. As for any other players, Vrabel mentioned a balance between players seeing regular action during Tuesday’s practice and Thursday’s game. “A lot of the front-line players and whoever’s available, some of the guys maybe won’t get as much work today, will get extensive work in the game on Thursday,” he said. “That’s just how it goes. Let’s see how today goes and we can always adjust and plan accordingly.”

title: Why joint practices matter, explained by Patriots players
summary: The New England Patriots have never been shy about joining forces with other teams in training camp. They did so under Bill Belichick, during Jerod Mayo’s one-year stint, and now that Mike Vrabel is in his second year as head coach. After holding sessions with the Commanders and Vikings last year, the Patriots will play […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 10: Line captain Marcus Jones #25 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 10, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots have never been shy about joining forces with other teams in training camp. They did so under Bill Belichick, during Jerod Mayo’s one-year stint, and now that Mike Vrabel is in his second year as head coach. After holding sessions with the Commanders and Vikings last year, the Patriots will play hosts to two more teams this summer. First, the Indianapolis Colts will come to town for one practice on Tuesday. Then, next week, it will be the Eagles to visit the Gillette Stadium facility for two more workouts; both sessions will be followed by preseason games between the clubs involved. Why are joint practices a thing in the first place, though? Because they are a useful tool for the teams participating. And don’t take it from us either; just listen to what Patriots veterans had to say about them heading into Tuesday’s session with the Colts . To break the monotony of camp “In the middle of the camp, it’s fun to do that because we’ve just been going against each other for two and a half weeks now over and over and over again. You’re going against the same guy over and over again.” — TE Hunter Henry The Patriots have indeed been focused on themselves so far this summer. Their first 13 practices exclusively featured Patriot-on-Patriot action, including multiple times in full pads. And while there is value in that, or else training camp as whole would lose its purpose, a certain monotony can be introduced by repeatedly facing the same players in the same set of circumstances. The so-called dog days of camp are real, and joint sessions help mix them up a bit. To get insight into different schemes “Very important, and the reason why I say that is because we get to see other schemes. Whenever we practice against each other, we get to know how our offensive guys work, the offensive line, their checks and everything. But now we get to see how different offensive schemes get to be. And then also on the offensive side, they get to see other defensive schemes as well.” — CB Marcus Jones The ultimate goal of training camp is to get the team ready for the challenges of the regular season, both physically and mentally. That mental aspect is, to a large degree, built through repetition; you get better at something if you practice it over and over. That is part of the repetitiveness mentioned earlier, but also why practicing against another team can be appealing: it gives a glimpse into what other teams like to run and are working on. While the exposure to those different schemes is relatively minimal in the grand scheme of things, it still can come in handy once the games start to matter. At the very least, though, it is more practice on how to adjust on the fly — a crucial skill in the NFL. To get better technically “You get to refine your skills, at the end of the day. That’s what it is. You refine your eyes, your feet, how you communicate with the backend, how you communicate with the front guys because they’re going to give us something that our offense hasn’t given us. And in the same way, our defense is going to do something that their defense doesn’t do. So, you just get a chance to see how your rules, how your job, and how your hands and feet work against a different team.” — LB Christian Elliss Every NFL player is different in what they can do and are comfortable with. Finding that out is a key element of training camp — an environment that allows for trying out and getting a feel for things. And while joint sessions are still practice when all is said and done, the technical focus needs to become more refined against an opponent who might not care all that much if your running back gets knocked out of his socks or not. To strengthen the team “It’s the first time we’re a full team. We’re all going to wear the same color and cheer on each other in a way instead of going against each other. It’s always fun to have those battles throughout camp and all of a sudden just kind of come together as a team and try to build that.” — TE Hunter Henry Ever since his introductory press conference last January, Mike Vrabel has made one thing clear: culture is important. Building that culture does not happen overnight and is an arduous process, but one that comes into full effect once the team stands united. Against the Colts and Eagles, the 2026 Patriots will do that for the first time. While the competitive element still is significant — only 53 roster spots are available come cutdown day — the culture and team spirit will truly come out when somebody else is lining up opposite you.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: For Patriots rookies, joint practices offer ‘real taste of the NFL’
summary: The training wheels are about to come off for the New England Patriots’ rookie class. After 13 training camp practices of only going up against their themselves and their veteran teammates, they now will get a chance to hit somebody else. That somebody else is the Indianapolis Colts, who are in Foxborough on Tuesday for […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots tackle Caleb Lomu (74) walks to the practice field during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The training wheels are about to come off for the New England Patriots’ rookie class. After 13 training camp practices of only going up against their themselves and their veteran teammates, they now will get a chance to hit somebody else. That somebody else is the Indianapolis Colts, who are in Foxborough on Tuesday for a two-hour joint session. It projects to be the most competitive practice of the summer thus far, and a new experience for the first-year players on New England’s roster. “That’ll be the real taste of the NFL going against a different team,” said offensive tackle Caleb Lomu. Lomu, who projects to spend his rookie season as the third offensive tackle behind starters Will Campbell and Morgan Moses, last competed against other players in late November. That day, he played 59 snaps as Utah’s left tackle in a 31-21 win over Kansas. There are obvious differences between that game and Tuesday’s practice. Nonetheless, the first-round draft pick is looking forward to the upcoming challenge. “It’ll be fun to go against another team besides the Patriots, who we have been going up against all camp,” he explained. “It’ll be nice to really put my my skills on tape going against the Colts. And so, I’m just excited for the opportunity.” The same is true for Tanner Arkin, the undrafted rookie tight end who has been one of the positive surprises of camp so far. “I’m expecting a high-energy, awesome day,” Arkin said after the Patriots’ practice on Monday . “Two teams colliding. First joint practice. So, hopefully there’s going to be a lot of great energy out there, great competition. I’m excited to just put my best foot forward and attack the day really.” While the excitement is palpable among New England’s rookies and roster in general, the joint session with the Colts is just the latest of several steps toward the regular season and start of truly meaningful football. Understanding that and keeping everything in perspective will be a key for the youngsters, according to fifth-year veteran and team captain Marcus Jones. “Take it one play at a time,” Jones said when asked about the advice he had for his rookie teammates. “You’re not going to make every single play, but the main thing is how you respond. There’s going to be some times where you don’t catch the ball. There’s going to be some times when you give up a big play. But at the end of the day, it’s minimizing that and making sure confidence-wise that you have it. Because, at the end of the day, you’re playing against one of the best. You know, it’s not college anymore and you’re playing in that 1%.”

title: Patriots training camp primer: Colts joint practice preview, schedule, more
summary: After spending their first 13 sessions of training camp competing again themselves, the New England Patriots are getting some company: the Indianapolis Colts are in town for one joint practice ahead of the two teams’ preseason opener on Thursday. Here is everything you need to know about the session. Schedule Unlike Monday’s session, the joint […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 4: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye at training camp on August 4, 2026. (Photo by David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images After spending their first 13 sessions of training camp competing again themselves, the New England Patriots are getting some company: the Indianapolis Colts are in town for one joint practice ahead of the two teams’ preseason opener on Thursday. Here is everything you need to know about the session. Schedule Unlike Monday’s session, the joint practice with the Colts is open to fans. As usual, attendance and parking are free. 9:30 a.m. ET: Mike Vrabel press conference 10:15 a.m. ET: Joint practice with Colts ca. 12:15 p.m. ET: Player availability (QB Drake Maye, QB Tommy DeVito, WR Efton Chism III, WR Kyle Williams, OT Morgan Moses, S Dell Pettus) As always, the schedule is tentative and subject to change. For more information, please visit our Pats Pulpit Training Camp Guide . Story of the day Competition is the name of the game at training camp, but you can only get so much out of going up against the same players and scheme time and again. The Colts’ visit is therefore a welcome change for the Patriots: they will get to measure their progress against another team and get a first feel where they might be headed. That is true both for the team overall and its individual players. Some, such as rookies Caleb Lomu, Gabe Jacas and Eli Raridon will get their first taste of real NFL competition. Others will get to see where they might still have room for growth. Needless to say, Tuesday’s practice will provide plenty of data points for the team to work with. Injuries to monitor PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler DNP (8/10): DT Christian Barmore, CB Charles Woods, WR Kyle Dixon (new) Even though five players were missing from Monday’s practice with two others — CB Carlton Davis, LS Julian Ashby — limited, the Patriots are in decent shape ahead of their joint session with the Colts. They nonetheless might try to limit the exposure for some players such as as tight end Hunter Henry or offensive linemen Alijah Vera-Tucker and Morgan Moses. Players to watch QB Drake Maye: The Patriots’ starting quarterback has looked good so far this summer, and is seemingly ready to pick up where he left off last season. Of course, Tuesday will be the most concrete confirmation of his progress yet. The Colts defense, headed by standouts such as DeForest Buckner, Arden Key and Sauce Gardner, is a solid unit in its own right. Whether it is better than New England’s can be debated, but it very much is different . That in itself brings a challenge for the third-year QB. WR A.J. Brown: The high-prized offseason acquisition has looked as expected since joining New England via trade from the Eagles, and his battles with Christian Gonzalez have been entertaining. Now, however, Brown will get a chance to compete against the aforementioned Sauce Gardner and company, and to show for the first time that his underwhelming 2025 season in Philadelphia was a fluke. LT Will Campbell and C Jared Wilson: The Patriots’ two youngest starting offensive linemen have had a solid start to their sophomore training camp, but now the first real test awaits. Going against a team with little reason to hold back, Campbell and Wilson need to be on their A-game to prove that they are indeed in the midst of making a sizable Year 2 jump. ED Gabe Jacas: The second-round rookie has increased his workload steadily since returning from the non-football injury list, and the Patriots will need him to develop quickly given their questions along the edge as well as Harold Landry’s continued absence. Going against a different opponent for the first time in his career will help with this development, and help show just how ready for a prominent role Jacas truly is at this point. CB Christian Gonzalez: Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones is not expected to play on Thursday night, which means that most of the work this week might come on the practice field. If so, it will be interesting to see how actively he will target the Patriots’ No. 1 cornerback, and how he will look against a receiver corps that is missing its own No. 1, Alec Pierce. Gonzalez has been arguably the best player on the field this summer for New England and now will get a chance to continue his hot streak against another team. Pats Pulpit will have you covered throughout the day, so please make sure to regularly check back to patspulpit.com for all the latest news from camp. Credentialed Patriots beat writers Brian Hines ( @iambrianhines ), Andrew Guindon ( @NestPgs ) and Taylor Kyles ( @tkyles39 ) will bring you live updates from camp on their Twitter/X feeds, so please make sure to give them a follow.

title: Drew Brees to join Saints Ring of Honor during halftime ceremony against Vikings
summary: Former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees, a first-ballot selection to the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, will be inducted into the franchise’s Ring of Honor and receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame Ring of Excellence during an on-field ceremony at halftime on Sunday, October 11, 2026, when the Saints host […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Former NFL quarterback Drew Brees is introduced prior to the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game between the Carolina Panthers and the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees, a first-ballot selection to the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, will be inducted into the franchise’s Ring of Honor and receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame Ring of Excellence during an on-field ceremony at halftime on Sunday, October 11, 2026, when the Saints host the Minnesota Vikings. “As we celebrate the 60th season of the New Orleans Saints in 2026, the Ring of Honor represents the very best of our franchise and those whose impact extends throughout the National Football League,” said Saints Owner & CEO Gayle Benson. “We are thrilled to welcome Drew into this distinguished group in October. His extraordinary accomplishments on the field, his leadership, and his lasting contributions to the New Orleans community make this honor so well deserved. We look forward to celebrating Drew with our fans and honoring the extraordinary legacy he built with the Saints and throughout the New Orleans community.” Drew Brees signed with the New Orleans Saints in 2006 and spent 15 seasons in New Orleans before retiring in 2021. During his time with the Saints, he led the team to its first Super Bowl victory in the 2009 season, defeating the Indianapolis Colts 31–17 and earning Super Bowl MVP honors. Brees also helped the Saints win seven NFC South division titles and reach three NFC Championship Games. He was a two-time NFL Offensive Player of the Year, earned five All-Pro selections, and made 13 Pro Bowls. He set an NFL record with five 5,000-yard passing seasons, and in 2011, he threw for a then-record 5,476 yards in a single season. Brees finished his Saints career with 68,010 passing yards and 491 touchdown passes, making him the franchise’s all-time leader in major passing categories. He was inducted into the New Orleans Saints Hall of Fame in 2024, and in 2026, he was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility, becoming the first Saints player ever selected as a first-ballot Hall of Famer. “It will be a privilege to recognize Drew as a member of our Ring of Honor in October,” said Saints Executive Vice President/General Manager Mickey Loomis. “Drew’s production and character both on and off the field sets him apart as the greatest Saint ever. This is a great opportunity for our organization and our fan base to show appreciation for his Hall of Fame career.” Brees will become the 9th person from the Saints organization to be inducted into the Ring of Honor, joining Owner Tom Benson (2018), K Morten Andersen (2016), G Jahri Evans (2024), LB Rickey Jackson (2013), QB Archie Manning (2013), LB Sam Mills (2021), T William Roaf (2013) and DE Will Smith (2019).

title: Statistical milestones that Saints players can reach in 2026
summary: With the 2026 regular season just a few weeks away, let’s take a look at some statistical milestones certain Saints players have a chance at reaching this year. Cameron Jordan Jordan returns to the Saints for his 15th season following his first double digit sack season since 2021. He has 132 sacks in his career […]
full_text: With the 2026 regular season just a few weeks away, let’s take a look at some statistical milestones certain Saints players have a chance at reaching this year. Cameron Jordan Jordan returns to the Saints for his 15th season following his first double digit sack season since 2021. He has 132 sacks in his career which ranks 17th all-time on the official list and 22nd on the unofficial list. He has a real chance to move up significantly on this list in 2026 however. If Jordan gets 6.5 sacks this year he will move into the top 10 all-time on the official list, and if he gets 10 sacks he will finish the season 6th on the official list and in the top 10 on the unofficial list. If he can replicate his production from 2025 he will finish with more career sacks than recent Hall of Famers Jared Allen, Jason Taylor, and DeMarcus Ware. Everyone who has finished their career with at least 136 sacks is a Hall of Famer or a future Hall of Famer in the case of Terrell Suggs and Von Miller. If Miller remains unsigned, Jordan will start the year as the active leader in career sacks. Jordan is also two tackles for loss away from moving into third all-time in the stat, which has been recorded since 1999. He would surpass Lavonte David and Von Miller (who both played last year but who are both currently free agents) and trail only JJ Watt, Calais Campbell, and Terrell Suggs. If Jordan finishes the year with 6.5 sacks and 2 TFLs, it will be very hard to justify keeping him out of the Pro Football Hall of Fame after he retires. Alvin Kamara The Saints running back is just 52 receiving yards away from 5,000 in his career. If he reaches this milestone, it will make him just the 6th player in NFL history to have 5,000 rushing and 5,000 receiving yards for his career. Four of these players are already in the Hall of Fame, and the other two (Tiki Barber and Christian McCaffrey) might also get there some day. Kamara has more receiving yards than Hall of Famer Roger Craig, and among running backs is just 235 receiving yards from passing Barber for 7th all time, and 463 away from passing Marcus Allen for 6th all-time (McCaffrey is currently 6th all-time but is just 21 yards behind Allen meaning he will likely finish the year in the top 5). Kamara is just one of six running backs in NFL history with 600+ career receptions and is 5 receptions away from moving into the top 5 all-time, and 19 away from moving into 4th all-time. You can narrow his accomplishments even further if you include touchdowns, as he would become just the 3rd player all-time with at least 7,000 rushing yards, 5,000 receiving yards, 60 rushing TDs, and 25 receiving TDs, with only Marshall Faulk and McCaffrey joining him in this club. Kamara would have reached these milestones last year or even the year before that if he hadn’t suffered from injuries, but this year he should finally reach these milestones. If Kamara can put together another season or two with his production, his career stats will also make it very hard for the voters to keep him out of Canton. Tyler Shough The Saints second year quarterback is coming off a great rookie season in 2025 and will be looking to already move into the top 10 in team history in passing yards in his sophomore year. 1,287 yards will move Shough past Ken Stabler into 10th, and 1,496 yards will move him into 9th. Derek Carr is 8th all-time in team history with 6,023 yards, 3,640 more than Shough. Shough averaged 216.7 yards per game last year, and if he maintains this average in 2026 and plays every game he would finish with 3,684 yards, just eclipsing Carr in only his second year with the team. He is also 11 passing touchdowns away from moving into the top 10 all-time in Saints history. The ultimate hope is that he will finish second all-time in Saints history in all relevant passing stats (I won’t ask him to pass Brees), and if he keeps up the production from his rookie year, he will be well on his way. Chris Olave Chris Olave bounced back from an injury plagued 2024 to show that he is still a top tier WR1 in the NFL, and his career year in 2025 earned him a well-deserved $132 million extension. He is currently 12th all-time in team history in receiving yards but will likely pass many former Saints this year and move way up on the list. He is just 122 yards away from the top 10, 1,064 away from passing Jimmy Graham for 7th all-time and 1,148 from passing Danny Abramowicz for 6th. In all likelihood he will finish in the top 5 in team history, as he is already over halfway to Michael Thomas’s career numbers, and is currently third all-time in team history in receiving yards per game behind Thomas and Joe Horn. Jordyn Tyson Setting any of the Saints rookie receiving records is a tough ask, even for a first round pick like Tyson. The Saints have a rich history of rookie receivers, as they are the only team in the Super Bowl era with three different rookie receivers to go for 1,030+ receiving yards. The team’s rookie records for a receiver are 1,138 yards, 93 receptions, and 10 TDs, all of which are a very tough ask. However, if Tyson can manage 1,000 receiving yards he would join Marques Colston, Michael Thomas, and Olave as the only rookies in team history to do so, which is a very good group to be in. Travis Etienne Jr. The Saints top signing in the offseason arrives from Jacksonville needing just 202 rushing yards to reach 4,000 for his career and is 1,202 away from reaching 5,000. Juwan Johnson Johnson is 714 yards and 1 TD away from moving into the top 3 in team history among Tight Ends in both categories. Which Saints do you think will reach these milestones in 2026 and why?

After retiring from the league ahead of the 2025 NFL season, Carr will now join the Bruins as a special advisor to head coach Bob Chesney. Carr was drafted to the NFL by the then-Oakland Raiders […]
full_text: UCLA has announced the hiring of Derek Carr, former Saints and NFL quarterback, to the football program’s coaching staff. After retiring from the league ahead of the 2025 NFL season, Carr will now join the Bruins as a special advisor to head coach Bob Chesney. Carr was drafted to the NFL by the then-Oakland Raiders in the second round of the 2014 draft out of Fresno State. The California native played collegiately with the Bulldogs before becoming the 36th overall selection. Following a whirlwind time in Oakland and the current home of the Raiders, Las Vegas, Carr was released by the team following the 2022 season. The New Orleans Saints would eventually sign the QB out of free agency in an attempt to garner some veteran leadership at the position. Unfortunately, Carr’s time in the Crescent City did not live up to the expectations of many as the team would manage just a 14-13 record in games played with Carr at quarterback. A severe shoulder injury sustained would eventually lead him to retire just before the 2025 NFL season kicked off meaning just 2 of his 11 pro seasons were spent with the Saints. Derek Carr’s return to the college ranks in his home state will begin a new opportunity post-playing. His role will involve assisting Chesney along with the rest of the Bruins’ offensive staff with game planning and aiding in the development of UCLA’s QB room.

title: Is Julian Blackmon’s ability to stay healthy worth concern?
summary: Julian Blackmon has already given the New Orleans Saints a reason to wonder whether they can count on him to stay healthy for an entire season. Now, another injury has brought that question back into focus. The 27-year-old left Saturday’s practice early with a knee injury, creating some concern given how his first season in […]
full_text: Julian Blackmon has already given the New Orleans Saints a reason to wonder whether they can count on him to stay healthy for an entire season. Now, another injury has brought that question back into focus. The 27-year-old left Saturday’s practice early with a knee injury, creating some concern given how his first season in the Big Easy played out. The good news is that the veteran safety returned to practice Sunday, suggesting the issue may not be serious. Still, it is understandable why Saints fans might be watching closely. Blackmon’s 2025 season did not go as planned and was essentially over before it ever got started. He suffered a torn posterior labrum in his shoulder during New Orleans’ season opener against the Arizona Cardinals. Despite the injury, Blackmon played the entire game and recorded seven tackles and a pass breakup. He ultimately landed on injured reserve and missed the remainder of the season. Unfortunately, last season was not the only example of Blackmon dealing with significant injuries. His career has included a torn ACL in 2019, a torn Achilles in 2021, an ankle injury that cost him time in 2022 and a shoulder labrum injury during the 2024 season with Indianapolis. That history makes Saturday’s knee issue worth monitoring, even if it ultimately proves to be nothing more than a minor training camp setback. At the same time, it would feel a little premature to suggest the Saints have another Blackmon injury problem on their hands. His return to practice the following day was an ideal sign, and there has been no indication that the knee injury is serious. So, is Blackmon’s injury history worth concern? Absolutely. Is it time to panic? Not yet. For now, this remains an overreaction. However, it is something worth keeping an eye on as the Saints continue their preparation for the 2026 season.

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 12 of Giants training camp. After Years Of Losing For Giants, John Harbaugh’s Arrival Is A Breath Of Fresh Air | FOX Sports [Practices are] different than what it was under Brian Daboll … and Joe Judge … and Pat Shurmur … and, to an extent, even Tom Coughlin, who drilled his players hard but not often for as long. Still, the early reviews from the players have been nothing but positive. Or, at the very least, they’re not complaining. There’s been too much losing around here for too long for anyone to be upset about an accomplished coach who wants to push them. And Harbaugh has been thrilled to learn that these Giants are ready to work. “I see it, in this organization and this team, with the players especially,” Harbaugh told me shortly after practice. “These players are determined to do what is required to become good enough, to earn the right to have a chance to win a football game. I feel like I see that. I see it every day in what they do and how they carry themselves and how hard they work. And I know they look back and they say, ‘Man, we’re getting better. We see it.'” Malik Nabers’ hands are still working Malik Nabers looking pretty good to me pic.twitter.com/OmT1xcX0Aj — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) August 11, 2026 The Giants were ‘starving for direction.’ The solution: Follow John Harbaugh | The Athletic “I feel really great about the situation, and I feel loose,” Harbaugh told me after a recent practice at the Greenbrier Resort’s Sports Performance Center, where the Giants spent the first two weeks of training camp. “You know, they tell the Marine snipers, ‘Stay loose, stay focused.’ You’ve got to be both. You can’t be focused and tight, and you can’t be loose and undisciplined.” As Harbaugh quickly clarified, those snipers confront stakes far more serious than anything the sport of football can throw at a head coach. “This is different,” he noted. “It should be easy to do it here.” 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates | ESPN.com The Giants’ biggest problem last season was their run defense. It was close to historically bad while allowing 5.3 yards per carry. It’s hard to succeed that way. New coach John Harbaugh is well aware. He and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson have made it a priority to stop the run this season. So far, so good. Veteran nose tackle DJ Reader has been a force in the middle throughout training camp. First-round pick Arvell Reese’s physical approach has been a major asset. That was again the case in live drills during Monday’s practice, which was the latest reminder that the Giants appear to have made serious gains on this front. “It’s just technique and mentality,” outside linebacker Brian Burns said. “We just really put an emphasis on being in our gap but also having … a mean mentality when it comes to the run. We’ve got some goals that we want to reach this year.” How Jaxson Dart’s training camp progress is showing up on and off field | The Record Jaxson Dart faked the handoff and rolled the other way on a naked bootleg, nothing but green grass between him and the first-down marker on a third-and-5 play during team drills. “Critical situations” is how Giants coach John Harbaugh termed it, and all Dart did was what he was supposed to do. Serby: Giants hopes completely hinge on Jaxson Dart taking second-year leap | New York Post Jaxson Dart rolled to his right and began scrambling. And when he slid for the first down inbounds by the right sideline, a cheer erupted from the defense. “I clapped,” John Harbaugh said and smiled. “I applauded.” Peter Schrager on John Harbaugh “Think about a country club, or somewhere really fancy, a nice five star hotel and resort and take the exact opposite of that. title: NY Giants to host CB with legal troubles on free-agent visit
summary: The New York Giants, who were without three of their top five cornerbacks at practice on Tuesday, will host former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold for a free-agent visit on Wednesday, a source confirmed. Arnold, a 2024 first-round pick by the Detroit Lions, was released on June 29. Arnold, 23, is facing eight felony charges stemming from […]
full_text: Terrion Arnold | Getty Images The New York Giants, who were without three of their top five cornerbacks at practice on Tuesday, will host former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold for a free-agent visit on Wednesday, a source confirmed. Arnold, a 2024 first-round pick by the Detroit Lions, was released on June 29. Arnold, 23, is facing eight felony charges stemming from allegations he orchestrated the abduction and beating of three men. The Lions released him after he was charged. The Associated Press summarized the reason for the charges against Arnold this way: In June, prosecutors in Florida said Arnold arranged for the men to be pistol-whipped after he wrongly suspected them of stealing $100,000 in cash and luxury goods from him. Police called him the “primary conspirator” in the February attack, and a judge set his bail at $1 million. According to Pro Football Talk , a conviction could result in a life sentence for Arnold. The legal troubles have not prevented NFL teams from looking into signing Arnold. He has already visited with the New Orleans Saints, Seattle Seahawks, and Houston Texans. Slot cornerback Dru Phillips, who has a knee sprain, has not practiced since late last week. Greg Newsome (knee) has been out of practice this week. Multiple reports indicate Paulson Adebo did not practice on Tuesday. The Giants have signed defensive backs J.T. Woods, David Long, and D.J. James during the past week.

Malik Nabers looking pretty good to me pic.twitter.com/OmT1xcX0Aj — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) August 11, 2026 Both Abdul Carter and DL Chauncey Golston returned to practice. QB Jaxson Dart likewise practiced after suffering a minor ankle injury on Monday. Practice reports Thomas Fidone II is heating up The second-year tight end made the play of the day for the offense, beating linebacker Tremaine Edmunds in coverage, reportedly laying out to snag a one-handed catch of a 40-yard pass from Jameis Winston . Fidone has been stringing strong practices together over the past week and is “catching everything in his direction” per Art Stapleton and Jordan Raanan . Arvell Reese is good It seems like we’re talking up Reese every day, but he’s giving us reason to on a daily basis. Whether it’s making plays in the run game, disrupting in the pass game, or busting into the backfield on a pass rush, he’s always showing up. Today he picked off Jaxson Dart in Red Zone drills, instinctively reacting to make a one-handed catch of his own, intercepting the pass as the offense tried to sneak a receiver (possibly Darius Slayton) behind him. ( Duggan ) The secondary is getting interesting Rookie cornerback Colton Hood might have gotten beaten by Darius Slayton on a double-move in Monday’s practice, but he had two pass breakups in one-on-ones against Malachi Fields and had good coverage of Isaiah Likely in Red Zone drills. ( Stapleton ) Safety Ar’Darius Washington is also continuing to show that he’s going to be a major piece of the defense. Dan Duggan reports that he once again split time with Tyler Nubin in team periods ( Duggan ). Modern “Ravens style” defenses make heavy use of safeties in sub-packages, and we’ll likely see a lot of Washington as one of the defense’s pivot players. Finally, safety Jevon Holland had an acrobatic circus-style interception off of WR Braxton Berrios , in which the ball bounced off of each player before Holland grabbed it out of the air. title: ‘Confident’ Darnell Mooney not worried about Giants’ WR depth chart
summary: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney has been around the NFL block enough times to know that worrying about where he fits on the team’s depth chaart at the position is pointless. “A lot of those things you can’t even control. You just got to go out here every day and just play your […]
full_text: Darnell Mooney | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney has been around the NFL block enough times to know that worrying about where he fits on the team’s depth chaart at the position is pointless. “A lot of those things you can’t even control. You just got to go out here every day and just play your game. Play your game, not worry about those things,” Mooney said. “When you start to worry about those things, it gets in the way of your mental capacity. I’m a big believer of God, and I feel like God is not worried. Once you start to worry, you don’t have the faith in God. Like I said, be where your feet are and just go play.” The Giants signed the 29-year-old Mooney to a fully guaranteed one-year, $3 million contract during the offseason. There are some who believe Mooney is competing for a roster spot. The view here is that Mooney is not competing for a 53-man roster spot, rather he is competing to see how high in the wide receiver pecking order he will be when the regular season begins. All of Mooney’s work during the team’s time in West Virginia came with Jaxson Dart and the first team, and it is hard to imagine the Giants would be wasting consistent first-team reps on a player who would not make the team. Mooney had 1,055 yards reciving on 81 catches for the Chicago Bears in 2021. He had 992 yards receiving on 64 catches for the Atlanta Falcons in 2024. A down 2025 season in which he had just 32 receptions for 443 yards left him needing to take a one-year deal from the Giants on the open market. Mooney dealt with a broken collarbone suffered on the first day of training camp last season, and a mid-season hamstring injury. “I feel like we go through stages in our life for reasons,” Mooney said. “As confident as I was last year, I felt like I was on top of the world. I felt like going into that year, I felt like it was just time to take over. “And then the first day of training camp, I break my collarbone again. Two times in one year. I mean, I can just be here. I can just be here in this moment and continue just to be in this situation. Be where my feet are and live in the day within the day. I’m excited about today.” Mooney said his role is “to make plays” on offense. “I feel like I’ve been doing well with that,” Mooney said. “My hands feel strong. I feel confident. I feel like I’m moving well, so everything’s going smooth.”

title: Survey: NY Giants vs. Vikings – What are you watching?
summary: Happy Game Week, New York Giants fans! That’s right, the New York Giants will be playing actual football this weekend. The Giants will host the Minnesota Vikings at 1 p.m. at MetLife Stadium in the first on-field action of the John Harbaugh era. Yes, it’s a preseason game and we likely won’t see much of […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants pass rusher Brian Burns sacks Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, forcing a fumble. | Getty Images Happy Game Week, New York Giants fans! That’s right, the New York Giants will be playing actual football this weekend. The Giants will host the Minnesota Vikings at 1 p.m. at MetLife Stadium in the first on-field action of the John Harbaugh era. Yes, it’s a preseason game and we likely won’t see much of the Giants’ stars, or the teams’ new schemes. But it’s still real, live football. This is also our first real opportunity to see the 2026 Giants in action. We’ll get to see how the arrival of a new coaching staff, off-season free agent additions, and draft additions have impacted the team. We’ll also get to see position battles play out on the field, with the opportunity for players to make real moves in live action. So then, we have a simple question for you this week: Which unit are you looking forward to watching the most? Do you want to see the offense? We might only see the vanilla foundations of the offensive scheme, but how do the Giants meld the input of former offensive coordinators Matt Nagy, Brian Callahan, Greg Roman, and Tim Kelly? Do you want to see how the offensive line is coming together? What the revamped receiving corps looks like? Isaiah Likely has been Jaxson Dart’s top target, so how do the Giants deploy him and Theo Johnson? Or maybe see the new-look running game? Do you want to see the defense? As with the offense, we’ll likely only see the fundamentals of the defense, but how does it differ from Shane Bowen’s scheme, or Wink Martindale’s for that matter? We’ve heard plenty about how disruptive the Giants’ hyper-athletic edge defenders and linebackers have been. Do you want to see the defensive line is being rebuilt without Dexter Lawrence? And what about the secondary? Is Deonte Banks for real? And how are Ar’Darius Washington, Tyler Nubin, Jason Pinnock, and Jevon Holland used? Or are you a real sicko who wants to watch the special teams? The Giants’ kicking competition has been one of the focal points of camp given that there’s three whole games worth of experience between Ben Sauls and Dominic Zvada. Not to mention, the Giants also have an undrafted free agent long snapper, which likely gives them the youngest and least-experienced battery in the NFL… Except for All-Pro and Pro Bowl punter Jordan Stout. There’s also the question of which players actually play on the Giants’ return and coverage units, and how they perform. That will be pivotal for how the bottom third of the roster is decided. This is expected to be a 2½-hour session in shells, rather than full pads. There are several injuries to note heading into Tuesday’s practice: Quarterback Jaxson Dart “got his foot stepped on” during Monday’s practice, according to coach John Harbaugh. This sounds like nothing to worry about. Abdul Carter missed Monday’s practice with a hand/finger issue. Harbaugh said Carter is likely to practice on Tuesday. Wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster is managing a knee issue. Harbaugh said the Giants knew they would have to deal with that when they signed him. Center John Michael Schmitz is in the concussion protocol. Backup center Lucas Patrick has what Harbaugh called an “old knee”, causing the team to manage his reps. Cornerback Greg Newsome worked on the side with trainers Monday due to an undisclosed injury. Harbaugh said Newsome would be “fine.” Nickel cornerback Dru Phillips worked with trainers on Monday. He has not practiced since suffering a mild knee sprain late last week. Wide receiver Jalin Hyatt suffered a knee or ankle injury. Harbaugh was not happy about the hit Hyatt took that led to the injury. “You can’t be laying out for a tackle in that situation,” he said. Did defensive lineman Chauncey Golston suffer a concussion when his head hit the turf on Monday? We should know today. What injury was guard Francis Mauigoa checked for? Again, we should get that answer on Tuesday. That is a long list. Nothing, though, long-term. Backup offensive linemen juggled With the injuries the Giants are dealing with, some shuffling was done with the backup offensive linemen on Monday. Per Dan Duggan : Rookie JC Davis got all of the second-team reps at LT for the first time with Marcus Mbow kicking over to RT. Josh Ezeudu slid into RG after spending the first 10 practices exclusively at RT. Aaron Stinnie and Daniel Faalele alternated at LG with Jake Kubas stepping at center. A few things of note there. Ezeudu at guard. That flexibility gives him a chance to stick on the 53-man roster, or at least the practice squad. Kubas at center. He has practiced there for the past two seasons. No surprise they turned to him with Schmitz out and Patrick limited. The right tackle work was probably good for Mbow. He has had little of that during camp. Come on back after practice for injury reports, a full practice report, and much more.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 11 of Giants training camp. What we learned from the Giants in West Virginia | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart & Co. are learning a new offense. This seems to be getting overlooked by many. The Giants are running an […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 11 of Giants training camp. What we learned from the Giants in West Virginia | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart & Co. are learning a new offense . This seems to be getting overlooked by many. The Giants are running an offense that merges input from Harbaugh (from Baltimore) and Matt Nagy (from Kansas City and Andy Reid) with Greg Roman’s intricate run concepts and Brian Callahan’s modern West Coast concepts. Dart is learning to play under center more than ever and alter his footwork. It’s a process. The coaching staff is learning what Dart & Co. do well. Dart is still learning and mastering the schemes and plays. It will take time. But at least the Giants’ offense feels it made progress throughout training camp, especially with its corrections. “You’re getting a big install each and every day,” Dart said. “So, you just continue to learn, continue to get reps at things and have a lot of really valuable communication.” As long as the Giants continue to improve as the summer progresses and wide receiver Malik Nabers returns soon (which is likely), the offense will be fine. The offensive line looks good. Colton Hood does a day in the life at training camp Colton Hood takes us through a day at camp! pic.twitter.com/wjDldZlT75 — New York Giants (@Giants) August 9, 2026 Giants depth chart analysis: Is CB Paulson Adebo losing grip on starting job? | The Athletic Cornerback continues to be unsettled, with four players getting first-team reps. This is my unofficial tally on who has taken the most first-team reps, in order: Greg Newsome II, Deonte Banks, Paulson Adebo and Colton Hood. Newsome has been steady on the outside and has gotten some work in the slot with Dru Phillips sidelined by a sprained knee. Banks continues to play better than he has in his first three seasons. Even though it’s a new coaching staff, there has to be some internal trepidation about relying on Banks after his past performance. That he has moved ahead of Adebo indicates how disappointing the big-money corner has been. Adebo has given up far too many completions in camp for a supposed No. 1 corner, and his standing on the depth chart reflects the coaching staff’s dissatisfaction with his play. Hood doesn’t look ready to be a Day 1 starter, which is fine considering the Giants will face the Cowboys’ and Rams’ high-octane passing attacks to start the season. Phillips has remained the starting slot corner, but he has split reps with Ar’Darius Washington depending on the situation. 1 Player Each NFL Team Should Put on the 2026 Trade Block This Preseason | Bleacher Report New York Giants: WR Jalin Hyatt. There’s simply no way that Nabers, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin III, Odell Beckham Jr., Isaiah Hodgins, Darnell Mooney, Braxton Berrios, JuJu Smith-Schuster, Ryan Miller, Beaux Collins, Jalin Hyatt, and rookie third-rounder Malachi Fields all make the 53-player roster. Of the receivers most likely to be cut loose at the end of the month, Hyatt is the one who could bring some sort of value back in a trade. The Tennessee product showed glimpses as a 2023 rookie, catching 23 passes for 373 yards and a 16.2 yards-per-catch average. While he’s largely disappeared since then, he’s still a former third-round pick with legitimate 4.4 speed who could interest receiver-needy teams. What’s next for Malik Nabers in return as he impresses at Giants camp? | The Record Malik Nabers is the best story of Giants training camp to this point, and it’s not even close. Now we will get the opportunity to see what the next chapter brings as the team takes the practice fields back home. And the Giants know Nabers will change the look of the offense the moment he steps into the huddle. title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Uar Bernard is showing some promise
summary: Today marked the tenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Wednesday. They’ll return to practice on Thursday morning at 10:00 AM Eastern. Then it’ll […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Uar Bernard #93 of the Philadelphia Eagles in action during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the tenth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES The Eagles were in full pads again today. EAGLES INJURY REPORT: IN-PRACTICE INJURIES: CB Quinyon Mitchell went to the ground after getting tangled up with Hollywood Brown in WR vs. DB 1-on-1 drills. Mitchell was slow to get up and spent some time on one knee with a trainer. He did not participate in team drills but he also did not visit the medical tent or leave the practice field early, so, those are some encouraging signs. OG Landon Dickerson visited the medical tent at one point but returned to practice. CB Tariq Castro-Fields visited the medical tent at one point but returned to practice. ACTIVE/PHYSICALLY UNABLE TO PERFORM EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) Prior to practice, Vic Fangio said the veteran edge rusher won’t be back on the field “for another couple weeks, at least.” DID NOT PARTICIPATE: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) Smith was doing some running prior to practice. Seems like he might be close to returning. WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder Fangio said that Jones is expected to “miss some time.” WR Johnny Wilson (knee) WR Danny Gray (concussion) S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) LIMITED PARTICIPATION LB Chance Campbell (groin) WR Britain Covey (hamstring) FULL PARTICIPATION OL Willie Lampkin left practice early on Monday but he seemed to be a full participant on Tuesday. RESERVE/INJURED RB Elijiah Mitchell RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large UAR BERNARD UPDATE: I know our readers like to hear about this guy, so, let’s start with No. 93 today. For the second day in a row, Bernard caught my attention for using his power to drive his blocker back into the quarterback. Today it was John Ojukwu who was pushed back towards Dalton. As expected, Bernard doesn’t have an array of pass rush moves at this point in time. But it’s cool to see how he’s already using his pure strength to his advantage. Really interested to see how he fares in Saturday’s preseason game, assuming he even gets snaps. JALEN HURTS UPDATE: More good than bad from QB1 today. THE GOOD: Hurts’ flashiest throw was an under-center play-action deep shot to Elijah Moore for a touchdown. Andre’ Sam was trailing behind the receiver. Moore celebrated his score by punting the ball onto the roof of the Jefferson Health Training Complex. Hurts ripped a good completion to Dontayvion Wicks along the left sideline to beat Riq Woolen. Hurts connected with Darius Cooper on a comeback along the left sideline to beat Woolen. Hurts hit Dallas Goedert in stride over the middle for first down yardage. THE BAD: Hurts got picked off by Quinyon Mitchell in 1-on-1s. Hurts failed to connect on a deep shot to Quez Watkins down the right sideline. Hurts had a short pass to Moore get knocked down by Jakorian Bennett. Thought it was notable that Fangio said Hurts is having a good camp. And the DC also spoke to how the offense is truly new. FANGIO: “Jalen’s having a good camp. He looks faster. Obviously, we can’t touch him during practice. There’s always that debate whether you had him or not. There’s been a few times where our guys think they had him and they really didn’t. He’s moving good and I think he’s doing a nice job with the new offense. A lot’s been made about him, all these coordinators he’s been with, but it’s basically been the same offense every year. This is different. He’s done a great job with it.“ The Eagles worked on a lot of run plays today. It’s not always easy to gauge those reps since there’s no tackling. But Saquon Barkley seemed to have some good runs, including when the offense was backed up against their own goal line. 1-on-1 WR vs. DB notes: Wicks caught a pass around Woolen … Moore beat Cooper DeJean … Hollywood Brown dropped a ball with Mitchell covering him … Hurts to Darius Cooper beat Kelee Ringo … Mac McWilliams had a nice breakup … Covey shook DeJean on an out route to get open for a completion … Erik Ezukanma roasted Castro-Fields deep and had the ball in his hands for a would-be diving touchdown catch but the ball popped out as he hit the ground … McWilliams had tight downfield coverage against Moore, who failed to track the ball in the air for an over-the-shoulder catch … Darius Cooper beat Woolen on an out … Andy Dalton dropped a pass in the bucket to Samari Toure to beat DeJean … Dalton threw a deep touchdown to Quez Watkins with Jakorian Bennett trailing … Darius Cooper made a good catch with his hands extended away from his body to pluck the ball in the air and beat Ambry Thomas. You may have noticed that Woolen lost a number of reps in today’s practice. I don’t think he’s had a bad summer by any means but, on the whole, he hasn’t looked as good as he did in the spring. He’s been most susceptible to getting beat on out routes and comeback patterns along the sidelines. DAILY DARIUS COOPER IS AWESOME REMINDER: Well, I already touched on a lot of the catches he made today. But this is your reminder in case you forgot. Also, Hurts was asked about how good Cooper can eventually be … and he said that Cooper is pretty good already. While I was watching the WR vs. DB 1-on-1s, OL vs. DL 1-on-1s were taking place multiple fields away. I did see Tyler Steen stifle Ty Robinson. It also looked like Drew Kendall had some good battles with Moro Ojomo. BGN alumnus Jimmy Kempski shared some more observations from those reps since he was focused on them. Ojomo got the better of Kendall during the rep where Hurts completed the deep ball to Moore. Quick pressure for a potential “sack.” Jalyx Hunt looked really fast while aiming to chase down a rolling Hurts from behind. Hunt was also in the area With Mitchell sitting out of team drills (and the aforementioned Jonathan Jones also injured), Mac McWilliams saw first-team cornerback reps. McWilliams has had an uneven camp but today was a good day for the second-year defender. He didn’t look out of place with the starters. Fangio talked him up a bit prior to practice. Q: Mac McWilliams, he’s done some nice things these last couple days. How different is he this year, year two, versus last year? … FANGIO: A lot different. He’s just matured. I’ve had a way of phrasing it to him that I really can’t say here, but he’s done much better. It’s been more than just the last few days. It’s been pretty much all camp and in the short offseason. With the backup offense backed up against their own goal line, Byron Young quickly got up the middle into the backfield to “sack” Dalton for a safety. Speaking after practice, Young revealed that his weight is down from where it was last year. He’s had a nice offseason to cement himself as DT4. Eli Stowers made multiple short catches in the flat. Nothing flashy but better to see him more active than not at all. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Today was Dalton’s day to be first up as QB2. Dalton apparently threw an interception to Cooper DeJean on the starting defense vs. backup offense field, which I didn’t see because I was watching the starting offense vs. backup defense field. Tanner McKee’s best throw was a well-timed anticipatory completion along the left sideline to a crossing Samari Toure to beat a diving Andre’ Sam. Dalton got off to a lead early in camp but McKee has been gaining on him recently. It’s still too close to call at the moment. Fred Johnson, not Markel Bell, worked at first-team right tackle again when Lane was not repping. Johnson also took some second-team right tackle reps with Bell working at second-team left tackle. During a situational drill, Bell reacted to A.J.…
