title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts looks “quicker and faster”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL training camp news, buzz, fantasy football updates – ESPNBest thing I saw/heard: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is looking like a viable dual threat again. The session I attended was a lighter day, but Hurts executed a designed run multiple times, and he looks as […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts #1 is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL training camp news, buzz, fantasy football updates – ESPN Best thing I saw/heard: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is looking like a viable dual threat again. The session I attended was a lighter day, but Hurts executed a designed run multiple times, and he looks as if he’s moving well. A team source agreed, noting Hurts looks “quicker and faster.” Hurts averaged nearly 700 rushing yards per season from 2021 to 2024, but that production dipped to 421 yards last year. The tush push isn’t going away, with new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion recently telling reporters the play is “extremely effective.” But based on early observations, I’m expecting Hurts to get to open space a little more often than last season, when he averaged around 6.5 attempts. Hurts says he feels as if he’s also making strides in Mannion’s passing game. He has doubled down on the details of the under-center offense, particularly the footwork. He says it’s all about sequencing and marrying the feet with the eyes. Mannion noticed that Hurts honed in on this particular area very early in the offseason, allowing the pair to then dig in on the big picture of attacking defenses. “In the end, you’re still playing the position, and you want to play the position the same way — play with your feet, sweep through your reads, know exactly where you’re supposed to go with the ball,” Hurts said. “[Know] where your alerts are, whether it’s down the field or whether it’s a man alert, just try and play fast. But that is more so just understanding what you’re doing, what we’re trying to attack, being on the same page and playing each play.” One observation from people here: The offensive operation is a little cleaner than it was last season. Going up against this stout Eagles defense every day requires that. Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Darius Cooper is undeniable – BGN DAILY DARIUS COOPER IS AWESOME REMINDER: Cooper was impossible not to notice today; I kept writing his name down over and over. Not a joke: I think he might’ve set a new franchise record for most catches by an Eagles player during team drills in a single practice. It began with back-to-back good receptions in 7-on-7. His success carried over to 11-on-11, where he got open on an out route to beat Riq Woolen. He made an over-the-shoulder grab down the right sideline with both Michael Carter II and Zack Baun trailing. Cooper also made a good adjustment while going to the ground to catch an off-target throw from Hurts late in practice. Put simply: good things happen when the Eagles throw the ball to Cooper. He’s proven himself to be a reliable option who gets open and catches the ball. Based on merit, I don’t know how one can argue he’s not a top three receiver on this roster right now. And if Cooper hasn’t already outshined Dontayvion Wicks, who is currently considered to be WR2, he’s pretty close to doing so. And that’s not a slight to Wicks, who’s looked good. If I’m the Eagles, I wouldn’t play Cooper much — if at all — in the preseason. He should be a real part of the offense this season. Hurts clearly trusts him, as evidenced by the quarterback shouting him out without even being prompted to do so. Eagles 2026 training camp practice notes, Day 9: Fight! Fight! – PhillyVoice Ty Robinson may have lost the fight, but he had a good day otherwise. On a two-play sequence he hit Jake Majors with his patented club move, getting free for a sack. Then he hit Majors with a bull rush that resulted in a pressure. Robinson had a slow start to camp — and it’s not as if Majors is Larry Allen — but he has come on of late. Eagles training camp: Darius Cooper shines, Quinyon Mitchell intercepts Jalen Hurts – The Athletic Cooper keeps making plays. (He could be in this diary on five different occasions. “80” is scattered on different pages in my notes.) Within a span of two minutes, Cooper caught an out route and then made an over-the-shoulder grab down the right sideline. He can run himself open, and he also makes contested catches. I was impressed by his ability to track the ball and make adjustments. There have been a few times when he had to come back for a ball or extend his body for a catch, and he has the control and spatial awareness to do so. I’m running out of ways to say that if you didn’t know the context — he was an undrafted player who had nine total catches last year — you’d think he’s one of the top receivers on this team. It’s why I asked coach Nick Sirianni how a player can “graduate” from a specific role — the “dirty work” receiver, in Cooper’s case — to a prominent role. “You graduate by trust and by consistently doing what you’re supposed to do and say, ‘Man, OK, we look at him as this dirty work guy, but man, he’s had opportunities in training camp to win on third down, and he has done that. Let’s give him those opportunities,” Sirianni said. “ Everything that we do is built on trust, and you get that through practice, you get that through meeting films, you get that through walkthroughs that you consistently do.” If Sirianni wants to see consistency, it’s showing with Cooper. ‘Extremely confident in myself:’ Can Jake Elliott rebound from 2 dismal seasons? – NBCSP Elliott has had a tremendous career. We all remember his clutch 42- and 46-yarders in the fourth quarter of Super Bowl LII in Minneapolis. We all remember his dramatic 61-yard game-winner vs. the Giants. And it’s impossible to ignore that he’s 28-for-29 in the postseason, 2nd-best in NFL history. He made the Pro Bowl in 2021 and was 30-for-32 in 2023. But he just hasn’t been the same guy the last couple years, although he has kicked very well this summer, going 19-for-20 on field goal attempts during team drills. “I’m extremely confident in myself right now,” he aid. “I feel like I’ve had a great offseason, I’m putting together a good camp. I feel like I’m striking the best I have in a while, and every day is a new day. title: ‘Hard Knocks’: Seattle Seahawks, Episode 2 recap, highlights, and what we learned
summary: If episode one of ‘Hard Knocks’ taught us anything, it’s that you should expect the unexpected with the Seattle Seahawks. From fullback Brady Russell getting peed on by who some would call the future team mascot in Buttercup the Goat to head coach Mike Macdonald using Phil Jackson’s legendary Chicago Bulls teams as a metaphor […]
full_text: If episode one of ‘Hard Knocks’ taught us anything, it’s that you should expect the unexpected with the Seattle Seahawks. From fullback Brady Russell getting peed on by who some would call the future team mascot in Buttercup the Goat to head coach Mike Macdonald using Phil Jackson’s legendary Chicago Bulls teams as a metaphor to emphasize how to build a continuous winning culture, it’s safe to say fans weren’t left empty handed . If you didn’t get the chance to tune in for episode two, I’d suggest you go watch it (and come back to this article later of course). For those who did, let’s dive into what we learned and have a look at who’s emerging as early candidates to be this year’s series stars. ‘Hard Knocks’: Seattle Seahawks, Episode 2 recap The episode opens with head coach Mike Macdonald scolding linebacker Derick Hall for bull rushing quarterback Sam Darnold. The first time he did it, Macdonald tried nicely, but after the second close call, he’d had enough. We’ll revisit this later. Comparisons keep coming, and the Seahawk machine is a good one. Otherwise known as a GPS guided robot used to repair the field, it’s much like the defending Super Bowl Champions — clean, precise and purposeful. Macdonald is working to prepare the defense for their first preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys on August 15, reiterating to the young guys there’s a lot coming ahead. Effects from wildfires in Canada and Eastern Washington trickled into the air during Seattle’s practices, but Sam Darnold doesn’t mind it — or so he says. But, that’s just the test coaches want, to see who’s going to be able to keep going. We’ve heard the hype surrounding second-year wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr., but man, it could be real. He made an unbelievable grab in the back of the end zone. Same goes for Elijah Arroyo, who ran a beautiful route for a touchdown. It’s the second “fight” we’ve seen in as many episodes, this time a quick scuffle between defensive end Rylie Mills and offensive lineman Mason Richman, with Mills throwing a punch at Richman’s face mask. Luckily for him, it didn’t quite escalate to that. Based on the reaction we saw from Macdonald in the series premiere after Hall chokeslammed Bryce Cabeldue, the situation wouldn’t have ended well for both Mills and Richman. Run game coordinator Justin Outten came up with with an interesting solution to resolving the beef: a sledgehammer holding competition. Richman and Mills squaring off to see who could hold two sledgehammers in the air longer had the team HYPED. Richman was good, but Mills was better and came out with the win. . @Seahawks players competed to see who could hold a sledgehammer the longest 😂 Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks airs tonight at 9pm ET on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/lI2IIn0lWR — NFL (@NFL) August 11, 2026 Some of the team bonding activities this team comes up with is truly hard to believe and really exemplifies the “12 AS ONE” mentality. San Antonio Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson swings by practice and is happily greeted by Macdonald, who invites him to his office to discuss leadership tactics. Hearing the way Johnson and Spurs general manager Brian Wright talk about Victor Wembanyama, you can’t help but be reminded of the way Jaxon Smith-Njigba conducts himself. Macdonald appears fascinated hearing the story of how Wembanyama found his way to San Antonio. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald and Spurs coach Mitch Johnson share leadership tips and talk Victor Wembanyama on Hard Knocks tonight 9pm ET on @hbomax . pic.twitter.com/yAyG8u2PZ9 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 11, 2026 “It’s rare for the best player in the game to also be the most so selfless, but the Seahawks were blessed with such a man,” says the soothing voice of Liev Schreiber. But the praise for Smith-Njigba wasn’t done there as wide receivers coach Frisman Jackson chimed in on the sidelined saying “he’s the only number one wideout I’ve been around where you can challenge him and he ain’t taking it personal.” It’s all fun and games for Smith-Njigba while talking with Jackson in his office, with the wideout even going as far as rage baiting his coach after he suggests more work on a play. But, he sees right through the reigning Offensive Player of the Year’s efforts. Their exchange ends in laughs and Jackson jokingly saying “They probably recording this, I was on record saying ‘Jax(on) dude, he’s a great guy we never have no arguments.” They were indeed. The attention shifts to Sam Darnold, who’s been throwing DIMES so far throughout training camp, and it’s largely in part to his spin rate of 639, which he leads all NFL quarterbacks in. Darnold describes himself as a “spin rate geek,” saying it all started with him laying on his bed and throwing the ball when he was young. Cooper Kupp describes how his mentality towards quarterback throws changed when he got to Seattle, previously believing it was more difficult to catch balls with too much too spin, but Darnold changed his mind. “You Spin Me Round” by Dead or Alive seems to be a the best way of explaining Sam’s passes. Any worry of a Super Bowl hangover seems a figment of the past as Darnold appears to pick up right where he left off with tight end Eric Saubert even going as to say “He’s so f—king consistent.” Another comparison comes to light with Macdonald attempting to instill the “Warriors in the Garden” mentality, enforcing the ability to play lethal and dangerously but also knowing when to unleash it. We then get a glimpse at the literal version of a warrior in the garden, Leonard Williams. His love for gardening is clear as he passionately describes his variegated Congo flower, showcasing a side we’ve never seen from the star defensive end. His passion for gardening reflects the peace that came with his move to Seattle, as his describes his love for the pacific coast. Despite being named “Big Cat,” Williams says he enjoys the peace, which has also been helpful for his wife and child, Zion, who Williams has high hopes for: “I want him to be greater than me one day,” he said jokingly. Then, Williams drops arguably the BIGGEST piece of news to come out of the episode. He said he contemplated retirement while playing on the east coast, where he spent the first 10 years of his career split between the New York Giants and New York Jets. Alongside Williams, Hall is certainly emerging as an early candidate to be a series star. DeMarcus Lawrence joked with him about last week’s fight to which Hall responded “I have not been fighting.” But, Lawrence didn’t end there. “You gonna fight everyone in the house … he really got little brother syndrome,” he joked as the pair laughed on the sidelines. However, the “little brother syndrome” bodes true to an extent as Hall describes how he was born a 2lbs premature baby given a 1% chance to live, hence the ‘1%’ chain for anyone who may have noticed. So while Hall may have built a monster truck which he described as “ain’t that hard, it’s just a bunch of nuts and bolts,” it all started from a stroke of luck when he was young. At practice, Macdonald screws up a play call and gives Hall the chance to try, saying “You can’t pull a Ron Burgundy,” but the linebacker couldn’t get the job done. Remember Macdonald’s outburst on Hall earlier? After the linebacker bull rushed Darnold, nearly hitting him, Macdonald wasn’t impressed and lost his temper after the second occurrence, taking him off the field. “Complain all the f—k you want, you’re too close, that’s twice!” However, the two hugged it out after practice and the situation blew over, as it seems most do with Seattle. Mike Macdonald doesn't mess around when it comes to protecting his QB. The new episode of Hard Knocks: Training Camp with the @Seahawks is available now on @hbomax pic.twitter.com/zsBfm7RRp8 — NFL (@NFL) August 12, 2026 Challenges like the sledgehammer holding competition appear common for Seattle, but none more iconic than the team’s shadowboxing. “We think shadow boxing…

title: ‘Hard Knocks’ goes behind the scenes of Seahawks’ Terrion Arnold tryout
summary: The second episode of HBO’s ‘Hard Knocks’ chronicling of Seattle Seahawks training camp and preseason had one very interesting nugget that remains an ongoing story for the Super Bowl champions. Former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold, currently facing several felony robbery and kidnapping charges, tried out for the Seahawks at the team facility at the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 30: Terrion Arnold #0 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Ford Field on September 30, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The second episode of HBO’s ‘Hard Knocks’ chronicling of Seattle Seahawks training camp and preseason had one very interesting nugget that remains an ongoing story for the Super Bowl champions. Former Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold, currently facing several felony robbery and kidnapping charges, tried out for the Seahawks at the team facility at the start of the week . While no signing is imminent and Arnold is slated to meet the New York Giants next, the ‘Hard Knocks’ crew does give us a revealing look into the Seahawks front office and their interest in Arnold. This comes shortly after they show Nick Emmanwori rehabbing his injured ankle, which obviously went well enough for him to be activated off of PUP . Aden Durde asked Mike Macdonald about Terrion Arnold Seahawks defensive coordinator Aden Durde : “Is there anything on that guy in Detroit, the one they cut?” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald : “John’s looking into it. He’s gone spy mode.” John Schneider conversed with Joey Schneider about Terrion Arnold Seahawks general manager John Schneider : “I’m trying to remember, like, with this Terrion Arnold thing, what would be another controversial signing that’s happened so we can kind of like understand that situation. Seahawks assistant GM Joey Schneider : Situations where someone has like an outstanding thing… John Schneider : Right, and then they’re signed and/or traded for—acquired, just acquired, you know what I mean? Joey Schneider : “Yeah.” John Schneider in sit-down interview: “We have 90 players here right now. We’re always kind of looking for what’s next. How do we get ready for a corner that’s not here yet? You know, like, guys that we’re going to need at a certain point. We want to be as strong and healthy as possible in December, January. John Schneider spoke to Jalen Milroe about his former Alabama teammate Schneider: “Last night I was talking about Terrion. I talked to Jalen [Milroe] about him.” Macdonald : “Oh yeah, what’d he say?” Schneider : “He was awesome. He’s got a buddy, a high school buddy. He’s like, ‘This place would be awesome for him.’ Just had a baby. His [wife/girl] would move up here with him. He’s just like [Devon Witherspoon]. “Joey [Schneider] thinks he is going to be able to play in the preseason.” Macdonald : “Sweet.” Episode ends with Terrion Arnold’s workout footage Arnold is seen working out in Seattle’s Renton headquarters facility. Among those in attendance are Mike Macdonald and Aden Durde. Macdonald can be seen shaking hands with Arnold at the end of the tryout, as the unmistakable tones of Liev Schreiber narrates the final line of Episode 2: “Mike Macdonald has questions: Will Arnold make the team better? And equally important, does he understand the culture and what Seattle is building?” The fact that this was the cliffhanger is compelling. Arnold has an arraignment hearing scheduled for Thursday, and even if the charges are dropped, he could still face an NFL suspension. However, he’s currently cleared to sign with any team and would be eligible to play in preseason. This only adds more intrigue as far as how genuine the Seahawks are about acquiring a recent first-round pick who’s had his early ups and downs on the field, and is facing serious trouble off the field.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 16: Robbie Ouzts #40 of the Seattle Seahawks gets set during the first half of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Inglewood, California. I can confirm that it is a neck injury that sent Ouzts to IR. https://t.co/by7EOVMpmV — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) August 11, 2026 Seattle signed former New England Patriots and Northern Illinois fullback Brock Lampe last week while Ouzts’ status was in limbo. Ouzts missed the NFC Championship win over the Los Angeles Rams and Super Bowl 60 against the New England Patriots with a neck injury suffered in the Divisional Round romp over the San Francisco 49ers. While he practiced throughout OTAs, minicamp, and the early stages of training camp, obviously this issue has flared up again. It is impossible not to think that Ouzts’ career is in jeopardy given the innate seriousness of neck injuries, and the Seahawks are no stranger to this. Mack Strong, Chris Carson, Kam Chancellor, and Cliff Avril all were forced into retirement with their respective neck injuries, so it’s absolutely reasonable to wonder what the future holds for Ouzts in terms of whether it is medically safe for him to continue playing football. Hopefully there will be good news for Ouzts’ health at some point, whether he returns to the Seahawks or not next season.

title: Seahawks, Broncos announce double throwbacks for ‘Thursday Night Football’
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos are turning Week 6 into a throwback party. Seattle announced Tuesday that it will wear its popular 1990s-inspired throwback uniforms when it travels to Denver for a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Broncos. The Broncos will also wear throwbacks, creating a rare double-retro matchup between two franchises with […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 08: Julian Love #20 of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass intended for Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter at Lumen Field on September 08, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Rio Giancarlo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos are turning Week 6 into a throwback party. Seattle announced Tuesday that it will wear its popular 1990s-inspired throwback uniforms when it travels to Denver for a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Broncos. The Broncos will also wear throwbacks, creating a rare double-retro matchup between two franchises with plenty of history dating back to their days as AFC West rivals. Thursday Night Throwback 📺 @NFLonPrime https://t.co/VRAVXJof8V pic.twitter.com/RZX2Vs4Zt3 — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 11, 2026 Seattle’s look will feature the familiar royal blue jerseys, silver pants and silver helmets, while Denver will go with its orange jerseys and blue helmets inspired by its 1977 team, which reached the Super Bowl for the first time in franchise history. And yes, Seahawks fans have already seen this matchup in these uniforms. Seattle wore its throwbacks for the 2024 season opener against Denver at Lumen Field, and Mike Macdonald’s first regular-season game as Seahawks head coach ended with a 26-20 victory. That game is one of the four wins Seattle has recorded in seven throwback appearances since the uniforms returned in 2023. The throwbacks debuted in 2023 against the Cleveland Browns, producing a memorable 24-20 comeback victory after Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored the go-ahead touchdown late in the game. Seattle’s other appearance that season came on the road against Dallas, where the Cowboys won a wild 41-35 Thursday night shootout. The 2024 season brought the aforementioned win over Denver before a 36-24 Thursday night loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Seattle then wore the uniforms three times during its Super Bowl-winning 2025 campaign. The results were mixed at first, with a 38-35 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, before Seattle bounced back with a 38-14 road victory over Washington and a 26-0 shutout of Minnesota. That brings Seattle’s overall throwback record to 4-3. Now, the Seahawks will get another chance to improve that mark in Denver. It’s also a particularly fitting opponent given that the Broncos were the team Seattle defeated in the first throwback game of the Macdonald era. There will be no shortage of nostalgia when these two teams meet under the Thursday night lights. The uniforms will look like the 1990s, but Seattle will be hoping the result looks a lot more like 2024 than some of its other throwback outings.

full_text: LAKE FOREST, ILLINOIS - JUNE 3: Coby Bryant #2 of the Chicago Bears stretches during a Chicago Bears OTA Offseason Workout at Halas Hall on June 3, 2026 in Lake Forest, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a mixed bag for injury news concerning the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday. The good news is that star defensive back Nick Emmanwori is off of the PUP list after passing his physical , but the bad news is that fullback Robbie Ouzts’ 2026 is already over after he was placed on season-ending injured reserve . There’s now a major update on a former Seahawks safety that has ramifications for both his new team and his old team. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Coby Bryant, who initially projected to be out 8-10 weeks after he was carted off with a knee injury during Chicago Bears practice, is now likely done for the entirety of the regular season after undergoing surgery. Bears S Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and now will miss 4-6 months. Bears are hoping he can return for the playoffs. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 11, 2026 It looked as if Bryant would be available for the Bears’ Week 8 Monday night trip to the Seahawks, but now it’s possible that the next NFL game Bryant plays is in the 2027 season. This is a big blow to the Bears defense, which has rebuilt its secondary and let both Kevin Byard and Jaquan Brisker walk during free agency. Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million contract with Chicago in March . Why Coby Bryant’s injury also hurts the Seahawks The upside to Bryant’s departure was the expectation of a 2027 compensatory draft pick. Per OverTheCap.com, this is how the compensatory formula works: Contracts are ranked via a Final Numerical Value based on the sum of points awarded as follows: An inverse ranking of the contract’s Average Per Year (APY) One point each for each percentage point of snaps played on offense or defense, with a minimum requirement of 25%. (Kickers and punters earn points based upon statistical performance.) 20 or 5 points based upon being honored by the AP All Pro or PFWA On Field Awards lists. Bryant’s contract in itself is going to give Seattle a comp pick, but if he misses the whole season then he will have 0 points assigned for snaps played, and obviously won’t have any points for AP or PFWA awards. This would downgrade Bryant’s projected comp pick value from a fifth (which is what is similarly projected for Kenneth Walker III and Riq Woolen) to a projected sixth, as explained by OTC’s Nick Korte. Obviously bad news for the Bears to not have Coby Bryant for the regular season. But there's also some bad news for the Seahawks, who could see one of their projected 5th round 2027 compensatory picks get demoted to the 6th round due to lack of snaps. https://t.co/zBnKvit6yF — Nick Korte (@nickkorte) August 11, 2026 If we’re going to rank severity of bad news, having a Day 3 comp pick drop 30+ spots is comparatively much tamer than the Bears losing their most expensive free agent signing, not to mention the personal devastation for Bryant after cashing in on a major pay increase. All the best to Coby as he recovers from surgery, and maybe he will be able to play again this season during Chicago’s stretch run.

title: Seahawks place fullback Robbie Ouzts on injured reserve
summary: After missing consecutive practices in the first week of training camp, concern surrounding Seattle Seahawks fullback Robbie Ouzts grew, and the worst case scenario came to fruition on Tuesday afternoon. The Seahawks announced they’ve placed Ouzts on injured reserve. Since this is preseason IR, Ouzts will not return this year. It remains unclear what injury […]
full_text: After missing consecutive practices in the first week of training camp, concern surrounding Seattle Seahawks fullback Robbie Ouzts grew, and the worst case scenario came to fruition on Tuesday afternoon. The Seahawks announced they’ve placed Ouzts on injured reserve . Since this is preseason IR, Ouzts will not return this year. It remains unclear what injury the second-year fullback is dealing with or how long he could be sidelined. When first asked about Ouzts’ situation on August 3, head coach Mike Macdonald indicated the team was looking into his situation , but hasn’t since provided full update. However, with the team practicing this afternoon, a clearer picture could soon come into focus. Although he participated in organized team activities (OTA’s), it’s worth noting Ouzts missed the NFC Championship game against the Los Angeles Rams and Super Bowl 60 against the New England Patriots with a neck injury. In a depth move, Seattle signed former Patriot Brock Lampe on Thursday , leaving him and Brady Russell as the lone fullbacks on their current roster. Ouzts missed Weeks 4-7 in 2025 with an ankle injury but finished the year logging two starts across 12 regular season appearances where he primarily served as the lead blocker. Seattle replaced Ouzts’ roster spot by signing inside linebacker Aaron Smith, who had a tryout with the Seahawks earlier in the week.

title: Seattle Seahawks release first unofficial depth chart of 2026 season
summary: It’s a Seattle Seahawks (preseason) game week, which also means we get to see the team’s first unofficial depth chart for the 2026 season. Ahead of Seattle’s preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, the Seahawks unveiled their 90-man roster in depth chart form. Have a look for yourself! A couple of things to note when […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 09: Quarterbacks Sam Darnold #14, Drew Lock #2, and Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks walk through the tunnel for warmups prior to the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lumen Field on November 09, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a Seattle Seahawks (preseason) game week, which also means we get to see the team’s first unofficial depth chart for the 2026 season. Ahead of Seattle’s preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys, the Seahawks unveiled their 90-man roster in depth chart form. Have a look for yourself! A couple of things to note when reading the Seahawks depth chart: Nick Emmanwori is now off of PUP after passing his physical , so this time next week the depth chart will look different. The unofficial depth chart was obviously finalized before Tuesday morning. If you want to know about ordinal ranking on a depth chart, read from left to right by row. For example, the cornerback room behind Devon Witherspoon would read: Nehemiah Pritchett, Shemar Jean-Charles, Michael Dansby, and Andre Fuller. Just in case it hasn’t been emphasized already, this is an unofficial depth chart, so don’t make too many grand declarations or worry about the fact that nearly all of the Seahawks rookies are buried in the back-end. That’s not uncommon for the Seahawks and probably not for many other teams. I can say that after a week of Seahawks training camp, and acknowledging that some players listed on here missed practice, that there’s a healthy set of accuracy attached to this depth chart. Pritchett and Igbinoghene have definitely had the bulk of the snaps with the ones and twos, and they look odds-on to make the roster. The running back room is very much a by-committee situation until further notice, so I wouldn’t read too much into Holani RB1 (especially once Zach Charbonnet returns). Logan Brown and Amari Kight, for example, have hopped between the second and third teams while working either tackle spot. Shaheed and Horton have worked with both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. Elijah Arroyo has had 11-on-11 reps with Darnold, Lock, and Milroe but obviously he’s much more of a receiving tight end in 12 personnel looks than Eric Saubert. The only eyebrow raiser to me is Rodney Thomas listed behind A.J. Finley, although in hindsight we’ve seen a lot of Finley and Maxen Hook with the second unit. There have been some three-safety looks in which Thomas is involved with the twos, so that competition is very tight. We’ll definitely have a better feel for Seattle’s depth chart—realistically, the non-starters—once preseason games get underway.

The team announced that second-year defensive back Nick Emmanwori, who began training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, has passed his physical. Based on the wording of the team release , Emmanwori hasn’t been formally removed from PUP, but it seems like it’s imminent. Update: As suspected, Emmanwori is off PUP. I have confirmation that this means Nick Emmanwori is off PUP. We will see if he is back on the practice field today or this week. https://t.co/NteUu8wqN9 — Brian Nemhauser (@hawkblogger) August 11, 2026 Emmanwori dealt with multiple ankle injuries last season, including a scare during Super Bowl week practice that ultimately did not keep him out of Seattle’s blowout win over the New England Patriots . title: Why Caedan Wallace trade could tell us about Christian Haynes’ trade value
summary: In looking at the Seattle Seahawks 90-man roster, one can quickly see the logjam in the offensive line room. A potential loser in this logjam could be former third round pick, Christian Haynes. Coming out of UConn, Haynes had big expectations as a rookie. Unfortunately he has yet to live up to those expectations. In […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - JANUARY 05: Seattle Seahawks guard Christian Haynes (64) walks off of the field after an NFL game between the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams on January 05, 2025, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In looking at the Seattle Seahawks 90-man roster, one can quickly see the logjam in the offensive line room. A potential loser in this logjam could be former third round pick, Christian Haynes. Coming out of UConn, Haynes had big expectations as a rookie. Unfortunately he has yet to live up to those expectations. In his first two seasons, Haynes struggled to see the field. He played as a backup throughout his rookie 2024 season despite optimism that he would be able to beat out oft-criticized right guard, Anthony Bradford, for a starting role. Entering 2025 there was hope that new offensive line coach, John Benton could bring out the best in Haynes. Haynes once again entered 2025 battling Anthony Bradford for the starting right guard position. However, Haynes still never seemed to truly be in contention for that starting spot. The competition became so lopsided that Haynes was even getting snaps at center to see if he could be an option there as well. Haynes ended up missing nine games in 2025 due to a pectoral injury. At the 2026 NFL Draft, Seattle drafted offensive guard, Beau Stephens. Adding Stephens to the room along with second year interior linemen, Bryce Cabeldue and Mason Richman, has caused the optimism around Haynes to fully fade away. At this point, if one were to look at the roster math, it would not be far-fetched to think that Haynes is in serious danger of not making the 53-man roster. That’s where a recent AFC East trade becomes fascinating. It was announced that the New England Patriots have traded their own 2024 third round pick, Caedan Wallace, an offensive guard, to the Miami Dolphins. Wallace was selected 68 th overall by the Patriots, just 13 spots ahead of Haynes (81 st overall) . The Patriots were able to receive a 2028 6 th round pick in exchange for Wallace and a 2029 7 th round pick to the Miami Dolphins. Could this be a potential framework for a Christian Haynes trade before the start of the season? Wallace appeared in 10 games in his two seasons with New England, earning a 72.9 overall PFF grade for 2025 (although that is incomplete as he only played eight snaps in 2025). In contrast, Haynes has played in 24 games in his first two seasons (including all 16 his rookie year). In 2025 Haynes earned a 43.9 overall PFF grade (although he also has an incomplete grade with only 32 offensive snaps played). Overall, Haynes, like Wallace, is a former third round draft pick who has underwhelmed at offensive guard in his first two seasons. Often in cases like these there may be another NFL team who would be interested in trading for the player if they had a high grade on them entering the NFL draft. The Dolphins trading for Wallace is a perfect example of this. Could Haynes, who was heralded as one of the top guard prospects in the 2024 NFL draft, potentially get some love from other teams? If Wallace could garner a trade package (albeit small), it stands to reason that Haynes could fetch a similar type of day three draft pick swap or conditional draft pick compensation for Seattle as well.

title: 49ers News: Sounds like the joint practice was LIT
summary: Fred Warner de-escalates fiery, fight-filled 49ers-Titans joint practice“The 49ers had two notable plays on back-to-back snaps highlighted by plays from defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa and safety Ji’Ayir Brown. Odighizuwa supplied pressure up the middle and grabbed a handful of Titans quarterback Cam Ward’s jersey as he ran past. The Titans did not take kindly to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 04: Fred Warner #54 of the San Francisco 49ers juggles softballs while working out during training camp at SAP Performance Facility on August 04, 2023 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fred Warner de-escalates fiery, fight-filled 49ers-Titans joint practice “ The 49ers had two notable plays on back-to-back snaps highlighted by plays from defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa and safety Ji’Ayir Brown. Odighizuwa supplied pressure up the middle and grabbed a handful of Titans quarterback Cam Ward’s jersey as he ran past. The Titans did not take kindly to Odighizuwa touching their quarterback during the joint practice. On the next play, Brown sniffed out a Ward throw over the deep middle for an interception. The Titans were unable to connect down the field against the 49ers’ defensive backfield.” Fred Warner drops eye-popping praise about ‘sticky’ 49ers defensive backs “The way they’re playing, sticky in coverage, playing the ball in the air, being able to play the run game or the ball thrown the flat, the ability to tackle, I think it’s one of the best I’ve seen thus far,” Warner said. “I’m really excited about what I’m seeing. We just got to continue to jell and mesh that thing together so it’s the best version for when that time comes.” Fred Warner, 49ers’ pass defense stand out in heated session with Titans’ Cam Ward (paywall) “ But the bulk of Ward’s completions came on screens and short throws, and his best opportunities deep down the field couldn’t be hauled in by his receivers. He was twice flushed from the pocket by third-round rookie Romello Height. On another play, Ward forced a throw to Wan’Dale Robinson in tight coverage, allowing safety Ji’Ayir Brown to step forward and pick off the pass. That play also ended in a brief dustup involving cornerbacks Green and Upton Stout. During the ensuing delay, Warner walked from the sideline to the east end zone, raising both arms to pump up the crowd. After all, it’s been a while since he’s been able to do that. “That’s why I love joint practices,” he said afterward. “You really have an opportunity to work on your craft and really see where your team is….I don’t know if I’ve felt that confident in that part of the game as I feel right now,” he said. “That’s not a knock on any team that I’ve played with before. But I think this group is kind of meshing together, playing together, sticky in coverage, playing the ball in the air. … I think it’s one of the best I’ve seen thus far. I’m really excited.” 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates “I had Purdy at 21-of-27 on the day, including multiple touchdown passes and no interceptions. His best throws came in a move the ball sequence in which he dropped a perfect ball between three defenders to rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling that would have gone for a long touchdown. And then, he had another layered throw over linebacker Cody Barton for a big gain to TE Jake Tonges.” 49ers’ Nick Bosa has knee tendinitis after ACL recovery, per Kyle Shanahan “Just soreness, tendinitis,” Shanahan said. “It’s a pretty normal thing with ACLs. Talking with our guys (medical staff), it happens with about 90 percent of the guys we’ve had.” How the 49ers’ defense looks different under Raheem Morris “The goal, not unlike coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense, is to utilize personnel groupings that make everything look the same before quickly transforming into something else. Through the first two weeks of camp, three young 49ers — second-year linebacker Nick Martin and rookies Jaden Dugger and Romello Height — have emerged as the top candidates for the job. Each has done one of those jobs well over their career, but they’re trying to add other tools to their belt throughout camp. It’s why Dugger spent some time at a recent practice with the defensive line, working to hone his pass-rush moves. And it’s why observers have seen Height take reps dropping into coverage. Martin has also occasionally lined up as the fifth defender on the line of scrimmage during team periods in this camp. Linebacker coach K.J. Wright said the winner of that competition, which he says is still wide open, won’t claim the job just based on physical attributes. They’ll have to prove they can handle the workload that accompanies so many responsibilities. Hence the position’s name.”

title: 49ers-Titans joint practice roundup: Brock Purdy continues to shine
summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Tennessee Titans held a joint practice in Santa Clara on Tuesday. We’ll round up a bunch of tweets and react. According to everybody in attendance, there were at least eight scuffles, with most of them coming in the first ten minutes of action. Fred Warner said, “No, I promise,” when […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 07: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after his team's win in the NFL 2025 game between San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Amanda Loman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers and Tennessee Titans held a joint practice in Santa Clara on Tuesday. We’ll round up a bunch of tweets and react. According to everybody in attendance, there were at least eight scuffles, with most of them coming in the first ten minutes of action. Fred Warner said, “No, I promise,” when asked if the defense intentionally picked fights. Warner added, “We’re not going to get through today if we continue on this path. I think we kind of found our groove after that fiery beginning.” Depending on whose timeline you look at, both teams won the day. Things did not start out well for the 49ers defensively: Embarrassing start to practice for the 49ers defense. They haven’t made a play, and they are instigating scuffles after nearly every whistle in their joint practice against the Titans. — Matt Maiocco (@MaioccoNBCS) August 11, 2026 Things got chippy early. Renardo Green, Upton Stout, Fred Warner, and Dre Greenlaw were all involved. Green allowing a reception early was the trigger: Renardo Green just popped Carnell Tate after Tate made a catch on an deep out. Both teams got into it. — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) August 11, 2026 Props to the 49ers pass rush The group, sometimes with help, generated plenty of pressure on Ward, who was under steady fire in the latter sections of practice. Ward said it was good work against pressure, real-game situations and some scramble drill. But as things settled down, the 49ers’ pass rush had their way. This is from longtime Titans reporter Paul Kuharsky’s recap: In Turron Davenport’s post-practice notes, he highlighted Alfred Collins having a sack, and multiple edge rushers from the 49ers being disruptive. That’s noteworthy, knowing Nick Bosa is out. It shouldn’t be news that Osa Odighizuwa was making plays. He’s supposed to do that. It is news when the role players and depth are contributing, as that wasn’t the case last year — or the year before, for that matter. Here’s more about the pass rush from Jim Wyatt from Titans dot com : One issue that troubled Ward and the offense was the offensive line’s inability to protect at times. There were 49ers in the face of Titans QBs on several occasions in practice as the team worked through a number of different combinations, for one reason or another. We should point out that the Titans lost their top two left tackles, Dan Moor Jr. and Austin Deculus, after they were ejected from practice after the first series. That could be part of the reason the Niners had so much success. Strong in the secondary Upton Stout, Ji’Ayir Brown, and Jakob Robinson had interceptions. Renardo Green had a couple of pass breakups. One Titans reporter was recapping a play and said, “Green simply had Ayomanor blanketed and there was no chance at a completion.” Stout’s interception came on an overthrow when Tate was wide open. So we should put an asterisk next to that turnover. Even after drafting Carnell Tate, nobody is going to confuse the Titans wideouts with, say, a team like the Bengals or Cowboys. But you still have to go out and make plays. The 49ers didn’t just do that today, but they also finished. That’s been a massive issue for years. Fred Warner had strong praise for the secondary. He said he’s never felt as confident about a secondary heading into the season as he has with this one heading into 2026. While that could be the typical teammate talking up his teammates, it was unprovoked. Hey, rookie Titans reporters were impressed with Fred Warner and his ability to diagnose. That’s nothing new. What is is Jaden Dugger. He saw reps with the starters when they went to 5-man fronts. That’s good news for Dugger, and not so much for Nick Martin. Dugger has the build you want for a linebacker playing on the line of scrimmage. And if there’s any motion or a tight end flexes out into the slot, he has the athleticism to walk out and still hold his own. It’ll be fascinating to see how he’s used and how Dugger’s role evolves this season. Warner said Dugger has a “rare” skill set and can “run like a deer.” He’s a rookie, so mistakes are inevitable. But if Dugger can mix in enough splash plays to outweigh the bad while he works his way to being consistent, the base defense should be stout. He’s not the only rookie linebacker making a name for himself. Larry Worth is working his way into becoming a practice squad player at the very least. If he shows enough special teams value, perhaps Worth can unseat one of the veterans for a final roster spot. Raise your expectations for Brock If you are in the belief that Brock Purdy is among the best quarterbacks in the NFL, then it should only be news if Purdy has a bad day. Everything else is expected. So when you see tweets like, “Purdy hits Stribling in stride,” the reactions should be, “Yeah, that’s what he’s supposed to do.” I’m referencing the Titans’ beat to avoid as much bias as possible. They had Purdy throwing only four incomplete passes. When I see something about Demarcus Robinson making plays, whether it’s in the red zone or at the intermediate portion of the field, my mind goes to, “Brock threw him open.” Brock gave Robinson way more credit after practice: “Yeah. I think he’s just one of the best receivers that I’ve played with in terms of the one-on-one matchup and his feel for the game. We’ll have something drawn up like, ‘Hey, the receiver needs to get this many steps and be here on time,’ but sometimes there’s situations where you cut it off short or you push up into a guy a little bit longer and then get out of the cut. Like, he has a good feel for the game when it comes to that. He’s played for a while. He’s got a lot of savviness to him. And obviously in the red zone, he’s got length, he’s got just the ability to go up and get the ball. So, obviously I learned a lot about him last year, but this offseason, watching film on him, it’s like, all right, we can give this guy more ops and have him be a huge part of our offense. He’s had a great camp. He’s been out there every day showing up, making plays and catches. Today against the Titans too. Same thing. So, I’m really excited for him.” Robinson will likely be viewed in a different light playing alongside Mike Evans and De’Zhaun Stribling. Speaking of, all eyes will continue to be on Stribling, who caught a team-high seven passes during team drills. Reporters are almost shocked that the Niners have a receiver who catches the ball without fighting it and continues to run without breaking stride. Not to pick on him, but there’s a vast difference in the way Stribling catches the ball compared to Deebo Samuel — who is lining up in the backfield more and more with the offense missing its top four backs. More importantly, they had the Titans defense generating little pressure. That’ll be a concern so long as we don’t know who the left guard is. That’s Robert Jones, for now. It might be Carver Willis. It could be Connor Colby. Better question: Does it matter? The other four starters are all a little better than average at worst. One player who gets lost in the sauce and might play a bigger role once the season begins is Jake Tonges. The 49ers might not want to spread things out if the offensive line cannot hold up or the wideouts cannot separate. Even if George Kittle is inactive early on, two-tight-end sets might be their best path for success. Tonges reportedly caught multiple passes downfield, which is noteworthy. A tight end is a quarterback’s best friend. Kyle Shanahan said the tight end groups have done a good job so far during camp. He also mentioned that Tonges can do all of the things Kyle Juszczyk can. The 49ers have their TE2 on the roster. It’s a matter of whether they use…

title: Kyle Shanahan isn’t concerned about Nick Bosa and Christian McCaffrey’s injuries
summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided updates about some of the team’s top players. Nick Bosa has missed several practices in a row after dealing with some soreness. No concerns about Bosa or McCaffrey’s injuries Shanahan said it’s nothing more than that: “Just soreness. Tendinitis. It’s a pretty normal thing with ACLs. Just […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided updates about some of the team’s top players. Nick Bosa has missed several practices in a row after dealing with some soreness. No concerns about Bosa or McCaffrey’s injuries Shanahan said it’s nothing more than that: “Just soreness. Tendinitis. It’s a pretty normal thing with ACLs. Just talking to our guys, it’s happened to about 90% of the guys we’ve had, so it’s a normal thing. We have to be smart here from week to week. No concerns about it being any more than that.” According to reporter James Palmer, the tendinitis Bosa is dealing with stems from his first ACL injury back in high school on his right knee.. There’s a similar lack of concern for Christian McCaffrey on Shanahan’s end: “No. My concern would be him toughing through tightness, like a lot of people do. Then hurting something bad, and pulling something. Then it could be a month. That would be our concern. So once we hear him talking a certain way, Christian’s a guy who needs to get prepared for Week 1. But also, we’re pretty confident in what he’s done before this, and what he’s done in these two weeks. We just want to make sure it’s not something we’re concerned about. Honestly, I think everyone goes through this. When you have vets who know how to get ready for Week 1…lots of guys have this stuff, and you need to push through it. He’s not a guy who needs to do that. It’s pretty simple with us.” Shanahan explained how De’Zhaun Stribling is in a different situation than McCaffrey, as the rookie needs the reps: “It’s been good to get him back. We were excited to, some of that stuff he did the first week. Then you know, he had some tightness and stuff, similar to Christian. Then we took him off for, I think, a week. I want to guess; I think this was like his fourth day back. I just love him getting the reps. We love his talent. We love the character and just how he plays. It’s such a different situation than Christian. We need to get him ready to play an NFL game. It takes a while for rookies to do that. So I want him ready for Week 1. So it’s been really good to get him back, the way he attacks each day. Each day he’s got better and better. Hopfeully, he doesn’t have any injuries, so he can continue getting those days in for Week 1. And if he does, feel real confident about him.” Too early to call the battle at left guard Shanahan said that it’s too early to say whether Robert Jones has taken a step forward in the left guard battle: “It’s open for anybody. Those guys will probably be the lead at it. Love to get Carver [Willis] in that, too. Him missing a week or whatever it was with his concussion made it out of him a little bit. But he’s been out two practices in a row. It’s still early, but we want to see those guys in games too. It’s definitely a battle for us to see who gets that spot.” Don’t expect to see starters on Thursday Shanahan said the team has made a decision about who will play during Thursday’s preseason game against the Titans, but they haven’t told the players: “There won’t be many starters playing. We’ll see with injuries today and stuff. That doesn’t mean none. But we’ve got to balance that out.” Robert Saleh is taking a different approach. He said everyone will play.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Renardo Green offseason work included talking to former All Pro cornerback
summary: When it comes to the San Francisco 49ers and their secondary, it looks like it’ll be much of the same in 2026, as the 49ers brought back each of their five starters while electing not to make any significant additions in the room. At cornerback, the 49ers are projected to start Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 11: Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers defends during the NFC Wild Card playoff game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The 49ers defeated the Eagles 23-19. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images When it comes to the San Francisco 49ers and their secondary, it looks like it’ll be much of the same in 2026, as the 49ers brought back each of their five starters while electing not to make any significant additions in the room. At cornerback, the 49ers are projected to start Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green on the outside again, with Upton Stout in the slot. At safety, the competition is ongoing, but Ji’Ayir Brown, Malik Mustapha, and Marques Sigle figure to be the top options there as well. San Francisco didn’t get the best results from its secondary last year. A part of it was the tough environment, as the 49ers’ pass rush didn’t do them any favors. But they also didn’t see the growth they had hoped for from Green, who was inconsistent and even benched at times, or the safety room. Green is a different person than most would imagine a cornerback to be. He’s quieter, rather than brash, and that can play into one’s mentality at the position. But he’s grown this offseason, according to new defensive pass game coordinator Jerry Gray, who came with Raheem Morris from the Atlanta Falcons this offseason. “Well, to me, I don’t think Renardo looks around in the room and say, ‘okay, I got to raise my game,’” Gray said. “I think Renardo understood that, you know what, I’m going into my 3rd year. What did they expect out of me? The expectation was high. And it’s different when young guys really don’t understand that, hey, you coming into an organization that’s used to winning. You step on this field, they expect you to be the best in the league. And then now I think he understands that. So it really doesn’t matter about Jack [Jones] or anything like that. I think that adds to it. This offseason, Green did a lot of work on his own, which included talking to former NFL cornerback Xavier Rhodes, who was a first-team All-Pro corner with the Minnesota Vikings and went to Florida State, where Green went to school as well. “There’s competition there, but I think Renardo had his agenda that, ‘hey, I want to go out there and I’m going to prove to the guys that I can go out there and play at a high level,’” Gray continued. “And then he took it out on himself. To me, he understands guys that I’ve kind of coached. He talked to guys like Xavier Rhodes and stuff like that in the offseason. They went to the same university. What do you get? What information are you going to get? How can Jerry teach you to be better? “And mostly it’s about the mental part of the game. With Renardo, you got the athletic ability, you got the talent. Hey, take the mental part of the game, put it with your athletic ability, and you’ll be really good. He’s going through rookie stuff right now, you know. It’s like, okay, where do I fit in? What am I supposed to do? He’s really quiet, so he really doesn’t talk a lot. So you have to kind of watch his body language and, you know, bring him in sometimes. We always have a lot of extra stuff, time for rookies, and that helps him a lot because now he can ask the questions that he won’t ask in front of everyone else.” The defensive back room has a ton of different personalities, which also means that each individual player is receptive to a different style of coaching. Cornerbacks coach Ray Brown has learned that about Green, figuring out the different ways to push him while keeping his confidence up. “I think it’s one of those things, you have to understand the individual,” Gray said about his cornerback room. “If you understand the individual, you understand what works for each individual person. I can’t say anything to Renardo. I’m gonna let Renardo just go do his thing. But there are ways that I can poke at Demo (Deommodore Lenoir). There are ways I can poke at Stout. But I think every guy is different. “Like if I said something to Renardo, he’s gonna say, ‘man, that doesn’t work for me.’ And he kind of laughs, but when he laughs, that does keep him loose so he can go play. I think it’s just, as a coach, you have to do a great job of understanding your players. I think you have to understand you can’t coach everybody the same way. So once you get a great understanding of them, you understand how to coach them. One, you have to care. I think that’s a big thing. And I think, I don’t care what level you’re at, I think you have to care. If you don’t care about your players, man, I don’t know why you do it. At the end of the day, life is about relationships. “In 20 years, those dudes should be able to call me and say, ‘hey, this is what I’m going through, or this is how life is going, you have any advice?’ If they can’t call me, I really didn’t do a great job. And so I think you do have to care. They have to know that you care outside of the football field. But once you get an understanding of them, what works for them, what doesn’t work for them, I think it elevates their play because you understand how to coach them. “Everybody’s different, just like everybody’s play style is different. If we go out there and we look at their press style, everybody’s going to be a little different because it’s catered to that person. And so once you understand that person, then you can kind of work, you can tweak some things, and you know how to motivate them, which honestly you don’t really have to motivate this group. But we all need to have great self-talk. I think those guys It’s kind of one of the things that Jerry [Gray]’s brought to the room is really the self-talk from each— from themselves, but also we can add in on those things. But as you get to understand a person, you understand kind of what they need in those moments, and you also understand when to leave them alone.” The results will have to come on the field, but it feels like the process has been a bit different for Green, who is attacking the offseason more as he understands the expectations and importance of having a good Year 3. He’ll be a vital part of the 49ers secondary as the team looks to get back to being a top 10 defense in the NFL after some mixed results in 2025.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers release their first unofficial depth chart for the preseason opener
summary: The San Francisco 49ers released their first unofficial depth chart ahead of their preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans. Fans aren’t interested in seeing the starters, according to our FanDuel Sportsbook poll from last week: That’s not too surprising. We don’t need to see players in August. We need to see them in January. Risking […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 12: Connor Colby #75 of the San Francisco 49ers blocks during an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers released their first unofficial depth chart ahead of their preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans. Fans aren’t interested in seeing the starters, according to our FanDuel Sportsbook poll from last week: That’s not too surprising. We don’t need to see players in August. We need to see them in January. Risking an injury or any type of aggravation makes little sense. Here’s a look at the depth chart that was released and put together, courtesy of the 49ers communications staff: Let’s start at wide receiver, in an attempt to break up how each player is being used. The depth chart has Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and De’Zhaun Stribling in the same cluster. At practice, amid the current injuries, those are the three wideouts on the field together. Robinson lines up at “X” with Mike Evans out. Deebo is at “Z” in place of Ricky Pearsall, while Stribling is mastering “F,” which is in the slot. Things can change in a hurry. A few weeks ago, we were debating whether or not Robinson would make the roster. A slew of injuries have made him a lock. The fight for the final spot(s) will be intriguing. Will one of the undrafted free agents make a name for themselves? Can Malik Turner find his way onto the roster once again? August is a big month for the wideouts. Equally as important is who is catching passes from which quarterback. Junior Bergen’s arrow is pointing up. The same cannot be said for Jordan Watkins, who is playing with…Adrian Martinez. As for the offensive line, we hardly knew ye, Connor Colby. The 49ers were always going to lean on a veteran at left guard. It’s Robert Jones’ job to lose. Carver Willis is doing a little bit of everything between playing both guard spots and center. His head might be spinning. Realistically, he’s going to soak up as much information as he can from Jake Brendel and take over for him next year. We also thought most of the competition would be on the defensive side of the ball. Reports have Sebastian Valez taking a step, but that feels eerily similar to last season. He’d have to beat out some quality undrafted free agents, or one of the draft picks from the past couple of seasons. I’ll believe it when I see it — aka, when Valdez isn’t going against Austen Pleasants or one of the Niners’ third-stringers. My pick is Bryson Eason, who would be in the mold of Alfred Collins and C.J. West, as the Niners continue to emphasize stopping the run. Eason is 323 pounds with an 85th percentile broad jump. You’re not moving him. It sounds like Jack Jones is a shoo-in to make the roster at cornerback. If that’s the case, Nate Hobbs might be on the outside looking in, unless the team wants to punt on rookie Ephesians Prysock. Jones is the kind of cornerback to intercept a pass on one possession and give up a 60-yard play on the next. Consistency has always been his issue. I’m interested to see how creative Raheem Morris gets with the secondary. He’s already worked Deommodore Lenoir at nickel. If that’s the case, will we see Upton Stout take reps at safety during the preseason? If the goal is to put your best five players in the secondary on the field, and you are confident that Jones can give you more than Ji’Ayir Brown, why not roll with a Renardo Green, Jones, Lenoir, Stout, Marques Sigle secondary?
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Trent Williams promises 49ers’ rookie De’Zhaun Stribling will be a ‘player’
summary: ESPN’s Dan Graziano spent a day at the San Francisco 49ers’ training camp and spoke to Trent Williams after practice. Williams explained how last year’s success injected even more confidence into the locker room: “I think that year did so much good for us, just in the belief and the culture and in the locker room. Because […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Trent Williams #71 of the San Francisco 49ers speaks with the media after a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images ESPN’s Dan Graziano spent a day at the San Francisco 49ers’ training camp and spoke to Trent Williams after practice. Williams explained how last year’s success injected even more confidence into the locker room: “I think that year did so much good for us, just in the belief and the culture and in the locker room. Because that’s what won games, was the culture. It wasn’t the players. For so long we’ve heard, ‘Aw, y’all got seven All-Pros, seven Pro Bowlers, that’s why y’all win.’ And then we do without all those guys, and we still find ways to beat really good teams and work our way into a playoff win. And yeah, once [George] Kittle was out, it was pretty much curtains, but what is there not to believe in?” If the report about Kittle returning as soon as Week 1 is accurate, confidence should be sky-high heading into the season. It seems as though the 49ers are being overly cautious with their injured core players, like Christian McCaffrey, Nick Bosa, and Mike Evans. The latter two missed all of last week. Speaking of Evans, that’s who Williams believes will be the biggest benefactor on offense: “I think Mike Evans is going to be the biggest benefactor for us. Just because you can’t have your safeties keyed in on filling the gaps. Because you can’t leave him 50-50, you can’t leave him one-on-one. And that’s the one thing that this offense in my opinion didn’t do as much, was attack downfield. Now, with the receiver room we have, and having the threats we have, I don’t know if you can just have everybody zero in on Christian [McCaffrey]. [Evans] is a guy that, you basically have to play him with two. He’s going to occupy two sets of eyes, 50-50 balls aren’t really 50-50. And he’s a deep threat, he’s always been that. Just one of the more dynamic receivers in the league.” Last year, teams had their safeties inching closer and closer to the line of scrimmage, without fear of the Niners’ perimeter threats running by them. It shrunk the field and made life a living hell for McCaffrey, both on the ground and in the running game. The 49ers didn’t have a receiver who could consistently win on isolation routes last year. It’s a different story heading into 2026. And Evans isn’t the only one who has that skill set, either. Williams, like just about everybody else, has been in awe of rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling: “He’s going to be a player. I promise you that. He’s like Jauan [Jennings], same body type, but he runs 4.3. And his 4.3 speed shows in the game. His acceleration, it shows every time he touches the ball. And I think he’s going to be a guy who, early, he’ll get off fast when people aren’t planning on stopping him and stuff, and then once he’s jotted down as a real threat, then it opens up everything else, too.” Stribling is playing the same position as Jennings, but the usage isn’t similar at all. A couple of times a week, we’re hearing about how Stribling got behind the defense for a long touchdown. I’m not sure if that ever happened with Jennings during camp.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Report: There’s a ‘high level of confidence’ that George Kittle plays in Week 1
summary: We are less than a month away from the season opener for the San Francisco 49ers, and the injury bug has been hitting the team hard in training camp. At times over the last few days, there have been 20 players out of practice, forcing the team to continuously work out other players and sign […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 11: Demarcus Robinson #5 and George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrate during the first quarter of the NFC Wild Card playoff game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are less than a month away from the season opener for the San Francisco 49ers, and the injury bug has been hitting the team hard in training camp. At times over the last few days, there have been 20 players out of practice, forcing the team to continuously work out other players and sign more camp bodies. But it’s not only players getting hurt during camp. The 49ers have a good contingent of guys working their way back from injuries sustained earlier in the offseason or from last season, such as George Kittle, who tore his Achilles in the playoffs back in January. Since the offseason began, it hasn’t been fully clear when Kittle would be ultimately available to play. He’s a 32-year-old tight end coming off a major injury, and there wasn’t any need to rush him back throughout the offseason. But, as the offseason has gone on, it’s seemed like the star tight end has continued to progress well and hit his benchmarks, although he’s still working his way back to being 100 percent on the field. Well, on Monday evening, CBS Sports’s Matt Zenitz reported that Kittle’s recovery progress had been ‘terrific’ and that the team expects him back on the field in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. “49ers star tight end George Kittle continues to make terrific progress working back from the torn Achilles he suffered in January and there’s a high level of confidence at this point that he’ll end up being able to play Week 1 vs. the Rams,” Zenitz wrote in a tweet. Kittle had started training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list, as he and several other 49ers worked back from significant injuries. With this current timeline, he would be back on the field eight months after sustaining the torn Achilles, which is quite impressive in itself. ESPN’s Nick Wagoner reported that Kittle had done his most ‘extensive’ practice work on the side yet during Monday’s practice, noting that he seemed to be moving quite well. “One notable thing from before practice: TE George Kittle did the most extensive side work we’ve been able to see so far in this camp,” Wagoner tweeted. “He was running routes, catching passes and doing some conditioning. Seems to be moving quite well as he bounces back from Achilles injury.” Things seem to be trending up for the 49ers star tight end heading into Week 1.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers News: Camp highlights are cool… Now do it against TEN
summary: 49ers guard Dominick Puni wondered if he’d peaked. Then he found a fix (paywall)“A coach tells you, ‘Man, if you keep doing that, you’re probably not going to get away with it much longer,’” Puni said. “But if it’s working, in my head, you’re just going to keep doing it. It’s hard to listen when […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 21: Robert Saleh and head coach of the Wildcats FFC, Kyle Shanahan look on during the Fanatics Flag Football Classic at BMO Stadium on March 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images for for OBB Media - FANATICS STUDIOS) | Getty Images for for OBB Media - 49ers guard Dominick Puni wondered if he’d peaked. Then he found a fix (paywall) “A coach tells you, ‘Man, if you keep doing that, you’re probably not going to get away with it much longer,’” Puni said. “But if it’s working, in my head, you’re just going to keep doing it. It’s hard to listen when something’s working.” Once defensive tackles began beating him, the message landed. Puni embraced Foerster’s coaching and reversed his slide. “I found something later in the season, attacked it in the offseason and worked with coach Foerster,” Puni said. “We’ve been getting better at it ever since. I feel a lot more comfortable knowing I have a technique I can go to.” 49ers-Titans joint practice sets up clashes with Cam Ward, Robert Saleh and an All-Pro DT (paywall) “Morris and his sticky corners soon face their first true test across from blue-chip wide receiver Carnell Tate, whom the Titans drafted No. 4 overall out of Ohio State. Tate, the first wideout taken in April, reportedly caught three touchdowns passes in a given practice over the weekend. The quarterback throwing to him, of course, was Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick last April. The 49ers have a competitive cohort of cornerbacks. They make plays and let you know about it. Tuesday will be a telling clash. “Every now and then, I’ll try and poke at them to see if I can poke the bear … it kind of gets them going,” defensive backs coach Ray Brown said.” Aloha, Mr. Hands: 49ers cornerbacks dissect De’Zhaun Stribling’s strong start (paywall) “I would say him just catching away from his body, just kind of trusting his hands,” Lenoir said of Stribling’s strength. “He’s got that catch radius where he’s gonna catch it away from his body. He’s got strong fingertips.” ….Lining up at the F or slot position has created regular matchups with Stout, who’s also having a strong camp. He and the other cornerbacks have more license to play aggressively this year, which suits their styles and has led to plenty of tipped passes and incompletions in the middle of the field. That close coverage has vexed receivers like Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins, with Watkins in particular having an issue with contested catches early in training camp. But Stribling has looked confident with a cornerback or safety draped over his back. “He’s going to be a dog,” Stout said. Rising coach on 49ers’ staff? Former Seahawk K.J. Wright “Saleh says linebacker coaches need to know the entirety of the defense, the importance of communication and how pass rush and coverage work together, which gives them a leg up on other defensive coaches aiming to become coordinators. He calls it a “global understanding” that can be hard to gain from other positions. When Saleh left the Niners the first time in 2021, Ryans was the easy choice to replace him. If Morris, who has been a head coach twice, gets San Francisco’s defense back to previous levels, it’s not out of the question he could get another opportunity in the coming years. For now, Wright says he is only thinking of his current job and not the future.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 10 of 49ers Camp: McCaffrey Out with Tightness “Every day, Dugger bats down a pass in this drill. He’s a work in progress, but he already shows so much potential in coverage, which makes sense, considering he’s huge and a former safety.….All things considered, that’s a good day for Purdy. He’s working with a bunch of backups he barely knows, and he’s still playing well.” Undrafted rookie wide receiver Will Pauling vying for role with uncertain 49ers “The 49ers demand that their receivers are willing and effective blockers, and Pauling has turned heads. “No matter if he’s going up against a D-end, a linebacker, or a DB, he’s been sustaining blocks,” Hankerson said. “And that shows up a lot.” Pauling had 155 receptions for 1,753 yards and 15 touchdowns in his 48-game college career that began at Cincinnati in 2021. At the very least, he appears to be a strong candidate to stick around on the 49ers practice squad. But that is only if he does not make the 49ers’ regular-season roster or another team does not claim him.” Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak shares updates ahead of 49ers-Titans preseason game “San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke with reporters after Monday’s training camp practice as the team gears up for its preseason game against the Tennessee Titans. Here’s everything he had to say.” 49ers bubble watch: One rookie whose job is in jeopardy “On Monday morning, the Patriots released offensive tackle Caedan Wallace, a third-round pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. Wallace’s rookie year was derailed by an ankle injury that landed him on the Injured Reserve. He’s played sparingly through two seasons and will look for a fresh start. If you’re the 49ers, you see the fourth pick of the third round two years ago. He’s 6’5”, 314 pounds with hand size (90th percentile) and broad jump (96th percentile) that you covet. The 49ers’ depth is so depleted that they are using Austen Pleasants at guard and have a forever camp body in Brandon Parker at tackle. One man’s trash is another man’s treasure, and in this instance, a player like Wallace could be just what the team needs to upgrade. During August, there may not be draft “busts” like Wallace available, but there will be plenty of different talents who could make the Niners think twice about Cruz Jr. Or at the very least, bring that player in to give one of the backups, like Cruz Jr., a run for their money.”

full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - JUNE 17: Head coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans speaks before the second day of minicamp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center on June 17, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. Robert Saleh said after today’s joint practice that all healthy Titans players will play in the game. He said the plan is for the starters to play more than one series. Saleh said early on that he planned on the starters playing in every preseason game. That makes sense with a whole new coaching staff trying to implement a new system on both sides of the ball. The players need all of the live reps that they can get. It’s part of the reason that the Titans are doing joint practices with all three of the teams they are playing this preseason. The plan is also for all four quarterbacks to play on Thursday night. I’m interested to see how Will Levis and Hendon Hooker look in comparison to each other. My guess is that neither one of them end up on the 53-man roster in week one, but I do wonder if we will be able to see a big difference in them on Thursday.
