title: 2026 NFL training camp news, buzz, fantasy football updates
summary: Here's what we heard on the road at training camp for the 49ers, Bengals, Bills, Browns, Cowboys, Eagles, Jets, Raiders, Ravens, Seahawks and Steelers.
full_text:
NFL training camps are underway ahead of the 2026 season , and Jeremy Fowler, Dan Graziano and Ben Solak have been on the road for their respective annual camp tours. We had updates from their first 12 stops last week , and now we're sharing nuggets and notes from visits to the 49ers, Bengals, Bills, Browns, Cowboys, Eagles, Jets, Raiders, Ravens, Seahawks and Steelers over the past seven days.

 At each camp stop, Jeremy, Dan and Ben talked to players, coaches, executives and scouts to get the latest buzz. We compiled everything they saw and heard, including some nuggets that might be important for fantasy football managers.

 How are quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley looking in the Eagles' new offensive system? Are the 49ers veterans worried about all the preseason injuries? Is the plan still for the Raiders to start Kirk Cousins over Fernando Mendoza ? And could the Steelers have one of the best defenses in the league? Here's what we learned for each team on our most recent visits.

 

 
 Jump to a team's camp notes: 
 BAL | BUF | CIN | CLE | DAL | LV 
 NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF 

 
 

 

 Fowler's notes from Seattle Seahawks camp 
 Dates visited: Aug. 7 
 Location: Renton, Washington

 Best thing I saw/heard: This new offense is brimming with camp optimism. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has impressed one of the league's best defenses by "dialing it up," per safety Julian Love .

 "We think they have our script, pretty much," joked Love, noting the timely playcalling mixed with pre-snap adjustments from savvy veterans such as wide receiver  Cooper Kupp and quarterback  Sam Darnold . "They know what we're in. They were on our ass the first few days [of camp]."

 The Seahawks will have two tight ends on the field "very, very often," according to tight end  AJ Barner . That position will help facilitate the motions and shifts, a staple of the San Francisco offense from which Fleury came.

 Wide receiver  Rashid Shaheed  should also be a major factor in 2026. Love said his "blinding speed" has been a problem for the defense all camp, and though Shaheed primarily lines up on the outside, he's also moving around. He was spotted in the backfield during one portion of a Seahawks practice last week. Wide receiver  Jaxon Smith-Njigba 's heavy workload should continue after he accounted for 36% of the targets last season, but Shaheed having a full offseason in Seattle makes him a more viable option in the intermediate parts of the field -- not just deep.

 One thing Fleury did early in the offseason that coach Mike Macdonald liked: He "doubled down" on the fundamentals and how Seattle played stylistically before implementing the full scheme.

 

 "That really resonated with me," Macdonald said. The end result is an offense with the "same bones" as last season under Klint Kubiak but has "a little more variation in the running game," per Barner.

 One key fantasy nugget: The running back rotation will feature "two, possibly three guys in a game plan," Macdonald told me, starting with the preseason. That muddles the fantasy picture a bit. But Jadarian Price will be hard to keep off the field. Macdonald says Price "doesn't feel like a rookie" based on his attention to detail and coachability.

 "He's an impressive guy," Macdonald said. "It will be fun to see him in a game."

 Love says Price's burst is "like a prime Dalvin Cook ." And Barner added that Price has a knack for following the "track" that blockers create.

 Seattle likes to spread the wealth at tailback ( Kenneth Walker III  averaged 13 carries per game last season). George Holani and  Emanuel Wilson  are steady veterans who should be factors early, and Macdonald says he thinks  Zach Charbonnet ( torn ACL ) is getting closer based on how he looks in workouts. But Price's profile should only grow as we approach September.

 Best of the rest: 

 
 Championship messaging permeates the Seahawks building. Barner said a team room that once featured a picture of the Lombardi Trophy has been replaced with the mantra "12 is 1." Macdonald said the Seahawks staff wasn't trying to send a message with that change and just thought it "would look cool." But he has stressed that winning a Super Bowl is something to cherish and hard to replicate -- but what his players can replicate is the team's "way of life" and "going to work with your boys" every day. 
 The Seahawks say safety/big nickel Nick Emmanwori has a chance to return in Week 1 from offseason ankle surgery , but that's not a certainty at this point. Defensive back D'Anthony Bell is expected to step into a bigger role, though Macdonald says "everything is on the table." That means a cornerback, safety or linebacker could fill that spot. Love says Emmanwori is a "unicorn" -- Seattle can't perfectly replace him. Second-round safety Bud Clark could fill in at one of the safety spots in Seattle's three-safety package, and the team is hoping to get third-round corner Julian Neal back from a leg injury in short order. 
 Barner is an ascending tight end who should come into his own in Year 3. He's finally healthy after multiple offseason surgeries. And Fleury's offense should accelerate his progress. Barner can do a little bit of everything. But he made a point to emphasize another tight end when asked about up-and-comers on the roster: Elijah Arroyo . "Tremendously talented player," Barner said. "Year 2, you get more comfortable." Those two will be working off of each other a lot in 2026 as a strength of the offense. 
 The Seahawks' receiver dynamic is interesting, as the coaches are excited about Tory Horton now that he's healthy after cracking his tibia last season. Kupp will remain a factor with his football IQ and rapport with Darnold, and team officials say they feel as if he's moving well at age 33. Expect Seattle to mix and match to find enough snaps for both Kupp and Horton. Really, Smith-Njigba is the only player who won't come off the field much. 
 General manager John Schneider said he knew the Seahawks couldn't bring back everyone from the Super Bowl roster, losing several key players to free agency. And with limited draft capital in April -- the team entered the draft with four picks but left with eight -- Schneider acknowledges Seattle had to emphasize its needs more than it probably wanted. The team drafted players it loves at positions it had to backfill, such as running back and defensive back. The Seahawks also had pass rush high on the list, though they ultimately didn't fill that spot. Schneider says the 2027 draft frees up his staff to prioritize good players regardless of position, as Seattle is projected to have 12 picks next April. He will also keep close tabs on his offensive line. Even though Seattle has a good core there, it wants to maintain strength at that position. Schneider says he feels Seattle didn't do enough of that after the first Super Bowl win a decade ago: "We're a little more cognizant this time with that."

 Dates visited: Aug. 7 
 Location: Rochester, New York

 Best thing I saw/heard: I started scratching out this note about halfway through practice when I realized just how many players were taking first-team snaps with the Bills' defense, this isn't complete. But aside from the obvious starters, here's my noncomprehensive list of players who took at least one "starting" snap last Friday for Jim Leonhard's defense: Javon Solomon , DeWayne Carter , Kaleb Elarms-Orr (a lot of excitement for the fourth-round rookie linebacker), Kani Walker , Sam Franklin Jr ., Phidarian Mathis , Keonta Jenkins , Jordan Hancock , Geno Stone  and  Zane Durant .

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Buffalo Bills' camp is taking place at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, and Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. We will update this file often. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday, Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 The Bills wide receivers room is a popular topic of conversation. While DJ Moore 's connection with quarterback Josh Allen has been a camp highlight, it was Joshua Palmer who stood out with a couple of nice grabs in Tuesday's practice.

 Palmer's first season with the Bills was disrupted by injuries, especially a left ankle injury, but the receiver said he is now feeling much more comfortable. Getting significant, and reliable, contributions from players such as Palmer would be big for Joe Brady's offense.

 "I don't have to question any of my movements," Palmer said. "I don't have to think before the route. I don't have to ... I'm not stressed before I go on the field. I just go out and play."

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said that he thinks the plan is for starters to play in the preseason opener Saturday but that it is TBD how much they will play. "It's gonna be exciting for guys to get out there and just kind of let it rip," Leonhard said. Leonhard said tackling is a big evaluation piece for the defense in the game, noting that getting offensive players to the ground and finishing plays was an "Achilles' heel" in Buffalo last year. 
 Rookie DT Zane Durant returned to practice, but a number of starters were still not participating. Among those not practicing are safeties C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop and center Connor McGovern . Cornerback Maxwell Hairston was doing some work on the side. The team has not disclosed injuries. 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford continues to be a camp standout. On Tuesday, he intercepted Allen for the third time in camp with a jump on a ball that was intended for receiver Keon Coleman . Alford said that he adjusted the call based on what they saw on film. "[Allen is] the best quarterback in the league, MVP. So ... any time you can catch an interception from him, man, it just shows what type of defender you are." 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Injuries were the theme of the day as the Buffalo Bills held their first training camp practice at the team's facility in Orchard Park, New York.

 Several starters did not participate, including safety Cole Bishop , cornerback Maxwell Hairston and center Connor McGovern . Also not taking part were running back Ty Johnson , wide receivers Skyler Bell and Ja'Mori Maclin , defensive tackle Zane Durant , defensive back D.J. Miller and punter Mitch Wishnowsky .

 The team did not disclose the nature of the injuries.

 Starting safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who missed two practices with a right calf strain, also left practice early after falling to the ground while making a pass breakup in the end zone. Athletic trainers looked at his right leg. He eventually walked to the locker room on his own.

 Practice was held inside the Kaleida Health Performance Center as rain and lightning once again threatened.

 More observations: 

 
 Veteran Lloyd Cushenberry III continued to work with the first-team offense at center in place of McGovern. 
 Top camp standouts include tight end Keleki Latu and cornerback Kani Walker . 
 Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame ceremony Saturday. He was there in support of Drew Brees, whom he coached in New Orleans. "It was really special," Carmichael said. "Special moment. It was great to see not only Drew and Coach [Sean] Payton but the whole group of guys that had come out just to be there on his behalf." 
 

 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 On Saturday night, the Bills held their annual "Return of the Blue and Red" practice at Highmark Stadium. It was the Bills' first football activities in their new $2.1 billion home.

 The official welcome featured plenty of fireworks, quite literally.

 One of the biggest came during a two-minute drill, when quarterback Josh Allen found wide receiver Khalil Shakir , as he darted past safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson  and twisted his way into the end zone. Moments later, Allen joined him in the celebration by sliding into the end zone.

 As coach Joe Brady described it, "Josh throwing an unbelievable play to Khalil."

 The night went smoothly, outside of a brief downpour midpractice, and players later marveled at the arena.

 "Wow," tight end Dawson Knox said. "... I got here four hours early. I was just walking around on the field, taking myself on a little tour around everything, just kind of looking at all the details and just taking it in, because it still doesn't feel real yet. ... It's the coolest place I've ever played football in."

 More observations: 

 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford had a nice interception off Allen. The defense made a show of celebrating the pick, even being a bit late to get to the next play. 
 RB Ty Johnson went down during one-on-one drills with a right leg injury. He was helped off the field by athletic trainers and did not return to practice. 
 Starting center Connor McGovern also was injured on the first play of 11-on-11 drills. He returned to play, but then needed further attention from athletic trainers, who were looking at his right leg. McGovern then walked off the field and did not return. Lloyd Cushenberry III filled in for him (outside of a brief appearance by Sedrick Van Pran-Granger ). Brady did not have an update on McGovern or Johnson after practice. 
 Cornerback Maxwell Hairston missed a second straight practice because of an undisclosed injury. Rookie DT Zane Durant , P Mitch Wishnowsky , DB D.J. Miller and WR Mac Dalena also did not participate. 
 The punting job remains Tommy Doman Jr .'s to lose. With Wishnowsky out, Doman punted and held for kicker Tyler Bass , who made all eight of his field goal attempts. The rookie had one fumble, but otherwise a solid day. 
 Rookie undrafted free agent CB Kani Walker  continues to be a surprise in camp. 
 

 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Bills wrapped up training camp at St. John Fisher University with a shorter practice in pads.

 Quarterback Josh Allen said one of his takeaways from the time away from Buffalo is how close the team has gotten.

 "This group from offense to defense is the tightest knit group that I've been around really since I've entered the league," Allen said. "The defense is meshing so well together. Just even when you walk in the dorm room or walk in the cafeteria, guys sitting down, talking, really getting to know each other. 
 
"There's just a lot of love on this team and that'll show on the field."

 Allen pointed to the veteran leadership new OLB Bradley Chubb brings as well as the growth of two-time captain ILB Terrel Bernard  in helping the team get to where it is.

 The Bills now head back to Orchard Park, New York, and camp practice starts with the first football work in the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday night.

 Other observations: 

 
 Two defenders took trips to the medical tent during…

title: 2026 Chicago Bears training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bears training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Chicago Bears ' camp is taking place in Lake Forest, Illinois, and Bears reporter Courtney Cronin has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bears camp. We will update this file often. Will the defense step up and lead the Bears back to the NFC North title? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bears news 
 
 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 Aug. 11 
 Tuesday's practice was about "creating evidence" for the coaching staff to be able to evaluate where players stand in specific roles and who is climbing their way into the 53-man roster.

 "Up to this point, it's been a lot more get the plays in, let's get them repped once or twice and now they can actually execute and go out there and play ball," coach Ben Johnson said. Coaches sent out a game plan Monday night for players to study in hopes of seeing who could play fast and adjust to not knowing what was coming their way.

 With the offense and defense having 98% of their installs in, the 11th practice of camp opened with focusing on short-yardage goal line team drills to build the intensity and competition that Johnson envisioned carrying over to the rest of practice. The starting offense dominated that period with chunk runs from  D'Andre Swift  and Kyle Monangai , who each scored. In the first move-the-ball period, Swift got loose and found his way down the right sideline for a 62-yard TD.

 Quarterback Caleb Williams  and the starters aced a tough test towards the end of practice with the offense backed up at its own 1-yard line. The goal for the drill was to get two first downs, which Williams accomplished by creating space to find Rome Odunze for a 50-plus yard catch-and-run followed by a big gain to Scotty Miller .

 Both the first and second-team offenses weren't as crisp in the situational drills at the end of practice, but Williams exited practice feeling confident in his ability to adjust on the fly and stack strong practices throughout the first two weeks of camp.

 "I just I want to keep getting better for the guys," Williams said. "I want to be faster with my process, to be able to help the O-line throughout you know long games and things like that, they're sitting in their stances, be able to get the communication throughout, you know whether it's on the ball or whether it's in the huddle, just be smoother and faster and everything so that I can be better for the guys and ultimately that helps us win."

 More observations:  

 
 Johnson dropped a major injury bombshell before practice and announced safety Coby Bryant will be out four to six months after undergoing knee surgery. According to that timeline, the Bears would hope for a Bryant return in the playoffs. 
 While the Bears are being cautious with  Luther Burden III 's groin injury and holding him out for the rest of the preseason, Johnson expressed optimism about left tackle Ozzy Trapilo , who is recovering from a ruptured patellar tendon. Months ago, Bears' brass thought they might not have Trapilo at all in 2026. Now, there's a chance, according to Johnson, that he could return at the end of training camp. 
 Safety Cam Lewis returned to practice for stretching and individual drills but went inside during 11-on-11. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson had a solid day and may have thought he came away with an interception (the officials did not call the play dead despite the ball touching the ground) but was not on the field for the final period, as he was replaced by Malik Muhammad . 
 Jedrick Wills Jr . and Kiran Amegadjie both got reps with the first-team offensive line, but it's hard to tell who is separating themselves in the left tackle competition between the two. Braxton Jones remains out after getting injured last Thursday. 
 The Bears practiced a fire-drill field goal, which went wide ride (44 yards). Cairo Santos connected on kicks of 43, 48 and 53 yards during the field goal period. 
 Williams and the starters had another clean practice with no turnovers while the backup units accounted for three turnovers. Linebacker Devin Bush picked off Tyson Bagent , who also threw an interception to Skyler Thomas on the final play of practice. Roschon Johnson was popped inside the 1-yard line by DB Dontae Manning , and linebacker Jon Rhattigan recovered the fumble. 
 

 

 
 Aug. 9 
 Practice No. 10 of training camp -- the Bears' fifth in pads -- moved indoors after a lengthy lightning delay and opened with physical, downhill run drills. D'Andre Swift has looked terrific through the first two weeks and was seemingly everywhere Sunday: in the run game, passing game and taking a direct snap during 11-on-11 reps.

 Swift picked up two big runs as the Bears repped their four-minute offense at the end of a two-hour session.

 Luther Burden III missed practice because of a groin injury and is expected to miss "a little bit of time," according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. In Burden's absence, Jahdae Walker had back-to-back solid practices and hauled in the best catch of the day from Caleb Williams on a busted-coverage deep ball.

 Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen worked in his dime package and emphasized blitzes/different pressures in 11-on-11 reps. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson , who battled through injury during Saturday's practice, picked off Williams' pass on an out route to Rome Odunze .

 In addition to Burden, the Bears were also missing Cam Lewis , Montez Sweat , Braxton Jones , Jaylon Jones , D'Marco Jackson , Terell Smith and Coby Bryant .

 Rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas appeared to injure his knee during 7-on-7 drills. He left practice with a trainer and did not return.

 Other observations:  

 
 Kiran Amegadjie got first-team reps at left tackle. The Bears continue to rotate Amegadjie and  Jedrick Wills Jr . at left tackle with the ones, twos and threes and have yet to get Theo Benedet in the mix. 
 Allen said he didn't think Lewis' injury would sideline the DB for long but did not have a timetable on his return. Lewis was injured Saturday as the Bears repped an end-of-game situation toward the end of practice. 
 Newly signed DB Xavier Woods filled in for Lewis at safety opposite rookie Dillon Thieneman . Woods laid a heavy hit on Colston Loveland over the middle and made a strong impression on his second day with the Bears. 
 Linebacker Ruben Hyppolite II had his best practice of training camp. He has been getting more reps in Jackson's absence. 
 The long-snapper competition appears to be over. Luke Elkin was waived Sunday before practice, leaving Beau Gardner as the sole long snapper on the 90-man roster. 
 Malik Muhammad continues to get a sizeable workload at nickel with the first-team defense. With Jaylon Jones sidelined and Josh Blackwell seemingly behind Muhammad on the depth chart, the rookie has stood out to coaches and shown signs of being able to hold his own at one of the most difficult positions for a young player. "The biggest challenge you've got is you got a big bull's-eye on your back and they're [opposing quarterbacks] going to be challenging you," Allen said. "They're going to be coming after you. The best corners have really short memories because everybody at some point in time has been beaten, and so it's just can you come back the next…

title: 2026 Cincinnati Bengals training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Cincinnati Bengals ' camp is taking place in Cincinnati, and Bengals reporter Ben Baby has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bengals camp. We will update this file often. Will Dexter Lawrence II spark a defensive resurgence to get the Bengals back in the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bengals stories 
 
 Joe Burrow, Bengals find camaraderie on unusual battlefield 
 Bengals DE Stewart out multiple weeks with hyperextended knee 
 Bengals' top storylines at training camp 
 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Expect to see Cincinnati's stars in the preseason opener on Thursday. QB Joe Burrow , WR Ja'Marr Chase , WR Tee Higgins and DT  Dexter Lawrence II  will see some snaps in the home game against the Lions, coach Zac Taylor said.

 "[Fans will] get a chance to enjoy some of our players there," Taylor said. "But how long I keep them out there remains to be seen."

 Last year, Burrow played in a career-high 21.2% of the team's preseason offseason snaps, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The effectiveness was hard to gauge since Burrow suffered a turf toe injury on Week 2.

 
 After the first 30 minutes of practice, Cincinnati had to shift indoors following a massive storm that rolled in. It looked like a scene out of a tornado movie. 
 The Bengals had just one team period. There were some mixed moments for the offense. But the secondary had another good moment when safety Jordan Battle had an easy interception for a potential TD ball intended for Chase. 
 Rookie center Connor Lew took snaps with the first-team offense as veteran Ted Karras received a bit of a breather. 
 Those who are confirmed out against Detroit: S Bryan Cook , CB Dax Hill , TE Erick All Jr . and Lew. Cook and Hill are battling injuries and will continue to be evaluated next week. 
 DT B.J. Hill (PUP) and DE Shemar Stewart (hyperextended left knee) are making good progress to returning to play, Taylor said. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Chalk it up to a good day for the offense. The first-team unit had some good moments on a Sunday afternoon that featured two extensive move-the-ball drills. One of them ended with a corner touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Tee Higgins . The running game also had some moments, which is a good sign for an offense looking to find bigger gains on the ground.

 

 
 Bengals safety Bryan Cook and cornerback Dax Hill did not practice. Both have been battling muscle tightness in recent days. The indication on Cook, who suffered his injury in the team's Friday night practice, is that his issue is nothing significant. 
 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Cincinnati wants to find bigger gains in the ground game in 2026. There was a healthy amount of that in the limited portion of practice that was inside Paycor Stadium on Friday night.

 Running back Chase Brown reeled off a long run for a TD, which is a good sign for team that lacked explosive rushing plays last season. The Bengals were tied for 24th in the NFL in gains of 10 or more yards on the ground by running backs, according to ESPN Research.

 More observations: 

 
 The team spent the bulk of the practice at its indoor bubble because of thunderstorms that were in the area. They came back to Paycor Stadium for a few periods for the fans that stayed. 
 Safety Bryan Cook received some treatment from trainers after favoring his left hamstring. He didn't come back out with the first-team defense for its final drive. 
 Others who did not practice today: CB Dax Hill , CB Jalen Davis , DT Jonathan Allen  and WR Tee Higgins . Hill has been limited with muscle tightness the past few days. 
 DT  Dexter Lawrence II  knocked QB Joe Burrow to the ground during team drills inside the stadium. It was a light brush. 
 For a passing offense that has struggled at times in camp, it had a good moment inside the stadium. Burrow connected on a deep throw to WR  Ja'Marr Chase  behind the Cincinnati secondary. 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The offensive tinkering continued on Thursday as the Bengals try to find different ways to put pressure on opposing defenses. Throughout training camp, Cincinnati has had a ton of reps with QB Joe Burrow under center, which is not typically how the Bengals like to operate. But it's clear that finding ways to mix up the offensive formations is a strategy that will be critical to creating a more explosive offense. And offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher is OK with any lumps that are taken during the process.

 "We just wanna have a lot of tools at our disposal," Pitcher said on Thursday. "And that's what we're developing right now."

 
 The offense and defense traded pre-snap victories during an unscripted 11-on-11 drill. First, the defense forced a delay of game. But the offense responded by drawing the defense offsides. 
 Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell continues to turn heads. Howell took reps with the first team and created pressure off the edge. The second-round pick has been one of the camp's biggest stars. 
 Cincinnati appears to be experimenting with its back-up offensive tackles. Cody Ford and Andrew Coker swapped between the left and right sides during second-team reps. Cincinnati is looking to solidify the swing tackle spot behind starters Orlando Brown Jr . and Amarius Mims . 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The defense continues its strong start to training camp. That was punctuated by a two-play exchange that started with a pass deflection by CB  DJ Turner  on a deep ball intended for WR Ja'Marr Chase , before safety S Bryan Cook had a pick-six off QB Joe Burrow during a team drill. Coordinator Al Golden's group has looked nothing like the team that has struggled in each of the past two seasons.

 "I think as a defense, we have an edge," Golden said. "We gotta continue to have that edge. We haven't done anything."

 
 Bengals CB DJ Ivey took first-team reps with Dax Hill sidelined. Hill was dealing with a bit of tightness and was limited for precautionary reasons. 
 DT Jonathan Allen was not at practice in what appeared to be a vet rest day. Allen also missed a day last week before quickly returning. 
 Cincinnati released S Isaiah Nwokobia on Tuesday. He had not practiced in back-to-back days. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The first day of pads belonged to the Bengals' defense. And in what has become a recurring theme, the defensive line was able to bring some good pressure. Boye Mafe continued to affect the quarterback and rookie Cashius Howell had a clean win off the edge against the second-team defense.

 The defense isn't letting any camp success get to their heads. "We haven't scratched the surface, which is the encouraging thing," said linebacker Barrett Carter . "Our floor right now is high. I'm not trying to jinx us or put expectations on us, but we're stacking days, and we just have to keep doing that. We're nowhere near where we can be."

 More observations: 

 
 Dalton Risner and  Orlando Brown Jr . spent a good amount of time decompressing in the locker room talking about how the day went for them. It was a detailed conversation, which Risner said was an example of the group being dialed in this early in camp. 
 Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young made a couple of good catches. The coaching staff has been adamant that the fourth-round pick out of Georgia can carve out a role on this year's offense.

Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Four days before their preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Saturday, the Browns listed " Deshaun Watson  OR Shedeur Sanders " at starting quarterback in their first unofficial depth chart.

 Coach Todd Monken has yet to announce which quarterback will start in Chicago, but spoke about the value the preseason adds for evaluating the two passers.

 "It does, in terms of getting the ball out, got to learn to get the ball out. Got to learn how to slide," Monken said. "You're not going to be able to just run around. I do want playmaking ability, so there is a balance there between playmaking ability and taking some sacks. You're going to have to live with that to an extent.

 "The other part is stacking plays, where it matters, because they got the scoreboard on in terms of points you put on the board. In terms of the flow of the game, that's a big part of it. We're going to be on the road. The ebbs and flows of positive plays and negative plays, overcoming that. I think there's a part of the quarterback's body language, how they are around the team. Do I sense, 'Hey, that's over. I've moved on to the next play.' So there's a number of things you get to evaluate once you get to the closest we have in terms of games, which is preseason."

 With rookie Spencer Fano securing a starting role at left tackle, Monken said the only starting position on the offensive line up in the air is right guard. Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston have been rotating at the spot.

 "I think Teven has the advantage there from experience," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Special teams coordinator Byron Storer said the team is "definitely taking a hard look at" punters Wes Pahl and Nik Constantinou , but "It's Corey [Bojorquez]'s job to lose." 
 Monken said he is "hopeful" that defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr . will return to practice "soon." Hall hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. 
 On the second-team offensive line, the Browns moved Dawand Jones from left tackle to right tackle and rookie Austin Barber from right tackle to left tackle. 
 Cornerback Damarri Mathis left practice on the back of a cart after he sustained an injury in coverage during a 1-on-1 drill. The team later placed Mathis on injured reserve. 
 Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. 
 Fifteen players did not practice Tuesday: Joe Royer ,  D'Angelo Ross , Denzel Ward (new absence), Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 The Browns claimed tight end Dae'Quan Wright off waivers from the Eagles, per the NFL transaction wire. 
 The Browns had three tight ends in for a tryout today, per the NFL transaction wire: Sal Cannella , Matt Lauter and  Jermaine Terry II . 
 

 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Coach Todd Monken explained the change in the quarterback rotation last Saturday.

 Though Monken said before the practice that Shedeur Sanders would get a "majority" of first-team reps, he said he was later informed that Sanders had received more padded practices with the starters than Watson in the week. So Monken changed the order of reps.

 Sanders practiced with the starting offense Monday, while Watson led the No. 2 offense.

 "As long as we're still sharing reps, it's a competition," Monken said.

 Monken also said he has not decided which quarterback will start the preseason opener in Chicago on Saturday, but he intends to start Watson in one of the first two preseason games and Sanders in the other.

 "I'd like to get our starters out there for the first series together [in the preseason opener]," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Both Watson and Sanders threw short touchdowns during red zone 11-on-11 team drills, but it was overall a mistake-filled practice for the offense. Monken ended a two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense after three consecutive pre-snap penalties. The head coach then called it a day after back-to-back pre-snap infractions for the No. 2 offense. 
 Monken made two notable non-quarterback personnel changes, as rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston practiced with the first-team offense. Fano had been alternating days at starting left tackle with Dawand Jones . Monken said Fano's performance Saturday, in which he went head-to-head with defensive end Jared Verse and even engaged in a post-play scuffle, "solidified" the decision to give the first-round pick more first-team reps. 
 Right tackle Tytus Howard , rookie linebacker Justin Jefferson and cornerback Damarri Mathis returned to practice. 
 Fourteen players did not practice: tight ends Joe Royer (personal) and Jack Stoll ; cornerbacks Myles Bryant and D'Angelo Ross ; fullback Michael Burton ; linebacker Carson Schwesinger ; defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr ., Elijah Chatman , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis and Maliek Collins ; and offensive linemen Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller and Zak Zinter . 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Browns made a major change to the quarterback rotation in their 10th practice.

 Despite Shedeur Sanders being scheduled to lead the No. 1 offense in his alternating reps with Watson, it was Watson who took every starting rep in team drills. Sanders split the remaining reps with Dillon Gabriel .

 Before practice, coach Todd Monken indicated that there might be a 7-on-7 session in which Watson threw to the team's top pass-catchers but added that "Shedeur will take the majority of the 1 reps today."

 The Browns are off Sunday, and Monken said the coaching staff would use that time to discuss which quarterback will start the preseason opener against the Bears next Saturday in Chicago.

 More observations: 

 
 Watson had another productive practice to cap a bounce-back week for him. His highlight throws included a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond in 7-on-7 after he got a step ahead of cornerback Tre Avery , then a short touchdown pass to rookie wideout Denzel Boston on a back-shoulder fade in 11-on-11, beating corner Tyron Herring . 
 Right tackle Tytus Howard left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. Rookie Austin Barber took Howard's spot with the starting offense in team drills. 
 Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins returned to team drills after being limited to individual drills Friday.

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Dallas Cowboys ' camp is taking place in Oxnard, California, and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 It was not a perfect performance for the Cowboys defense against the Los Angeles Rams Tuesday, but it was a lot better than the work against the Rams in last year's joint practices.

 "It's just showing what we've been building on from the spring up until now," linebacker DeMarvion Overshown said. "It was good to hit a different color jersey. I feel like we've been going at it with our offense. They're one of the best in the league so getting to see what we got against another top offense, it puts stuff in perspective. Just another block that we're building on."

 On the first series of team drills,  Shavon Revel Jr . was able to close on a deep ball from Matthew Stafford to  Puka Nacua  and break up the play. Later, DaRon Bland was able to bat away a fade to Davante Adams .

 The Rams' run game was able to get a couple of good runs, but nothing out of the ordinary.

 "We just looked at it as another opportunity to get better. We know [Stafford] is one of the best in the business, then their receiver corps, the running backs and O-line, so we know it wasn't going to be no just easy come in, handle our work and get back on the bus and not break a sweat," Overshown said. "We got some good work in, but I feel like it was good for them to see what we got on our side of the ball as well. I know it's completely different than when they came to Oxnard last year and damn near had a field day."

 More observations: 

 
 The player of the day without question was linebacker Justin Barron . He intercepted three passes, including one on the final play of the two-minute drive off of  Stetson Bennett IV . Barron also had a few stops in the run game. 
 Fresh off agreeing to a three-year, $105.9 million extension, Quinnen Williams was stout in the middle of the defense. On the first set of team drills against the Rams, Williams stopped the running back cold and flexed his right biceps in celebration. He had a couple of tackles for loss. 
 After a slow start, the Cowboys run game was better in the second portion of drills. Tyler Smith had a block to open up a Javonte Williams run. After a fumble, Jaydon Blue was able to get a positive gain on a wide run. 
 Rams OLB Byron Young gave the Cowboys' pass protection some fits early on, getting to the edge on right tackle Terence Steele , which would have negated a completion to George Pickens . 
 The Rams' biggest completion for the first teamers may have been to tight end Terrance Ferguson , who was able to sneak down the sideline against outside linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku . Stafford gently laid the pass over the top for Ferguson to run under. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Coach Brian Schottenheimer already announced that the starters won't play in the preseason, so the joint practices against the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints will take on added importance over the next two weeks.

 The Cowboys practice against the Rams on Tuesday -- could it be the first of three meetings? The Cowboys play the Rams at SoFi Stadium in the regular season. Could there be a playoff rematch? It has crossed quarterback  Dak Prescott 's mind.

 "It's all you can ask for," Prescott said. "... This is a team that we're going to play in the season, and it's probably a team that if we want to get to where we want to get to, we're going to have to see them again. So call this probably one of the first of three meetings, I'd assume, if everybody takes care of business.

 "So it's definitely going to be a test. It's going to be fun. It's going to be two great teams competing against each other. And at the end of the day, it's practice. We'll have a lot of time after that to clean it up and to say, 'This is what we got to get better,' but we can't go out here and also have a hell of a practice and think we've done something."

 Last year, the Rams' offense toyed with the Cowboys' defense. The Cowboys' offense had some good moments, but now will have to contend with pass rusher Myles Garrett , which will test tackles Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele .

 "The one thing about when you play tackle in this league, it's pretty easy to see, I mean, you're either blocking the guy or you're not," Schottenheimer said. "And I'll say this about TG, he's having a great camp. His very first start in the National Football League was against the Cleveland Browns and a pass rusher by the name of Myles Garrett, who I think is an incredible football player, but TG did a nice job in that game.

 "We need those matchups. We need those battles. And what happens in training camp is these guys get pretty comfortable with one another. They know their counter moves. They know, 'Hey, this is his go-to speed rush move. This is his power counter.' And so going up against an opponent that you don't really know as well is truly a great test because you can't anticipate maybe what they're going to do."

 
 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 The Cowboys' practice had a little that would make coaches on defense and offense happy.

 To start, the defense controlled the line of scrimmage against the run and was able to keep the passing game in check. In the final two periods of team drills, the offense was able to respond.

 In between, there was plenty of talk back and forth in what was the most physical practice of training camp.

 "It's fire, man," receiver CeeDee Lamb said. "I embrace it. It was good to see our defense come out with that type of energy, that type of fire, that type of aggression early on. For us as an offense, it leaves us no choice but to bow down or fight back and get on top. And I know one thing about us, we won't bow down to nobody."

 Other observations:  

 
 Dak Prescott and Lamb connected on two deep passes, including one that would have been a touchdown of more than 50 yards after he was able to get a step on cornerback DaRon Bland . His first deep reception came when he got a step on Cobie Durant . 
 After a Jaydon Blue touchdown run to the edge, safety P.J. Locke was able to read Prescott's eyes perfectly and come up with the interception in the end zone on what looked like a 2-point play. Later, Shemar James intercepted Prescott, who was under pressure. 
 Safety Jalen Thompson (hip) returned to 11-on-11 drills for the first time in a few days. The hope is he will be good to go from now on and practice against the Rams on Tuesday. 
 On the first two plays of team, edge rushers Donovan Ezeiruaku and Rashan Gary blew up consecutive runs. Ezeiruaku got off the ball quick to get to Javonte Williams . Gary's physical play with Tyler Smith stymied a Blue run. 
 The Cowboys do not practice Monday. They next time they hit the field in pads will be Tuesday at the Rams' facility in Woodland Hills.

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on the QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Broncos owner/CEO Greg Penner, who had not spoken publicly since the league meetings in March, covered a variety of topics with local media on Tuesday. At one point he was asked about his expectations for the season, and he made it clear a team that returns all but two starters from the AFC Championship Game has the same expectations from him as the next year's team and the ones that come after that.

 "Our goal is to compete for championships every year and if we put ourselves in that position every year, we're going to be successful and win Super Bowls," he said.

 He also talked about the new five-year deal for coach Sean Payton that Payton signed in June, saying: "I've been really pleased with what he's built here, the culture, the performance on the field (and) it enabled us to line up he and [general manager] George [Paton's] contracts now. George has done a fantastic job building this roster."

 More observations: 

 
 Center is suddenly a trouble spot, as injuries continue to happen at the position. The Broncos' top two centers -- Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth -- have missed time in camp and on Tuesday Michael Deiter -- who was signed for depth in the offseason after spending seven seasons in Miami, Houston and Washington -- was carted to the locker room. Calvin Throckmorton slid in as the first-team center, with undrafted rookie free agent Gavin Ortega providing depth. All-Pro guard Quinn Meinerz played some center early in his NFL career and could shift over if needed, but moving one of the NFL's best guards to another position is not ideal. 
 Sam Ehlinger continues to flash in his quest for the No. 2 quarterback job. He has consistently moved the offense in team drills during camp, and his throw to undrafted rookie wide receiver Kolbe Katsis for a touchdown in situational red zone work with the third-team offense was one of the best plays of the day. 
 Running back J.K. Dobbins , who left Monday's practice with what Sean Payton referred to as a soft tissue injury, returned to practice Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 A recent spate of what Sean Payton called "soft-tissue" injuries prompted the coach to adjust the end of practice. After the two-and-half-hour workout, Payton had the strength and conditioning staff add a longer, more formal warm-down period. Payton said he expected to continue to have the players go through the longer warm down in the days ahead.

 

 "Got to get a handle on some of the soft-tissue stuff. ... Strains, hamstring or groins, [we] continue to fight through that," Payton said. "I don't think it's heat related. ... You always try to look at your pre-practice routine, your hydration obviously."

 Running back J.K. Dobbins left the practice field with an injury and did not return. Wide receivers Marvin Mims Jr . -- who returned to practice Monday -- and Jaylen Waddle have also had similar injuries in recent weeks.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton said he will play most, if not all, of the healthy starters for at least some snaps in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta. Payton said the coaches hadn't yet formalized the snap counts yet, but that he wanted regulars to get at least some work. "You have to build callouses," he said. 
 Quarterback Bo Nix hopes first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb will be on the sideline during games to call plays instead of in the coaches' box. Payton said Monday he and Webb hadn't yet discussed the gameday setup yet, but that he expected Webb to call plays from the sideline. "I always loved quarterback-to-playcaller when they're on the sideline with me," Nix said. "You get the feel of the game a little differently. ... They get to feel the emotions of a game on the sideline. ... I like when the playcaller is right there, and when I come off I can have that eye-to-eye conversation." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 When the Broncos went through a scripted scrimmage, it was safety Brandon Jones who was 3-of-4 in field goal attempts.

 Why? Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi said most of the Australian punters he has worked with in his long coaching career, including the Broncos' Jeremy Crawshaw , have not kicked field goals.

 So the Broncos need a contingency plan in case  Wil Lutz gets injured in a game. And with Lutz and several Broncos coaches, including Sean Payton, in Canton, Ohio, to see Drew Brees be enshrined into the Hall of Fame, it was Jones getting the kicks.

 Rizzi said Jones' longest made field goal was 39 yards, but Jones said he made a 50-yarder in OTAs. At one point, as Jones moved into position before the snap, the crowd of several thousand people chanted his name.

 "Have a lot of respect for kickers when the crowd started chanting my name, I got really nervous, and I'm like, 'I'm about to shank this,' but thankfully it went in," Jones said.

 Jones was 2-of-2 from the center of the field, 1-of-2 from the left hashmark.

 Other observations: 

 
 With wide receiver  Courtland Sutton getting some rest days in camp to go with recent injuries to Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., Pat Bryant has consistently made play after play as a reliable option for quarterback  Bo Nix . Bryant's leaping, get-the-toes-down scoring grab in red zone work was just another example. Bryant leaped over a double-team of Ja'Quan McMillian and Jahdae Barron to make the catch. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb said, "Man, Patty Ice has had some really, really good practices." 
 The Broncos closed out a stretch of six consecutive days on the practice field with a scripted scrimmage, but held out some of their healthy high-profile players, including cornerback Pat Surtain II , tackle Mike McGlinchey , safety Talanoa Hufanga and running back J.K. Dobbins . 
 The defense shut down both two-minute drives by the offense to close out the practice -- the situation was offense trailing by four with 1:14 left in the game. Nix led the first group, and  Sam Ehlinger led the other, which made it to the 8-yard line before the defense was credited with a sack to end the drive. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 If Broncos coach Sean Payton checks his phone on his flight to Canton, Ohio, on Friday he isn't going to like some of the messages. It was a rugged day of practice, as wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr ., tight end Nate Adkins and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen left with injuries.

 Mims pulled up after running a deep route and hopped off the field before he went to the locker room. Adkins walked into the locker room with Mims and a trainer while Henningsen, who missed last season with a ruptured Achilles he suffered in last summer's camp, was carted to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.

 That comes in addition to the other injuries the Broncos suffered already this week to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (leg) and edge…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Detroit Lions camp is taking place in Allen Park, Mich., and Lions reporter Eric Woodyard has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Lions camp. We will update this file often. Can Dan Campbell & Co. get Detroit back in the playoffs in 2026? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Lions camp 
 
 Lions OL Mays out into season; RB Pacheco hurts knee 
 Lions make Jahmyr Gibbs highest-paid running back in NFL history 
 Ex-All Pro LB Devin White joins Lions on 1-year deal 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph is currently away from the team while dealing with a personal issue.

 But his rehab process for his knee injury is coming along "very well," according to head coach Dan Campbell.

 It's still unlikely that Joseph will be back ahead of Week 1, but the Lions envision him returning around the same time as Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch , who is also coming off a season-ending Achilles injury in 2025, for practices in late training camp or possibly early September.

 "And Branch is doing well, too," Campbell said ahead of Tuesday's practice. "So, those guys, we're talking about on down the road, the season's already begun. But I like where Kerby's at."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Newly signed Lions QB Joshua Dobbs participated in his first full practice after being signed on Monday. Dobbs has begun his second stint with the Lions. He was previously on Detroit's practice squad in 2022 and felt comfortable returning to the team's facility. "It felt really good. A lot of familiar faces. Some change but not much so I've really enjoyed that," Dobbs said following Tuesday's practice. "Just being able to kind of at least know where everything is, as you get your feet under you to get ready to practice." 
 The Lions will be sporting their new Rivalries uniforms against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 on Nov. 1. 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Veteran OL Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury that is expected to sideline him for 8-10 weeks. In his absence,  Seth McLaughlin took first-team reps at center, where he battled against former Ohio State teammate Tyleik Williams and DT Alim McNeill  during Monday's practice. OL Michael Niese took the bulk of the second team reps at center as Detroit tries to identify the best starting unit ahead of the regular season.

 "I'm taking it one practice at a time, getting better," McLaughlin said. "With practice, it's (Day) 11 at camp and you're not who you wanna be on the first day of the regular season so there's a long way to go to keep getting better."

 Prior to Monday's practice, Lions QB Jared Goff didn't have many reps with McLaughlin, but has been impressed with him so far as he continues to adjust to the role. Throughout OTAs and the offseason, Goff mainly worked with Mays and veteran OL  Juice Scruggs , who is also expected to be in the mix for the starting role once he returns from a soft tissue injury that has kept him out.

 "He did a good job. He really did," Goff said of McLaughlin. "He stepped in there. He had good authority with his calls. He was sharp. He was decisive. I think that's all you can ask for."

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff , and most of the starters, will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22, according to head coach Dan Campbell. Undrafted rookie QB Lions  Luke Altmyer will now continue in the QB2 role behind Goff and is expected to take heavy snaps on Thursday, but Detroit will likely be adding another veteran QB for depth purposes as early as this week after Teddy Bridgewater decided to step away from the team. Altmyer says he's "excited" for the opportunity ahead.

 "I've played at a high level with the Big Ten and I've played in football games but it's a different level and I think that's the challenge is can you maintain emotions because it can get you really high and really excited," Altmyer said after Sunday's practice. "But, trusting my abilities, trusting my preparation, trusting my teammates. I think that's the word trust."

 Other observations:  

 
 Lions veteran QB Teddy Bridgewater has decided to step away from the team amid training camp and was officially placed on the reserved/retired list ahead of Sunday's practice. Campbell says he will be "missed" but this retirement could be for good. 
 Lions HC Dan Campbell and his wife Holly attended the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Canton to support legendary New Orleans Saints QB Drew Brees on Saturday on an off day. Campbell was an assistant/tight ends coach in New Orleans from 2016-20 and signed with the Saints as a player in 2009. "It was a reminder. It was refreshing just to be able to stand in the presence of greatness with those guys," Campbell said. 
 The Lions signed CB Ryan Cooper and LB Amen Ogbongbemiga and waived TE Nick Muse . 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 The connection between Jared Goff and  Amon-Ra St. Brown  was on display as St. Brown scored a touchdown in Friday's scrimmage off a slant at the goal line through tight coverage. St. Brown had a two-point conversion while also converting multiple fourth downs on a monster day in which his playmaking was consistently on display. WRs coach Scottie Montgomery credits Goff and St. Brown's friendship as the driving force of their on-field chemistry.

 "These guys, their timing is correct, but their off-the-field relationship also gives us an opportunity that a lot of people don't have," Montgomery said. "The communication between the two of them is probably what makes them as consistent as they are. There's certain things and there's nonverbal communication that happened between them now because of where we are in the offense, where they are in their relationship away from the building."

 More observations: 

 
 After signing a record three-year extension on Thursday, RB Jahmyr Gibbs was on the field and in uniform for the second straight day of practice but didn't participate in full team drills. "This process has been extremely stressful. I just wanted to play ball," Gibbs said. "I missed being out there with my teammates and coaches and it's just fun being out there now with my pads and stuff on. It just feels a lot better." 
 Detroit rapper Sada Baby and popular comedian Haha Davis were both in attendance for Friday's practice, sharing their excitement for the upcoming season while mingling with fans. "When you go 15-2 and reach the NFC Championship, at some point it has to go down and this is the year," Haha Davis said. "I really believe that." 
 The Lions are signing veteran DT Ben Stille to a one-year deal, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 Detroit has waived injured CB  De'Shawn Rucker .﻿ 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Lions held a 2 ½-hour practice session in humid conditions. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell wasn't pleased with the performance of the defense during red-zone drills and was brutally honest in his assessment. He also took accountability for his "fair share of mess ups" as they're looking to improve to reach their standard ahead of Week 1.

 "Not very good. I'll be completely honest with you," Campbell said. "What caused it? I feel like there's obviously communication and technique. It's really simple. Like football is simple, but it's hard to do. It's easy to talk about and hard to do."

 Campbell feels they will continue to get better.

title: Jared Goff understands urgency, eager for Lions to return to form
summary: Coach Dan Campbell is thrilled with the urgency and guidance Goff shows his Lions teammates.
full_text:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. -- Moments after Monday's intense two-hour practice in which he was chased around by Detroit Lions defenders, veteran quarterback Jared Goff chased his young daughter around on the same practice field.

 As Goff enters his 11th season, the five-time Pro Bowler has felt more appreciative of sharing these training camp moments after practice with young Romy Isabelle and his wife, Christen.

 Now that everything is set -- his future, his money, and his team is in place -- the 31-year-old is looking to the help the Lions get over the hump to return to the postseason and potentially bring home a Super Bowl.

 And fatherhood has helped him keep that perspective that time is valuable as Detroit hopes to bounce back from a disappointing 9-8 season.

 "Yeah, makes it fun when it's over. I get to see her and yeah, it's really fun," Goff said. "It's really cool. Something you've always dreamed about as a player, having your child here and her being able to enjoy it. I know she probably won't remember these days, but I know I will."

 Moreso than any mechanics or techniques, Lions coach Dan Campbell feels that Goff has grown over the past seasons with his "urgency" to win now, with his family routinely present throughout training camp.

 Goff and most of the Lions starters will not play in the preseason opener against the Cincinnati Bengals this week but could see some action against Washington on Aug. 22 ahead of the season opener against New Orleans on Sept. 13.

 "It's the mentality, the urgency, the leadership, the, 'Hey man, let's go.' We cannot accept anything less than the best. He wants to be the best in the league, and he wants to run the best offense in the league," Campbell said. "And to get there, we've got to go, we don't have time. That's where I really feel him growing. And every year I felt more of an urgency out of him in that regard, more command, more leadership and that has to come organically. It can't be forced on somebody, it can't. And so that's great to see out of him."

 Goff credits that seriousness to age, maturity and previous experiences in the NFL. He wants to erase that feeling of missing the playoffs for the first time since 2022 after back-to-back 12-win seasons.

 "I think it's just human nature. You start realizing where things can slip and you don't want to allow that to happen," Goff said following Monday's practice. "And the older I get, the more I'm learning and trying to stay on that type of stuff, but yeah, it's good that it's noticeable.

 "It's not necessarily something I'm conscious of every day, but I think it's maybe just overall a little bit more of that mindset this year."

 It's no secret that Goff is on the back half of his career, but backup rookie QB Luke Altmyer has also been attentive to how detail-oriented he still is, since the start of training camp. That professionalism continues to rub off on his new teammates.

 "Doing things at a high level, consistently day after day. Doing the mundane things, the ordinary things at a very high level," Altmyer said. "He makes the ordinary look extraordinary. And I try to master that as well, this position, and during camp it can get pretty mundane and ordinary and he does the things, the little things at a high level, over and over again."

 Goff spent the first five seasons of his career with the Los Angeles Rams , after being selected first overall in the 2016 NFL draft, and is heading into his sixth season in Detroit.

 He recently joined NFL legends Peyton Manning and Tom Brady as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to win 13 games in a season for multiple franchises and is one of six quarterbacks in NFL history to log 100 touchdown passes with multiple franchises.

 But he hasn't thought about how much longer he wants to play. His focus is on helping the Lions get back on track right now.

 "No, I'm right in the middle of it. No, I haven't," Goff said. "I think I said this other day, until I don't feel like I can help a team win a championship. And I think that's going to be a long time."

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Three weeks and 11 practices into training camp, and something's missing: fighting.

 
There hasn't even been so much as a scuffle or shoving match.

 
This is training camp No. 7 for veteran safety Xavier McKinney and when asked if this is the deepest into training camp he has ever gone without seeing a fight, McKinney didn't hesitate.

 
"Hell yeah," he said. "For sure."

 
But McKinney doesn't think that's a bad thing. Nor is it a sign that the players are not competitive enough.

 
"I think we're past that, to be honest," McKinney said. "I think we have a bigger goal, and that bigger goal is to get over this hump that we've been kind of dealing with these last couple years. We're not focused on fighting. Nobody's trying to get kicked out of practice. Nobody's trying to have practice stop early. We're just trying to focus on our technique. We're trying to find ways where we can improve as individuals. We want to be the best group that we can possibly be. We want to be better than what we were last year."

 
The Packers also haven't had a joint practice yet. So even McKinney said all bets are off when the Cardinals come to town for a practice Aug. 26.

 
"That always happens," McKinney said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Just when it looked like the injury list would keep getting longer, a few key players returned to practice. Receivers Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle) were back after missing two practices. So was tight end Josh Whyle (neck). All took part in team (11-on-11) periods. Cornerback Carrington Valentine , who dropped out of practice Aug. 2 because of a hamstring injury, returned for individual drills only. The only new addition to the DNP list was rookie edge Dani Dennis-Sutton , but it was because of an illness. 
 The Packers had a pair of new defensive backs on the field after signing Trey Dean III and Travion Fluellen . They both worked with the safeties during individual drills. Safety Javon Bullard (foot) remained out. 
 After taking reps with both the second- and third-string defenses Monday, Keisean Nixon was back at his regular left cornerback spot with the No. 1 defense. In fact, he worked exclusively with that group and appeared to be on the field for every snap that the starters took. Brandon Cisse continued to work as the No. 1 right cornerback. 
 Trey Smack went 4-for-5 during a field goal period. His miss was wide right on a 45-yarder. He hit the right upright on a 41-yarder but it still went through. He's now 20-for-28 (71.4%) during camp. 
 A day after the NFL said it will allow head coaches to designate a member of their sideline staff to initiate replay challenges , coach Matt LaFleur said he doesn't plan to pass off the red challenge flag. "I probably should give it up based on past actions," LaFleur joked. "So no, I'll probably hold the challenge flag." 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 It was the kind of practice that would have excited a young, backup quarterback.

 But what about a 37-year-old going into his 16th NFL season?

 
"Oh yeah, the game still excites me," Tyrod Taylor said.

 
In what was perhaps Taylor's best practice since he signed with the Packers this offseason, he completed passes of all varieties. There was a deep post to Kisean Johnson . A quick-hitting slant to Will Sheppard for a first down. A 20-yarder to Sheppard down the left sideline. A big gain over the middle to J. Michael Sturdivant .

 
It didn't matter to Taylor that it was all with backup receivers -- many of whom might not make the team.

 
"There's a healthy rotation of guys that's going in and out with the group that I'm running with, and it's just up to me to communicate, get them in the right position but also give them a chance to make plays," Taylor said. "We've got a ton of playmakers at our skill positions."

 
The Packers had one of the best backup quarterbacks in the NFL last season with Malik Willis , who signed with the Dolphins as a free agent. Now, they have one of the most experienced.

 "I'm a firm believer that your actions speak louder than your words, especially early on," said Taylor, who has played in 100 career games (with 62 starts) for seven teams. "It's about me coming in, being myself, preparing on the field, off the field, being ready for the opportunities and taking advantage of them as well, and then gradually growing into more of a vocal leader and speaking on things when they fit."

 Other observations: 

 
 As if it weren't unusual enough to see cornerback Keisean Nixon with the second-string defense Sunday, it was even more surprising to see him taking snaps with the third-stringers Monday. In the very next period, he was back with the No. 1 defense, but it's a baffling way to handle a player who last season was considered the team's No. 1 cornerback. When Nixon wasn't with the starters, Benjamin St-Juste was in his spot along with rookie Brandon Cisse on the other side. Could it be a sign the Packers are thinking about demoting Nixon? "There's always competition," coach Matt LaFleur said. "All these guys got to be prepared for that. As far as the substitution, that's not something that I'm always micromanaging. A lot of that's on the position coach." 
 Though starting linebackers Edgerrin Cooper (foot) and Zaire Franklin (rest) returned to practice, the offense was still without two of its top receivers, Matthew Golden (toe) and Jayden Reed (ankle). Without running back Josh Jacobs (groin) and with tight end  Tucker Kraft (knee) not yet doing 11-on-11 periods, the primary skill position players with the No. 1 offense were MarShawn Lloyd at running back; Christian Watson , Bo Melton , Skyy Moore , Savion Williams and Isaiah Neyor at receiver; and  Messiah Swinson and Drake Dabney at tight end. 
 Add safety Javon Bullard to the injury list. He had a walking boot on his right foot during practice but said afterward that the issue was just a bruise that won't impact his availability for the start of the season. Kitan Oladapo played in Bullard's usual spot in the slot in the nickel package. 
 Two of the biggest plays of the day came from players fighting to make the roster. Cornerback Jaylin Simpson ended practice with a goal-line interception off undrafted rookie quarterback Kyron Drones . Meanwhile, Melton came down with a true 50-50 ball on a deep throw from Jordan Love . It looked like Nixon might have been in position to break it up or even intercept it before Melton came back for the ball and snagged it. "I just wanted it to be like a 80/20 or 100/0," Melton said. "My ball or nobody's."

 If the Packers were looking for someone to emerge behind their top three receivers, then perhaps…
