The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Coach DeMeco Ryans called Tuesday's indoor practice "outstanding," after characterizing Monday's practice as subpar. You would have never thought there's a Thursday preseason game against the Chargers looming as the physicality was intense. There were several plays with players driven to the ground or tackled.

 There was even a dust-up between center Keylan Rutledge and All-Pro defensive end  Will Anderson Jr . that exceeded the typical millisecond hand locking of helmets. Anderson and Rutledge engaged in shoving even through their teammates' attempts at separation.

 The defense forced turnovers, highlighted by linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair intercepting quarterback  C.J. Stroud 's tipped pass. But Stroud also connected for a 80-yard touchdown to running back David Montgomery down the sideline.

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 For the Texans' first preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers  on Thursday, coach DeMeco Ryans said, "We'll have a select group of guys who will not go out there and play."

 So don't expect the key starters to play much. Anticipate seeing only rookie starters, such as center Keylan Rutledge , and a few second-year players, such as wideout Jayden Higgins  and left tackle Aireontae Ersery .

 The preseason opener will be about early impressions from younger players and seeing where they are with depth. It'll be about seeing the guys they'll have to make decisions on to fill out the back end of the roster with limited spots among the starters being unsettled.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 The Texans held a night practice on Saturday. It was not pretty for the Texans offense as quarterback C.J. Stroud had many incompletions and the run game had little running room.

 However, the defense displayed the potential of a top-three unit in the NFL. There were plenty of sacks, an interception from Pro Bowl safety  Calen Bullock  and pass break ups. But most importantly, they're not satisfied. Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke's assessment of the defense was "okay."

 Burke said Houston is chasing perfection defensively.

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After an off day, the Texans dialed back their intensity as they went through drills without pads, but notably, wide receiver  Tank Dell practiced for the second straight day of training camp, albeit in a limited capacity.

 It's another step in Dell's recovery, with Wednesday being his first time practicing since he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in Week 16 of 2024.

 Speaking to the media for the first time, Dell said he had no fear in the strength of his knee, pointing towards Houston's doctor stating his knee is "100 percent stable." 

 "Trusting the work you put in prior to going out there," said Dell when asked about trusting in his health. "Going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me. So when I got out here, I wasn't scared."﻿

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 One year after being in contention to be the Colts' starting quarterback, Anthony Richardson Sr . now finds himself in a fight for the Colts' No. 2 quarterback spot behind Daniel Jones .

 
Sunday was another day of evaluation for the Colts, with Richardson displaying some ups and downs throughout the workout before finishing with an impressive 2-minute drill that led to a touchdown. Meanwhile, Riley Leonard , his competition, has had a strong couple of days after battling his own inconsistency.

 
Richardson requested a trade in February and was granted permission to speak with other clubs to see if a deal might materialize. Nothing did, so Richardson is back trying to re-establish himself with the organization. Richardson on Sunday said his accuracy needs to be more consistent.

Richardson and Leonard will split preseason snaps.

Haulcy . Later, running back Jonathan Taylor had a pass go through his hands, landing squarely in the hands of safety Cam Bynum .

 The Colts are still working to identify their best lineup at linebacker, and it's beginning to look like they might not have the luxury of settling in with a consistent starting group.

 "At the end of the day, I think we're going to have a lot of guys in that room that play for us this year in different types of roles," Anarumo said.

 Having two rookies -- Allen and Bryce Boettcher -- among the leading candidates to start, is a factor, Anarumo said. Streamlining young players' responsibilities can allow for faster growth.

 Receiver Josh Downs missed practice with a groin injury, leaving the Colts without their top two wideouts. Alec Pierce remains sidelined after offseason ankle surgery, and the Colts have provided no specific timeline for his return.

 Cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward have been making life difficult for the team's wide receivers so far in camp, much to the Colts' contentment.

 The length of both players has been especially challenging for the receivers, a group that is trying to find its way with the No. 3 spot still up for grabs.

 "When you can go up against two of the best in the league in practice every day, it's going to make everybody better," coach Shane Steichen said.

Among the highlights was tight end Tyler Warren 's leaping catch in the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Daniel Jones . Another impressive completion came when Jones delivered a strike to receiver Josh Downs in the corner of the end zone.

 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Jaguars coach Liam Coen is the offensive playcaller so he naturally wants to see that side of the ball have success in practice. When it doesn't -- which happened on Tuesday -- he's still learning not to get mad.

 The offensive line is dealing with injuries to five players -- including three likely starters -- and as a result struggled to run the ball in 11-on-11 work against what was the top rush defensive in the NFL last season.

 "We were supposed to do four-minute [offense] today and go, hit, bang, another four-minute [period] run, run, run, run, run," Coen said. "And the way that those guys came out on defense [and dominated], at the end of the day, I'm the head coach [and] I've got to be happy with something."

 Coen said starters will not play in the preseason opener against New Orleans on Saturday. They will get the majority of the reps in the joint practice against the Saints on Thursday.

 Udinski is in his second season as the Jaguars' offensive coordinator after joining Coen's staff last season following three seasons in Minnesota, moving from the assistant to head coach Kevin O'Connell/special projects in 2022 to the assistant offensive coordinator/assistant quarterbacks coach in 2024.

 Udinski, 30, interviewed for the head coaching jobs in Cleveland and Buffalo in the offseason.

LT Cole Van Lanen (knee) and OL Garrett DiGiorgio were already on PUP. This is potentially a problem area if the injuries to Mekari, Little and Pregnon linger.

 Talks between the Jaguars and receiver  Parker Washington 's camp on a contract extension remain active, but the fourth-year player out of Penn State isn't focusing on when a deal could get done and isn't upset that an agreement hasn't yet been reached.

 "It's there and it's a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence] ," Washington said Thursday. "So that's my mindset and that's how I'm going to attack it. I'm not going to step on my agent's toes. They can have those conversations. I'm going to come out here and do my job."

 Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said early in the offseason the team was working on extensions with Washington and tight end Brenton Strange . They reached a deal with Strange, signing him to a three-year extension worth up to $48 million in June but have yet to finalize anything with Washington.

title: How Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. prepared to be better in 2026
summary: Thomas has worked intentionally to improve his hands for 2026, and as Liam Coen said, "It elevates everybody's game when BT is playing at his highest level."
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars receiver  Brian Thomas Jr . stands in front of a JUGS machine after every practice with his hands inches away from it and his thumbs and pointer fingers forming a triangle. The setting on the machine is usually between 2 and 3 -- for reference, when it's used to simulate a punt it's set on 6. Each football rockets out between the two spinning wheels and slams into his hands over and over.

 And Thomas has caught them nearly every time.

 Over the offseason, strengthening his hands was a main goal. The JUGS routine is one of the things the third-year receiver is doing to bounce back from a disappointing 2025 season that saw him catch eight fewer touchdowns than the year before.

 "In the spring, very early on, honestly, you could sense that he had really looked at things in areas in which he thought he could improve upon, and he was attacking those areas," head coach Liam Coen said. "I thought he was extremely intentional about the things he wanted to improve on."

 Coaches and teammates noticed a difference this spring and it has carried over into training camp.

 "When you put the work in and just be super intentional about little things like that, you'll definitely see the work paying off," Thomas said. "I feel much stronger at the catch point. I'm able to go and do a lot more things. I really just feel stronger in general."

 As a result, there's optimism that Thomas is headed for the kind of big season he had as a rookie when he ranked third in the league with 1,282 receiving yards.

 "He's playing confident right now," Coen said.

 

 After making the Pro Bowl as a rookie in 2024, his second season was filled with drops -- five in the first seven games -- and injuries to his left ankle and shoulder that cost him four games. There was also a nagging left wrist injury that started in Week 1 and lingered throughout the season.

 At one point the Jaguars moved rookie Travis Hunter ahead of Thomas as WR1, but a knee injury ended Hunter's season after seven games. The team then traded for Jakobi Meyers in early November, and by the end of the season Parker Washington had become  Trevor Lawrence 's No. 1 target.

 Thomas finished 2026 with 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns -- and the determination to have his best offseason.

 "I knew I had to be super intentional about everything I did, whether it's just staying focused, staying locked in on catching the ball, staying locked in to the catch point," he said. "Getting my body right, to come in and be the best I can be, being [in] the best shape I could be. Just little things. My whole offseason was about just fixing all the little things ... that I know I can clean up."

 Thomas put together a workout plan, focused on his nutrition and emphasized improving his hand-eye connection in catching the football. Part of that was actually strengthening his hands by using the JUGS machine as well as jamming his hands into a bucket of sand and moving them around. He also caught tennis balls to improve his focus and worked on making sure he watched the ball all the way from the throw until he tucked it. And he never deviated from his plan.

 "It's basically just growing up," Thomas said. "I was young. Coming in, I just had to learn. Really, everybody's got to learn. Coming in and learning, seeing the things that vets do, learning how to take care of your body, what works for you, what doesn't work for you."

 When he got back around his teammates, they noticed.

 

 "He's having a great camp so far," Meyers said. "And it's just built off the spring. He had one of the better springs that I've seen of a younger guy since I've been in the league (eight years), but if he's just doing half of what he's doing now [during the season], I think he would be in a good spot."

 Receivers coach Edgar Bennett was also impressed.

 "It all starts with the mindset [and] he came in with the right mindset," Bennett said. "He knew these are the areas that I want to improve on. And I mean, he literally takes a day-by-day approach. Every single day we're improving at something.

 "You see BT now loving the process. And [Coen] talks about it all the time, the process, loving the process. And you see a guy loving it."

 Thomas said this is the best he has felt mentally and physically going into a season. His confidence is sky-high, too. That's evident by what he has done in practice, Coen said, and the rest of the offense is feeding off it.

 "I think it brings everybody up," he said. "It elevates everybody's game when BT is playing at his highest level."

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 One player fans should be interested to see in Saturday's preseason opener against the Los Angeles Rams is receiver Andrew Armstrong .

 A second-year player who was cut last year by the Miami Dolphins , Armstrong joined the Chiefs in January and has been impressive throughout training camp. When fellow receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy were out last week, Armstrong had several highlights with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the rest of the first-team offense.

 "I've been out there being the best I can be and learning," Armstrong said after Tuesday's practice. "One of the main goals is being trustworthy for the quarterback. I'm trying to build that with [Mahomes].

 "This has been my favorite team since I was a little kid. I really wanted to be around a serious environment and this is an extremely serious environment. I love that."

 Armstrong is in a tight competition with second-year player Jalen Royals for the sixth and potential final receiver spot on the initial 53-man roster. If Armstrong performs well against the Rams, he could gain a sizable lead in the battle.

 "Oh, it's going to feel great, just looking and seeing all the red," Armstrong said of playing inside Arrowhead Stadium. "It's different playing on a [video] game than in real life. I know it's going to feel amazing."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 Before Tuesday's practice, the Chiefs agreed to sign defensive end Emmanuel Ogbah to a one-year deal. A 10-year veteran, Ogbah was with the Chiefs in 2019, the year the team won the Super Bowl. "I always had an affection for E," defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo said. "I've always periodically been in touch with him. If he's part of our group, I'll be excited about that." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 With just seven practices left in training camp, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes appears to be close to having his full complement of receivers on the field. For the first time in camp, Monday's on-field work featured Mahomes' top four receivers -- Rashee Rice , Xavier Worthy , Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen .

 Worthy, who missed last week's practices with a sprained right shoulder, was the lone receiver who didn't participate in the 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 reps. He could be a full participant later this week ahead of the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 In the 7-on-7 period inside the red zone, Allen showed his ability to improvise in the middle of one play to get behind linebacker Nick Bolton for an 11-yard touchdown. A few minutes later, Rice caught a 6-yard touchdown pass in the back of the end zone against tight coverage from Nohl Williams .

 Mahomes had several reps with his top three receivers being Rice, Thornton and Allen alongside tight end Travis Kelce and running back  Kenneth Walker III .

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower-back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 For the first time in camp, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane was in pads and cleared to participate in 7-on-7 periods, although he was still wearing a noncontact yellow jersey for the shoulder injury he sustained in May that forced him to miss the mandatory minicamp in June. In Monday's practice, Delane had two quality reps, where he covered Kelce and the other against Thornton inside the red zone. "He did a nice job with that," Reid said of Delane. 
 For the third straight practice, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, had his reps at right guard in place of Smith. Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, played at right tackle with the first-team offense. "I think it's good for him to have some flexibility to do both [positions]," Reid said of Benson, who began camp at right tackle. "We worked him a little bit in there in OTAs and liked what we saw. This gives him real competition in there now where [defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo] is throwing a lot of different things at you, so you have to be able to adjust. It'll do nothing but help him, even at the tackle spot once he jumps back there." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 More than halfway through camp, the Chiefs finally had a practice where multiple players had physical altercations. Coach Andy Reid doesn't want his players to fight, but he designs the Chiefs' camp to push the players, both physically and mentally.

 This was the sixth consecutive practice before an off day Sunday. After an 11-on-11 repetition, defensive end  Felix Anudike-Uzomah  and left guard Kingsley Suamataia , who kept engaging him after the play was over, got into it. Suamataia even threw a punch with his right hand while several teammates were trying to separate him and Anudike-Uzomah.

 "It's kind of unusual, and we haven't done that in the past," special teams coordinator Dave Toub said of the Chiefs' six straight practices. "It was a little bit of a grinder. It was chippy. That's how you know. It's hot and that's football sometimes."

 Toward the end of practice, the first-team offense was in the middle of the long-drive drill -- a period in which the projected starters had 16 consecutive repetitions -- when running back Kenneth Walker III became frustrated with safety Alohi Gilman . Walker felt Gilman hit more than was necessary when he had the ball near the sideline. After the repetition, Gilman put his face mask directly in front of Walker's. When Gilman shoved his teammate, Walker threw the ball at him and tackled him, which forced multiple teammates to separate them.

 "Going against the same guys and just being competitive, I think that's what's been great about this camp," quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "It's super competitive on both sides, so little scuffles here and there but nothing crazy. As long as we keep it like that and keep competing, that's where you get the best team you can get."

summary: Follow our daily updates from Chargers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 The defense dominated Tuesday's padded practice, with defensive tackle Teair Tart and cornerback Donte Jackson among the most active players.

 Tart had at least two pressures that likely would have resulted in sacks of quarterback Justin Herbert , bursting through the interior offensive line. Khalil Mack also appeared to share one of those would-be sacks with Tart. Tart was disruptive against the run throughout practice as well.

 Jackson had two interceptions and a pass breakup. He first intercepted Herbert after jumping a route on a pass intended for JaQuae Jackson . Later, Donte Jackson made a nearly identical play against DJ Uiagalelei , jumping another pass intended for JaQuae Jackson.

 More observations: 

 
 
 Wide receiver  Tre' Harris  got a win against cornerback Donte Jackson in 1-on-1s, making a contested catch as he fell to the ground despite tight coverage from Jackson.

 
 
 Tight end Charlie Kolar had a nice catch over safety  Derwin James Jr . on a good ball from Justin Herbert .

 
 
 Outside linebacker Akheem Mesidor blew by OL Travis Burke on a rep that might have resulted in a sack of QB Trey Lance . Mesidor also easily shed OL Branson Taylor on a Kimani Vidal run that likely would've been stopped in the backfield.

 
 
 Defensive tacke Jahmeer Carter has stood out recently. He had a powerful win against Jake Slaughter in 1-on-1s that knocked Slaughter off balance. Carter also blew up a Vidal run in 11-on-11.

 
 
 Safety Devin Grant intercepted quarterback Uiagalelei.

 
 
 Linebackers Daiyan Henley and Bud Dupree and OL Cole Strange left the team period early and worked off to the side with strength coach Ben Herbert.

 
 
 Outside linebacker Andre Carter , who had his first practice yesterday, batted down a Lance pass at the line of scrimmage.

 
 
 Wide receiver Derius Davis had a nice catch down the sideline near the end of practice. It was an impressive throw from Justin Herbert, who fit the ball over a cornerback underneath and a safety over the top.

 
 
 Slaughter, Taylor and Kayode Awosika rotated at left guard.

 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 

 Left tackle Rashawn Slater and cornerback Tarheeb Still missed practice for the third straight day. Coach Jim Harbaugh originally said Slater's absence two days ago was part of a veteran rest day, but his continued absence suggests there may be more to it. The Chargers have not provided a reason for Still's absence.

 In Slater's absence, Branson Taylor and  Trey Pipkins III  have played left tackle, and Cam Hart has taken the bulk of snaps at outside in place of Still. Before, Still and Hart rotated with the first group.

 More observations: 

 
 Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika rotated at left guard, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said "no one's eliminated themselves from the tournament." 
 McDaniel ran across the field yelling, "Great job,  Joe Alt " during practice Monday after Alt blocked outside linebacker Khalil Mack on a screen, something the Chargers have struggled to do throughout camp. McDaniel said Alt has "exceeded my expectations that were pretty high coming in" and called him an "over-the-top pleasant surprise." 
 McDaniel said he'll use running backs Omarion Hampton , Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell in probably every game this season, with the workload depending on the opponent and "hot hand." 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 During the first 11v11 period of Sunday's practice, the crowd roared for a Quentin Johnston reception that quarterback Justin Herbert perfectly placed by the outstretched arms of cornerback Nikko Reed .

 But had this not been training camp, Herbert likely would've been on his back or running for life before that ball had the chance to be released. Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu -- rushing from the interior on a front that featured Justin Eboigbe , Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack -- put a swift spin move on center Tyler Biadasz and was in Herbert's lap as the play was beginning. This sequence was a microcosm of Sunday's practice, as the defensive line controlled the day, constantly putting pressure on quarterbacks and stopping running plays before they could begin.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Branson Taylor , Kayode Awosika and Jake Slaughter rotated at left guard throughout practice. 
 Cornerback Tarheeb Still and left tackle Rashawn Slater both missed practice for a second straight day. Trey Pipkins and Taylor played left tackle in his absence. 
 Tre' Harris was active throughout practice with several receptions. 
 Avery Smith blew up a running play on a blitz, drawing celebrations from the defense. 
 Junior Colson pressured DJ Uiagalelei into a throw that landed in the hands of cornerback Isas Waxter , but Waxter dropped the interception. 
 Kyle Kennard had perhaps his best practice of camp, with several impressive wins in one-on-ones and pressures during 11-on-11 periods. 
 Trevor Penning had a good day, holding up well in one-on-ones and during team periods while working with the second and third groups. 
 Mesidor had one of the most impressive one-on-one wins of practice, beating Joe Alt cleanly with a spin move. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 

 Rookie left guard Jake Slaughter got his first reps with the group blocking for Justin Herbert in a padded practice this training camp. The Chargers drafted Slaughter -- who played only center in college -- to be the team's starter at left guard, but he seemed to fall out of favor through camp as veteran Kayode Awosika and second-year lineman Branson Taylor emerged.

 Slaughter fared well in his reps at guard, showing a firm anchor when pressured from defensive tackles and the ability to pick up defensive stunts. His best moment came on a pancake block of defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson , but he was also beaten badly on a rep by defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe .

 More observations: 

 
 Offensve lineman Trevor Penning appears to be falling back in the competition for the starting left guard job. He continues to work largely with the group, blocking for DJ Uiagalelei , though that could still change. 
 Rookie wide receiver Brenen Thompson made an impressive toe-tap catch down the left sideline that drew a roar from the crowd. 
 Outside linebacker Khalil Mack was explosive throughout practice and had several would-be sacks. Tuli Tuipulotu and Nadame Tucker were also consistently disruptive off the edge. 
 Defensive tackles Jamaree Caldwell , Teair Tart and Eboigbe continued to disrupt the run game and generate pressure on the quarterback. 
 Uiagalelei, may have had the throw of the day, a 50 or so yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Derius Davis . 
 Herbert continues to be sharp and on target with his receivers. It appears he -- and the other quarterbacks -- has grown comfortable with the timing of McDaniel's offense. Receivers are getting passes early and in space.

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Rams training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Rams' Myles Garrett misses practice again; Puka Nacua exits early 
 Sean McVay praises Aaron Donald as Rams await DT's decision 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 With Myles Garrett missing the Rams' joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys while dealing with swelling in his knee, outside linebackers Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart stood out as part of the Rams' pass rush.

 Rams head coach Sean McVay said he wanted to look back at the tape because he was bouncing between the two fields, but said he noticed the pressure from the Rams' edge rushers.

 "I did see that," McVay said. "... [Cowboys quarterback] Dak Prescott  does a good job being able to move in the pocket and I think there's some excellent players on the perimeter that we were able to get some really good looks at, but it did feel like those guys were able to make their presence felt."

 McVay said he's not concerned about Garrett missing time, saying the pass rusher told him he feels "about 85 percent" healthy.

 "When he's been out there, he has certainly made his impact felt, but we want to make sure that when he returns to play, he's able to return to full performance and feel like himself," McVay said.

 Other observations: 

 
 Cowboys linebacker Justin Barron had three interceptions on Tuesday, including one of Matthew Stafford . McVay said he thought Stafford "was great," during the practice but said "there was one where just a little bit late over the middle." McVay said in general, Stafford "kept the ball in play" and "saw coverage really well." 
 McVay said he hasn't made a decision on how he will handle the quarterback reps during the Rams' preseason opener in Kansas City on Saturday. McVay has previously said Stafford will not play and that rookie quarterback Ty Simpson will "definitely" play. McVay said he is still deciding whether Stetson Bennett IV will get reps during the preseason. 
 Similarly to how the Rams have operated throughout training camp, Bennett got most of the second-team reps against the Cowboys. 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Tuesday will mark the first joint practice of training camp for the Rams, as they will host the Dallas Cowboys at their Woodland Hills facility. Because head coach Sean McVay does not play his starters or key backups during the preseason, he especially values the chance to get his starters in these competitive, but more controlled environments.

 McVay said he tries to schedule at least two joint practices during the preseason; the Rams will host the New Orleans Saints for a joint practice on Aug. 20.

 The Rams don't gameplan for the practice, but McVay said he's looking forward to "the competition" of going against a different team than his players see practicing against each other.

 "I think when you go against each other as much as we've done up to this point, it's good to be able to just change it up and get a feel to go against different schemes and great players," McVay said.

 
 Monday's practice was a rest day for quarterback Matthew Stafford . He is scheduled to practice against the Cowboys on Tuesday. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 In the Rams' return to their Woodland Hills facility for the remainder of the preseason, "the defense was outstanding," coach Sean McVay said.

 "There was great coverage, some great individual plays, disrupting timing and rhythm," McVay said. "It was a great day for the defense. Offensively they were able to run the football with some success, but throwing and catching was a real struggle."

 McVay said he was not discouraged by the performance by the offense, because the takeaways "were more of a reflection of great individual plays than necessarily poor execution."

 "What I get upset about is when the other opponent or whether the other side of the ball doesn't have to earn it because it's sloppy -- whether it's poor execution or communication on one side or the other," McVay said. "The plays that happened today, there was a handful of turnovers, but I thought it was a really great reflection of excellent execution defensively, some outstanding individual plays. And sometimes that's the price of doing business."

 And that defense might even get stronger as the Rams await the news of a possible return from defensive tackle Aaron Donald. McVay said Saturday that he did not have an update on Donald's decision.

 Other observations: 

 
 First-round pick Ty Simpson will "definitely" play in the first preseason game next Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs , McVay said. 
 McVay said he has not made a decision on whether  Stetson Bennett IV  will play in the game. McVay typically does not play his starters or key backups in preseason games. Last year Jimmy Garoppolo , the Rams' established backup quarterback, did not play. Bennett and Simpson are competing to back up starting quarterback Matthew Stafford , but if Bennett does not play, that could be an indication he will start the season in the backup role. 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Much of the talk during Rams training camp has been about a player not currently on the roster: Aaron Donald.

 On Thursday, as the Rams concluded training camp at Loyola Marymount University, coach Sean McVay said he didn't have an answer on whether the defensive tackle would come out of retirement.

 And if Donald does return? While defensive coordinator Chris Shula emphasized he's focusing on the roster guys now, he said, "I think I'd be lying if I said I hadn't thought about" the possibility of pairing up Donald and reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 "You're anticipating, but at the same time, we're putting it in the core of our defense right now," Shula said. "We're building our defense step by step. If he decides to come, whenever that is, that's not going to affect exactly how we're doing it right now."

 McVay said Thursday that if Donald comes back, "those are things that you have to be able to figure out on the fly."

 "But what we are focusing on is the guys that are here," McVay said. "And then if Aaron is a part of it, it's obviously going to add value to our group, which is a positive."

 Another observation: 

 
 Thursday was the Rams' final practice at LMU before they head back to their team facility in Woodland Hills for the remainder of the preseason. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 The Rams had a familiar face at their team facility this week, as Aaron Donald's name appeared on the NFL's transaction wire on Wednesday as a player taking part in a tryout for the team.

 The workout had to be reported to the league because it was supervised by a member of the Rams' football staff. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula said he was not at the Woodland Hills facility for the tryout, but said he talked to defensive line coach Giff Smith afterward.

 Last week, Rams head coach Sean McVay said he doesn't expect Donald to make a decision about coming out of retirement until after the team returns to its facility in Woodland…

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Under the bright lights at Allegiant Stadium on Tuesday, the connection between rookies Fernando Mendoza and Malik Benson continued to thrive.

 In the team's final practice before the preseason opener against the Arizona Cardinals , Mendoza relied heavily on the sixth-round wide receiver. He connected with Benson on an out route while playing with the second-team offense. Later in practice, Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage to Benson on a slant route.

 Benson said he and Mendoza began developing a strong bond when they first met at the scouting combine in February -- two months before they officially became teammates. The former Oregon pass catcher said after they were both drafted by the Raiders, he wanted to make sure he could be a player who Mendoza could rely on.

 That has been the case since OTAs and mandatory minicamp.

 "I know, when it comes to Sundays, when it comes to practice, he's going to rely on me to be in that spot, and I'm going to rely on him to place the ball where it needs to be placed," Benson said.

 Overall, Mendoza was solid in what can be described as a light practice. The only blemish on his performance was a tipped pass and interception by linebacker Cody Lindenberg .

 More observations: 

 
 Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . missed his fourth straight practice. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford did not wear a red non-contact jersey and was a full participant during practice. He recorded a sack on Mendoza while playing with the second-team defense. 
 Quarterback  Aidan O'Connell  had the best throw of the evening --- a 55-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Brandon Johnson during the 7-on-7 period. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 

 Maybe coach Klint Kubiak's decision to hold Kirk Cousins from Saturday's practice due to his scuffle with Maxx Crosby sparked a fire within the veteran quarterback. Maybe it didn't. Either way, Cousins had his best performance of training camp.

 Monday featured Cousins fitting the ball into tight windows and effectively conducting two-minute drives. He threw a touchdown pass to Brock Bowers in the corner of the end zone despite tight coverage from Taron Johnson . Both players later connected on a deep pass over the middle, positioning the offense near the goal line.

 Cousins delivered a nice pass to wide receiver Tre Tucker on a crossing route with rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses in coverage. He also connected with Malik Benson , who made a contested catch against cornerback Darien Porter .

 During the two-minute period, Cousins completed four passes, including a touchdown throw to wide receiver Jalen Nailor .

 Fernando Mendoza , on the other hand, went back to playing with the second-team offense. He didn't put together his best performance. He ran into running back Dare Ogunbowale during the handoff exchange.

 He threw his third interception of camp. Mendoza attempted a pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins on an out route. Greedy Vance was in front of Thompkins in man coverage, and Mendoza threw the ball directly into the second-year defensive back's hands.

 His best throw -- a back-shoulder pass to Benson -- was called back because he was sacked on the play.

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Kwity Paye returned to practice, but did not participate in the team period. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford practiced, but wore a red non-contact jersey. Guard Caleb Rogers , tight end Carter Runyon and wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . did not participate. 
 From a health standpoint, rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy said he feels closer to how he was in 2024. McCoy, who missed the entire 2025 college football season at Tennessee, said the Raiders' rehab plan has him feeling much better. "I'm still getting there. It's been a long time since I really played football. 
 McCoy mentioned that the biggest challenge was getting back into football shape and pre-snap stuff. McCoy felt rusty during the first day of camp, but was comfortable by Day 3. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 With  Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby  not practicing for violating team rules ,  Fernando Mendoza  played with the starters for the first time in camp.

 Mendoza had his good and bad moments. He overthrew wide receiver Jack Bech a couple of times. And he had trouble securing the ball when snapped to him by Tyler Linderbaum and Jordan Meredith .

 Mendoza, however, didn't get flustered. He had one of his best throws of camp during the red zone period. He threw a touchdown pass to Tre Tucker , in which he zipped the ball through tight coverage by cornerback Taron Johnson .

 Mendoza also threw touchdowns to tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer .

 The highlight of the day was Mendoza's efficiency during the two-minute period to close out practice. He completed five straight passes, including a throw to Tucker in tight coverage, to set up a field goal from kicker Matt Gay .

 During Mendoza's reps with the first-team, quarterback coach Mike Sullivan said the biggest things he was evaluating were the rookie's command of the offense and not panicking in the pocket. Sullivan added that the team is pleased with Mendoza's development.

 Mendoza's comfort and command of the operation have grown since the spring. Sullivan has also noticed improvement in Mendoza's play from under center.

 Other observation: 

 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor and running back Dare Ogunbowale returned to practice after being sidelined Friday. Defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , wide receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr.  and tight end Carter Runyon did not participate.

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Friday was an eventful morning at Raiders HQ.

 Las Vegas' eighth practice was highlighted by a scuffle between Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins . Other than that, both sides made plays throughout the team's third padded practice.

 Cousins was picked off twice in the red zone. First, Crosby disrupted Cousins' pass attempt, causing the ball to be picked off by safety Jeremy Chinn . On the following play, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted Cousins in the back corner of the end zone.

 

 Cousins responded well. He connected with tight ends  Michael Mayer  and Brock Bowers on a few big throws in the middle of the field. He was even efficient during the two-minute period near the end of practice, quickly moving the offense down the field into field-goal range.

 Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . had an explosive run, in which he ran over cornerback Jermod McCoy and continued to sprint down the field for a big gain.

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 After his first public practice with the Vikings this spring, Kyler Murray uttered a four-word phrase that hovered over the team's quarterback competition all summer.

 "My confidence," Murray said in May, "is unshakeable."

 That helps explain why Murray didn't sound much different Tuesday after coach Kevin O'Connell named him the team's starter as the third week of training camp began. Murray said he did not expect to be handed the job and acknowledged that not every practice this summer has gone smoothly as he split reps with J.J. McCarthy .

 "There's going to be good days," Murray said. "There's going to be bad days. We're facing adversity every single day. But I'm definitely getting more comfortable as each day goes."

 Murray had a sharp practice Tuesday while taking all of the first-team reps for the first time since Week 5 of last season when he was with the Arizona Cardinals . McCarthy said he would address the decision publicly Wednesday.

 More observations:  

 
 Right guard Will Fries did not practice Tuesday. He was replaced on the first team by second-year guard Joe Huber . 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 As the third week of training camp began in the evening, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was not ready to name a winner in the QB1 competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy .

 "Nothing has really changed from a standpoint of the timeline and things like that," O'Connell said before the Vikings took the field at TCO Stadium for their annual night practice. "So we'll see how the reps continue to go and when we feel like we're at that place, we're going to make sure we communicate that both in house and internally and obviously to you guys as soon as possible."

 The Vikings have a scheduled off day Monday to reset the competition if they desire. Murray entered training camp as the favorite for the job, and sources say they believe he still is. Asked Sunday where Murray is in the offensive system compared to where he thought he would be at this point, O'Connell said: "I think mentally he's definitely probably ahead of where I thought." O'Connell went on to say there are some parts of the offense that are new to everyone.

 
 It was a rough practice for the offense as defensive pressure made it difficult for quarterbacks Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy to get into a rhythm. Murray threw two interceptions, to cornerbacks James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers , the latter when he was scrambling and tried to get the ball to Justin Jefferson on the sideline. McCarthy continued his theme of hitting deep out routes, including another to receiver Myles Price . McCarthy completed a deep pass to Jefferson down the right sideline but it forced Jefferson to slow down to bring it in, and he struggled later in a red zone drill. 
 Part of the protection issue was caused by the absence of left tackle Christian Darrisaw , who took a veteran's rest day. The Vikings also rested rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks , who remains on a maintenance plan to ensure full recovery from a broken left foot. 
 Defensive linemen Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins also sat out the practice, giving rookie nose tackle Domonique Orange extensive first-team action. 
 Safety Jay Ward is in the latter stages of the concussion protocol, O'Connell said. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Two members of the Vikings' draft class -- both Day 3 picks -- made splash plays during a low-key practice.

 Rookie tailback Demond Claiborne ran about 70 yards off left tackle using a nifty jump cut to get outside. Claiborne, a sixth-round pick from Wake Forest, has mostly worked with the third team behind Aaron Jones Sr . and Jordan Mason . He could also get some work as a kick returner during the preseason.

 Meanwhile, cornerback Charles Demmings -- a fifth-round pick from Stephen F. Austin -- broke up a J.J. McCarthy pass intended for receiver Tai Felton near the goal line. For Demmings, it was the latest in a series of pass breakups, including two earlier in camp while he was defending Justin Jefferson . The Vikings seem to have their top three cornerbacks set with Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre , and it is always dangerous to get too excited when a rookie makes splash plays. But to this point, he has demonstrated he could provide an immediate contribution this season should defensive coordinator Brian Flores need him. 

 Other observations: 

 
 Veteran Jamal Adams said he appreciates the Vikings giving him a chance to work at safety, the position the New York Jets drafted him as in 2017, and that his new number of 32 is "definitely a better feeling" than the number he opened camp with (54). But Adams agreed it was likely he will also resume his linebacker duties at times in Flores' scheme. "I think it's going to be a little bit of everything, just being versatile in a lot of ways," he said. 
 Adams continued to get first-team work at safety in some packages with fellow safeties Jay Ward and Jakobe Thomas sitting out team drills. 
 Right tackle Brian O'Neill appeared to be taking a veteran's rest day. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison (left thumb) caught passes from quarterbacks for the first time since he suffered the injury while working in some team drills. 
 The Vikings will have their annual night practice Sunday at TCO Stadium. 
 

 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 NFL training camps can be tediously routine at times, but some days close observers can be surprised.

 The Vikings changed linebacker Jamal Adams ' jersey number from 54 to 32 and worked him in some of their safety specialty packages during full-team drills. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is well known for experimenting with personnel during training camp, and it's quite possible that Adams could alternate between linebacker and safety.

 Two other safeties, Jay Ward and rookie Jakobe Thomas , did not appear to be taking part in team drills.

 According to NFL rules, linebackers can wear numbers between 1-59 (and also 90-99). But defensive backs can't wear numbers higher than 49, which necessitated Adams' number change.

 Adams was drafted as a safety by the Jets in 2017, but he moved to linebacker for the Raiders last season. The Vikings signed him on the eve of training camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback J.J. McCarthy had one of his better days of camp as the competition with Kyler Murray continued. McCarthy hit wide receiver  Dontae Fleming  on a deep out, a route McCarthy has excelled at this summer, and also threw three touchdowns in a four-play red zone sequence. 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug.5 
 The Vikings haven't won a playoff game since 2019 and have three playoff victories in the past 25 seasons. So during his annual training camp meeting with reporters,…

title: What Kyler Murray as QB1 means for Vikings, J.J. McCarthy
summary: McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in 2024, will take a back seat to offseason addition Murray. Here's what we know.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- No one should be surprised that Kyler Murray won the Minnesota Vikings ' quarterback competition.

 Murray demonstrated this spring that he had recovered from a foot injury that limited him last season with the Arizona Cardinals . From that point on, it was clear that his talent level represented a formidable obstacle for the Vikings' incumbent, J.J. McCarthy . 

 Murray got a bit bogged down in a complicated offense toward the end of minicamp, which he noted was happening while getting only half the reps that a starter normally would, and then again during the second week of training camp. But at some point, coach Kevin O'Connell had to make a call. It came Tuesday .

 What went into the decision? Is Murray the Vikings' long-term answer, or could McCarthy one day reemerge? Let's take a closer look. 

 

 

 Was Murray's win inevitable? 
 No, but he was always a heavy favorite. 

 This was a genuine competition in the sense that the best quarterback on the roster would start and neither would benefit from an off-field advantage. There would be no organizational inertia toward finances -- the Vikings are paying Murray the veteran's minimum of $1.3 million, while McCarthy is in the third year of his rookie contract -- nor toward draft status. The general manager who traded up to draft McCarthy No. 10 in 2024, Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, was fired in January. O'Connell was free to simply pick the best player, which turned out to be Murray, the No. 1 pick by Arizona in 2019.

 Murray faced some potential roadblocks given his recent injury history -- he has played fewer than 10 games in two of his past three seasons -- and the fact that McCarthy had a two-year head start on learning O'Connell's scheme. But once Murray showed he was healthy, his inherent skill set advantage was obvious to any objective observer.

 

 Did Murray perform well in camp -- or just better than McCarthy? 

 This gets to the crux of the matter moving forward. It's one thing to be the best quarterback on a roster. It's quite another for Murray to have positioned himself to power an explosive offense during a regular season that will start with crucial games against two NFC North rivals, the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears , in its first two weeks.

 

 Murray had some intriguing days when he appeared to move through his reads in rhythm and find open downfield receivers, sometimes after breaking the pocket. He also demonstrated his ability to rescue broken plays with his speed and open-field running.

 But in the three practices leading up to O'Connell's announcement, Murray struggled. To top it off, he threw two interceptions -- and barely missed throwing a third -- during the Vikings' annual full-pads night stadium practice on Sunday. There were other days when his passes misfired, although usually it appeared less an accuracy issue than it was that he was still learning exactly where to place the ball.

 The most charitable way to put it is that through two weeks of practice, Murray has shown that he has a long way to go before anyone should believe he is ready to have the kind of season that would revitalize his career. 

 

 So why did the decision come now? 

 O'Connell had boxed himself in. He acknowledged Tuesday that his plan had always been to make a decision in this time period, about nine or 10 practices into training camp, to allow enough time for Murray and the offense to come together before the regular season begins.

 

 When that time arrived, neither quarterback had established himself. But O'Connell prioritized maximizing the time remaining before the start of the season. He also reiterated that part of the point of the competition was creating "a competitive environment filled with wildly capable players that could then obviously elevate our quarterback room through that process and in doing so elevate our team."

 To that point, while Murray has not had an eye-opening camp, it is more than reasonable to believe the Vikings would get better quarterback play from him this season than from McCarthy.

 

 Can Murray run the Vikings' offense? 

 That remains to be seen, in part because the Vikings are perhaps coincidentally in the process of adjusting their offense in ways that would benefit him.

 They have been experimenting with more shotgun and pistol run plays after spending the third-most time (47%) under center during O'Connell's first four seasons in Minnesota. During Murray's time with the Arizona Cardinals , the team was under center at the league's third-lowest rate (18.3%).

 Murray has displayed superior arm talent to McCarthy in getting the ball to downfield receivers, a big part of O'Connell's offense. But in team drills during full-pads practices, when pass rushers are active, Murray has not always appeared to see whether receivers are open in the middle of the field. That will no doubt be a focus during the coming weeks. 

 

 

 What does this mean for McCarthy? 

 It's bad news, obviously, but in truth that news was delivered the moment the Vikings signed Murray.

 McCarthy finished the 2025 season on an upswing, ranking No. 7 in QBR (69.8) after Week 13. But he would have still needed to make significant progress this offseason and summer to mount a true challenge.

 

 Instead, his level of improvement was incremental at best. It was not nearly enough, and O'Connell's decision to end the competition at a down point in Murray's training camp performance was a reflection of how difficult it was going to be for McCarthy to win.

 He'll enter his third NFL season as a backup, and there is not much precedent for top-10 picks getting replaced in the offseason -- as McCarthy was, for all intents and purposes -- and then coming back to regain the organization's permanent starting job.

 O'Connell said he "absolutely" thinks McCarthy has a future with the organization. But the next opportunity might not happen unless Murray is injured, a possibility that merits a close eye due to recent history.

 

 Will the Vikings trade McCarthy? 

 While O'Connell gushed over how McCarthy has handled training camp, and the months that preceded it, a trade can't be ruled out. The Vikings re-signed their 2025 backup, Carson Wentz , in March and he has worked as the No. 3 quarterback in camp. O'Connell confirmed that McCarthy will be the No. 2 quarterback, but Wentz's presence shouldn't be discounted. If the Vikings had deep conviction about McCarthy's future, they wouldn't have felt compelled to sign Murray and would have given McCarthy more than 10 starts to develop. 

 

 What does this mean for WR  Justin Jefferson and the rest of the franchise? 
 Murray will be the Vikings' fourth different Week 1 starter in the past four seasons. After he struggled to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, with McCarthy and then-rookie Max Brosmer starting 12 combined games, Jefferson has a better chance of elevating his production if Murray plays a full season.

 But Murray's ascension, and McCarthy's demotion, continues a decadeslong organizational tradition of plucking veteran quarterbacks for potentially short-term roles. During O'Connell's tenure alone, he'll be the ninth different quarterback to start a regular-season game.

 The Vikings agreed to a contract clause that prohibits them from using the franchise tag to retain Murray in 2027. So if he has a career season, he will have a clear path to the free agent market and a potential bidding war. If he struggles or is injured, it's hard to project the Vikings' interest in bringing him back.

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Drake Maye isn't expected to play in Thursday's preseason opener against the Colts, coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday.

 "That's where my mindset is right now, standing here today," Vrabel said before Tuesday's joint practice with the Colts in Foxborough. "That can always change, but I wouldn't anticipate that happening right now."

 Vrabel noted that Tuesday's practice essentially takes the place of the game for Maye & Co.

 "That's really the only reason that we do these joint practices. It will be a lot of the front-line players and whoever's available [in the practice]. Some of the guys that maybe will not get as much work will get extensive work in the game on Thursday," he said.

 The plan for practice was to have the offense take 24 full-team reps, which Vrabel pointed out was more than Maye & Co. would likely see in a preseason game.

 Maye's final rep in practice wasn't to his liking, as he threw an end zone interception to Colts safety Cam Bynum on a second-down play in the two-minute drill. Otherwise, he was pleased with the Patriots' effort, energy and execution.

 "We challenged our guys to be consistent throughout the day, and I think they responded to that," Maye said.

 More observations: 

 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez missed his first practice of training camp. It might have been related to his final play of Monday's practice, when he landed hard in the end zone while defending WR Romeo Doubs . Gonzalez has also been in negotiations with the team on a contract extension. 
 With Gonzalez and fellow starting CB Carlton Davis III not practicing, and top backup Charles Woods also out, any evaluation of the pass defense came with a caveat. The Colts were without two top WRs, however. 
 The Colts' first units on offense/defense won the end-of-practice two-minute drill, while the Patriots' second units were victorious -- QB Tommy DeVito connecting with WR Mack Hollins on a long TD and S John Saunders Jr . notching an INT. 
 DeVito had another deep ball earlier in practice as speedy WR Kyle Williams got behind the defense and tracked the ball well. 
 With the Patriots' first-unit offense on one field and the first-unit defense on the other, Vrabel stayed with the offense. That left assistant head coach Terrell Williams and coordinator Zak Kuhr to lead the defensive field. 
 WR A.J. Brown had an active practice, with Maye looking in his direction often. He was charted with five receptions. 
 Starting LB Christian Elliss limped off early in practice. 
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson as a reliable pass catcher in the red zone has been a theme in recent days. He had another TD catch from Maye that had the crowd buzzing. 
 Colts DT Grover Stewart powered into LG Alijah Vera-Tucker on one play and got his hands up to bat down a pass. 
 OLB Elijah Ponder had the Patriots' most decisive PBU, getting his hands up at the line to swat away a pass from QB Daniel Jones . 
 Owners Robert Kraft (Patriots) and Carly Irsay-Gordon (Colts) watched practice together at one point. 
 Former Patriots safety Devin McCourty was in attendance to sign autographs. 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 10 
 First-round draft pick Caleb Lomu has been a full participant in all 13 training camp practices, and he shared insight Monday on the top thing he has learned.

 "The biggest thing is really focusing on not so many things. On defense, these guys are coming off the ball, they know their assignment, and everyone on the field has to know what they're doing. If you're thinking about multiple things, and if you hesitate at all for a quick second, the guy on the other side of the line is going to beat you.

 "Coming out here, at first I was thinking a lot and that caused me to play a little slower. I realized you can't think too much. You have to trust in what you learned in the classroom and go out and play ball."

 The 28th pick, Lomu had mostly been working at right tackle until the team's 12th practice last Friday, which was an intrasquad scrimmage. He flipped more to the left side that day, and that continued Monday in a practice held in shorts and light shoulder pads, as he was the backup left tackle behind Will Campbell .

 Lomu played left tackle at Utah, so he noted changing sides has been an adjustment with the different footwork and hand placement, among other things. But he said he feels comfortable on both sides.

 He shared that his primary focus at practice Monday was playing with "tight hands" and not giving up his chest to pass rushers. He appeared to have one of his better days in drills.

 More observations: 

 
 WR Romeo Doubs caught a leaping TD from QB Drake Maye to cap off a "game-ending" drive despite being blanketed by CB Christian Gonzalez . Doubs crashed to the ground, and fellow WRs Efton Chism III and Kayshon Boutte gave him a mock-CPR celebration by pumping his chest. 
 Chism showed strong hands at the catch point, leaping over CB Marcellas Dial Jr . to catch a TD pass from QB Tommy DeVito to produce another offensive highlight. 
 CB Kindle Vildor had one of the top defensive plays of the day, running stride for stride with Doubs along the right sideline and turning at the last moment to bat away a pass from Maye. 
 WR Kyle Williams hauled in a long bomb from DeVito along the left sideline (CB Channing Canada  was closest in coverage), which was a result of high-level tracking of the football. But Williams later dropped a short pass on a crossing route. 
 TE Hunter Henry , fresh off signing a two-year contract extension, caught a laser from DeVito for a TD at the goal line in red zone work. 
 With starting DT Christian Barmore missing his second straight practice (injury unknown), 2025 fourth-round pick Joshua Farmer aligned with the top defense alongside fellow DTs Milton Williams and Cory Durden . 
 Starting CB Carlton Davis III , who had been sidelined since July 28 with what appeared to be a hamstring injury, returned to practice for the first time on a limited basis. 
 Rookie OLB Gabe Jacas (second round, Illinois) had a speed rush in one-on-one drills that helped produce what looked like a decisive win over backup RT Marcus Bryant . 
 Likewise, rookie OLB Quintayvious Hutchins (seventh round, Boston College) had a decisive win with an inside move on rookie OT Dametrious Crownover (sixth round, Texas A&M) in one-on-one drills. 
 Long-snapper Julian Ashby didn't practice due to an ankle injury that isn't expected to keep him out long. The team signed snapper Niko Lalos  and moved on from OL Caedan Wallace to make room for him. 
 

 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 
 A middle linebacker running a time of 4.77 seconds in the 40-yard dash isn't ideal, so when the Patriots hosted…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New Orleans Saints ' camp is taking place in Metairie, Louisiana, and Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. We will update this file often. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Offense and defense went at each other in an unscripted red zone scenario to end practice. The first side to 18 points won, with four points given to the defense if they held the offense to a field goal, three points to the offense for a made field goal, and seven points for a touchdown or turnover.

 The defense went up 4-3 after Charlie Smyth kicked a field goal for the first unit. Tanner Brown kicked a field goal for the second team after after  Martin Emerson Jr . broke up a Spencer Rattler pass on third down. With the defense up 8-6, Carl Granderson almost picked off Tyler Shough and then did manage to snag the ball three plays later, before punting it in celebration. That put the defense up 13-6, and Zach Wilson took advantage of an offsides penalty to throw a touchdown to Barion Brown to tie things up.

 The first-team offense took over with a chance to win outright, but Quincy Riley picked off Shough in the end zone, giving the defense the win. Coach Kellen Moore said the idea was to create a competitive environment. "It's just play ball and defense has the opportunity to score and obviously they won the day in the red zone," he said.

 Other observations:  

 
 The Saints first-team offense had multiple false starts during team periods. 
 Shough threw a touchdown to Juwan Johnson with Kool-Aid McKinstry in coverage during an early team period. 
 The two kickers had previously alternated practices, now they'll alternate kicks during practice moving forward. Brown went 7-of-7 and Smyth went 5-of-6. 
 Devin Neal worked off to the side with an athletic trainer. Rejzohn Wright left with a hip injury, Davon Godchaux left with an ankle injury.  
 Jeremiah Wright returned to practice, while  Cameron Jordan  did not practice with a hamstring injury. Kendre Miller ,  Chris Rumph II and John Ridgeway III  did not practice. 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 
 Sunday's practice featured the most 11-on-11 work yet, and it was an up-and-down day for the first-team offense.

 Quarterback Tyler Shough got off to a quick start with completions to Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson in his first session. He was able to roll out and find Olave after an incompletion to Juwan Johnson . Later, Shough had three straight completions to Johnson, Olave and Tyson after a miss to Olave, but the offense was flagged for a false start, and then Shough was sacked on the next play. Shough targeted Olave downfield on the next session but couldn't connect and then was sacked before a completion to Travis Etienne Jr . His next period had completions to Etienne and Olave before he ran it himself for a first down. The unit finished the day working specifically on third down, and Shough had a completion to Noah Fant , incompletions to Vele and Barion Brown (with good coverage by Kool-Aid McKinstry ), and a completion to Tyson.

 Other observations:  

 
 Cesar Ruiz was back at starting right guard after playing second-team center Saturday. 
 Reserve guard Dillon Radunz is done for the season with a torn ACL. 
 Defensive end Cameron Jordan has a hamstring issue that could cause him to miss time in training camp. He was not at practice Sunday. 
 Kicker Charlie Smyth had his second straight three-miss day. After missing three kicks in a row during his last practice session Thursday, he went 4-of-7, missing from 47 and 56 yards and then missing a 50-yard field goal in the two-minute drill. 
 Alvin Kamara and Zach Wood were back at practice after attending Drew Brees' Hall of Fame ceremony (Jordan attended as well). 
 Rookie Bryce Lance had the play of the day, scoring a touchdown after a deep pass by Spencer Rattler . Running back CJ Donaldson had an impressive run with the third-team offense. 
 Quarterback Zach Wilson threw a deep touchdown to Ronnie Bell with the third-team offense. 
 John Ridgeway III  and Pete Werner left early with injuries. 
 Olave and Julian Blackmon practiced after both dealt with injuries in Saturday's practice. 
 Devin Neal , Kendre Miller , Christen Miller , Jeremiah Wright , Rejzohn Wright , Bub Means (personal) didn't practice. 
 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 It was Drew Brees day at practice as the former Saints quarterback goes into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

 The Saints painted a No. 9 on the practice field, and the staff, including coach Kellen Moore, wore No. 9 shirts. Running back  Alvin Kamara , defensive end  Cameron Jordan and long-snapper Zach Wood , along with coaches Josh Hill and Joel Thomas, were absent to watch the enshrinement in Canton, Ohio, but are expected back tomorrow.

 But the excitement of Brees being enshrined wore off early as the Saints dealt with some injuries. Offensive guard  Dillon Radunz  (knee) limped off the field after going up against Vernon Broughton in a one-on-one rep and did not return, while starting safety Julian Blackmon also left with a knee injury.

 Wide receiver Chris Olave walked to the sideline late in practice and had his wrist inspected and taped by athletic trainers before returning to take part in a "run down the clock" sequence at the end of practice, where he made a contested catch across the middle.

 Jordyn Tyson also had back-to-back catches from Tyler Shough in team drills, including one that Shough floated over the head of a defender attempting to break up a pass.

 Other observations:  

 
 Defensive tackle  John Ridgeway III  took over long-snapping duties with Wood out. 
 William Sherman played first-team right guard with Radunz out. The usual starting right guard, Cesar Ruiz , played second-team center. Moore said that was part of the plan to get Ruiz snaps there and that he will play in that position tomorrow as well. 
 Kicker Tanner Brown was 4-of-6 with misses from 39 and 54 yards. 
 Travis Etienne Jr . got all the first-team reps at running back.  
 Jordan Howden played first-team safety with Blackmon out. 
 Isaiah Stalbird intercepted Spencer Rattler in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Kendre Miller (back), Devin Neal (hamstring), Rejzohn Wright , Christen Miller (toe),  Chris Rumph II  (ankle) missed practice. 
 This was a scheduled shorter practice intended to end at 10:30 in front of the fans, but the Saints had to finish the final minutes inside because of lightning in the area.  
 New linebacker Deion Jones was at practice and wearing No. 45. 
 The Saints waived injured player Zxavian Harris . 
 

 

 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Rookie wide receiver Barion Brown continues to be the rising star of camp after he concluded Thursday's practice with a 46-yard touchdown from Spencer Rattler to finish out the two-minute drill.

 "Spencer got out of it -- we'll watch the film to see if there's a sack.…
