title: 2026 Washington Commanders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Commanders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Washington Commanders camp is taking place in Ashburn, Virginia, and Commanders reporter John Keim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Commanders camp. We will update this file often. Can Washington bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Commanders camp 
 
 Stefon Diggs settles in with Commanders, ups NFL best talk 
 Daniels finds voice, aims to fill leadership void 
 Commanders tab ex-All-Pro WR Wes Welker to coach tight ends 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 The Washington Commanders ' offensive line could get reinforcements soon with center Nick Allegretti  possibly set to return from a strained calf muscle.

 He suffered the injury on July 29 and hasn't practiced since, but coach Dan Quinn said there's a good chance he'll return next week. Washington will hold a joint practice Wednesday with Miami before playing the Dolphins in the preseason opener Friday night.

 They will conduct a walk-through Sunday when Allegretti could rejoin his teammates on the field. He and tight end John Bates (hamstring) have been working on a side field this week with the strength and conditioning coaches and athletic trainers.

 Getting Allegretti back can help start to settle the line, which lost its top player in tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps. Allegretti is considered the favorite to start at center. Bates, too, might return at this time. He's a crucial part of their run blocking.

 Washington coach Dan Quinn said the early disruption along the line is "not ideal, but it's not unusual." And he said he liked the Commanders' line depth entering camp -- pointing to Coleman, who had been competing with Chris Paul to start at left guard, and veteran Andrew Wylie , who typically fills in at both spots on the right side.

 Meanwhile, Wylie said that after his triceps surgery Tunsil told his teammates that he will undergo his treatment at the Commanders' facility rather than at home in Houston, as is customary with many players expected to miss significant time.

 Also, corner Trey Amos (ankle) will not practice Wednesday nor will he play Friday. He'll be re-evaluated Sunday.

 More observations: 

 
 A number of Commanders players did not practice Tuesday after a two-hour session in full pads Monday and the joint session Wednesday. Among the group sitting out: receivers Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs ; defensive linemen Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw and linebackers Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson . Safety Jeremy Reaves , corner Amik Robertson and tight end Ben Sinnott . 
 Tight end Colson Yankoff made multiple catches in practice Tuesday and has had a productive camp as a pass-catcher. His best catch occurred earlier this week when he made a one-handed grab. And, last week, he leapt high for a pass down the middle of the field for a catch -- and hung onto the ball despite hitting the ground hard. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Washington Commanders cornerback  Trey Amos will miss the next "day or two" after injuring his ankle during practice Saturday.

 "We'll see where he's at in the next day or so," coach Dan Quinn said.

 Amos had just returned to practice Friday after opening on the physically unable to perform list. He suffered a fractured fibula in Week 10 last season but was dealing with a soft-tissue injury prior to camp.

 On Saturday, Amos sprinted downfield with receiver Terry McLaurin on a deep ball in full-team work that he defended. But the way he landed on his ankle led to soreness, and he exited the field.

 Amos and Mike Sainristil were Washington's only returning corners with substantive play time. But the Commanders fortified their corner depth this offseason by signing Amik Robertson ,  Rasul Douglas  and  Fabian Moreau .

 Amos was arguably Washington's top corner in 2025 before getting hurt.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Jake Moody continues to struggle. He has 11 missed field goal attempts in his past four practices, including four on Monday (from 44, 49, 51 and 55 yards). He made 18-of-20 field goals for Washington and Chicago last season but has struggled of late. Drew Stevens also missed three in practice Monday (43, 51 and 55 yards). 
 On quarterback Jayden Daniels ' first play from scrimmage he connected on a deep ball with receiver Dyami Brown down the right side. Daniels also hit Stefon Diggs on the right side, after sliding a yard or two to his right. Daniels did a good job finding Diggs, throwing with trust to a spot. Daniels and Diggs continue to spend time together -- they had breakfast together before practice. "He's as accurate as he's ever been," offensive coordinator David Blough said of Daniels. 
 Diggs has spent time each practice going over plays and routes with receivers coach Bobby Engram, as others work on special teams. Engram will discuss the play, and Diggs will walk through his responsibility. 
 

 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Left tackle Laremy Tunsil left practice after a one-on-one rep versus linebacker Odafe Oweh and was being evaluated for what appeared to be an upper-body injury. Oweh rushed to the inside, with his left hand at Tunsil's right shoulder.

 Corner Trey Amos also left practice early, returning to the building along with Tunsil. Amos returned to practice Friday after being activated off the physically unable to perform list. He fractured his fibula in Week 10 last season but also dealt with a soft-tissue injury in the spring.

 It's uncertain why Amos had to leave practice. He did participate in some full-team work before exiting, running downfield on a deep post to receiver Terry McLaurin on one play that resulted in pass interference. 

 Washington's players are off Sunday so coach Dan Quinn won't provide updates on the players until practice resumes Monday morning.

 Other observations:  

 
 Brandon Coleman and  Chris Paul  continue to rotate with the first group as they compete for the starting left guard position. Paul started 15 games at the position, taking over for Coleman. 
 Quinn said center Nick Allegretti (calf strain) and tight end John Bates (strained hamstring) will miss another week of practice. Both were injured on the first day of practice. Washington will practice three days next week, including a joint session with Miami on Wednesday before playing the Dolphins in the preseason opener Friday. 
 With Allegretti out, Washington signed two centers -- Trey Hill and Daniel Brunskill -- and guard Max Scharping . The Commanders were thin at center before his injury. Brunskill offers experience, having started 71 games in his seven-year career at guard, center and right tackle. The Commanders also signed tackle Nicholas Petit-Frere . 
 Undrafted rookie receiver  Jaden Bradley  made two nice catches Saturday. The first catch was on a nice throw from quarterback Marcus Mariota on an out route -- just over corner Fabian Moreau and Bradley made a leaping catch. Later, on a pass that might have been tipped at the line he had to stretch out to his left to make the grab. 
 Receiver Stefon Diggs was more active, catching several passes in full-team work. On one, the offense put the defensive backs in a bind -- the safety had to run with another target and the corner had to move up to cover someone on an out. That left Diggs in a soft spot for a long gain.

title: Brandon Coleman eager to fill in for injured Laremy Tunsil
summary: Coleman joined Laremy Tunsil for offseason workouts at his home then found out he'd have to replace him for a good portion of 2026.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders tackle Brandon Coleman picked the right offseason to know that something needed to change. He wanted to improve his durability. He wanted to eat better.

 And he wanted to train better -- so he convinced his wife they needed to spend time this summer, as he said, in the middle of Alabama working out.

 Now he hopes those changes help him with another one: Coleman will shift from left guard to left tackle, replacing the injured Laremy Tunsil , who will undergo surgery to repair a torn triceps and miss a significant portion of the season. Quinn said they won't know the exact timetable until after the surgery.

 

 Without Tunsil, Washington will have to at least alter part of its offensive approach. As coach Dan Quinn said, he was at the "top of his game."

 The Commanders could use more tight ends to help Coleman -- Tunsil was part of a double-team pass block only 31.5% of the time; Coleman was part of one 42.1% of the time in each of his first two seasons.

 Washington also will use more play-action passes from under center -- designed to fool coverages and slow the pass rush.

 There's also quarterback Jayden Daniels, about whom one AFC executive said "covers up for a lot of sins." Indeed, in practice Daniels has excelled at sliding in the pocket to avoid pressure and find an open target. It helps, too, that Washington just signed receiver  Stefon Diggs to pair with Terry McLaurin  -- both of whom can create quick separation. And that would help offset the loss of a player such as Tunsil.

 But Coleman's play will matter as well. He did post a 92.3% pass block win rate the past two seasons. He also had a run block win rate of 77.2%, above the league average of 72.3% in that same period.

 That's why Washington trusts Coleman; after this offseason, he said he's learned to trust himself.

 "I have the athleticism, I have the strength," he said, "and it's just to learn that I'm able to do whatever I want to. It's just about having the mindset."

 Washington won't know how long Coleman will have to start at tackle until after Tunsil's surgery. He's expected to miss significant time. After an injury-filled season -- 10 projected starters or key backups missed at least seven games apiece -- it was a difficult development early in camp.

 

 Tunsil's loss is a sizeable one for Washington. He was one of its impact players -- general manager Adam Peters has called him "one of the best, if not the best" players at his position. Washington traded four picks to Houston to acquire the five-time Pro Bowler in March 2025.

 But the Commanders opted to promote Coleman rather than sign someone from outside the organization. They point to his athleticism, his experience with 18 starts at left tackle, including three in the postseason. They drafted him in the third round for a reason in 2024; now he has to fulfill that promise.

 Offensive coordinator David Blough said Coleman's face "lit up" when they told him he'd be the starting left tackle.

 "His speed, athleticism just flashes every time you turn that film on," Blough said. "We've seen a young man grow from having to [make] all those starts as a rookie and the different experiences last year. ... He has demonstrated everything that we're looking for to protect that side."

 But Coleman also said he needed to become more of a pro in his approach. He was benched after two games at guard last season in part because of his durability, former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury said at the time. He missed a month of training camp while learning to play guard then, after two games, he showed up in practice three days later in a black jersey signifying no-contact. He did not start at guard again.

 Coleman missed time in his rookie training camp because of a shoulder injury. From Weeks 9 to 17 as a rookie, he played every snap but missed 18 in the regular-season finale.

 

 "There's injuries that I've had in the past during training camp," Coleman said, "that fully could have been prevented if I would've just sacrificed a little more time in rehab and working on certain things."

 To help, Coleman said he has taken more care to use preventative maintenance on his body -- from how he stretches to how he eats, to his daily recovery sessions after workouts. He hired a nutritionist. He worked out with Dominic Studzinski, a former Ole Miss strength and conditioning coach who has trained Tunsil for more than a decade. "Just taking care of myself a lot better," Coleman said. "There are priorities I didn't do the first couple years that I just have to reflect on and kind of be accountable on. I changed that last year, but then even more this year."

 That included spending several weeks training with Tunsil in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, this summer.

 "I dragged my wife out there to the middle of nowhere," Coleman said. "What she understood is just really seeing how one of the greatest tackles ever does it. How do I need to live to give myself a chance to be like that guy?"

 That will be difficult. The Commanders did not attempt to sugarcoat Tunsil's loss. Quinn pointed to his leadership -- he has mentored right tackle Josh Conerly Jr ., who also worked out with him this summer. He also pointed to his skill, as a pass protector in particular.

 "Game on the line you run behind a player like that," Quinn said. "Running game and pass protection, you don't [need] a lot of help."

 But Washington did go 10-5 in his rookie year when he started, including 2-1 in the postseason. The Commanders still opted to trade for a premier talent in Tunsil after that season and moved Coleman to guard, where he was competing with Chris Paul this summer to start. Paul will be the starting left guard now.

 "He was off to a very good start at left guard," Quinn said. "To switch him outside, when you go through things you want to come out the other side stronger, harder, learn the lessons. Brandon and a couple guys are in that space, just maybe the resilience you have to show. Going through it sucks, but there is a [new] guy on the other side."
